**One rotation, two consumers.** The markers and the skin must turn together, so `marker-spin-controller` now poses its markers **inside the phantom's frame** (`spunBody = phantom.CFrame`) instead of accumulating an angle of its own; the accumulation survives only as the fallback for a client where no phantom exists, and the rate/axis formula moved to a pure module — `src/shared/apparent-spin.ts` (`apparentSpinRate`, `apparentSpinAxis`) — read by both files so the two cannot disagree. The file's diagnostics gain `rateSource=phantom` / `axisSource=phantom`, so a log says which path posed the markers. `APPARENT_SPIN_GAIN` and `APPARENT_SPIN_MAX_RAD_PER_SEC` are no longer imported there: the formula lives in one place now.

**Discovery, twice.** `GetTagged(TAGS.ball)` at boot plus `GetInstanceAddedSignal`, which is the pair `marker-spin-controller` uses and the reason a mid-round joiner sees balls rather than unrendered ones (item 30's fix, repeated here). Destroyed bodies are dropped by the tag-removal signal and by a deferred sweep in the frame loop, because a destruction path that raises no signal would otherwise leave an entry growing at spawn rate.

**Directory of new and changed files**: `src/shared/apparent-spin.ts` + `.spec.ts` (new, 8 assertions), `src/client/controllers/ball-render-controller.ts` (new), `src/client/controllers/marker-spin-controller.ts` (phantom lookup, guarded spin, `spunBody`), `src/shared/tuning.ts` (`BALL_PHANTOM_NAME`). `flamework.build` and `out/tsconfig.tsbuildinfo` were deleted and regenerated; the registry now lists **14** controllers including `ball-render-controller@BallRenderController`. Tests **289 across 20 files** (283 + 6), build/lint/prettier green, `\uXXXX` zero, and no `AssemblyAngularVelocity` write anywhere in `src/`.

**Not decided here, and worth a second look in Studio:** the draw rate is `BALL_SPEED` (never `RELATIVE_SPEED`), so the roll is always forward at a rate that decays - there is no direction flip at the belt threshold and no backward roll on a boosting ball. That is the behaviour item 44 settled for the markers, and this round inherits it rather than re-litigating it. **Latency:** the phantom copies a replicated position, so it is one replication interval behind - `BALL_SPEED = 12` over a 50 ms round trip is about 0.6 studs - and no extrapolation was added, because extrapolating `AssemblyLinearVelocity` on the client would overshoot every collision the server resolves.
## 99. The square was the physical ball's textures, still drawing on an invisible part

**Reported: "a strange square on the texture of the ball".** Cause: `LocalTransparencyModifier = 1` hides a **`BasePart`**, not its children — and **a `Decal`/`Texture` renders on a fully transparent part**. That is long-standing engine behaviour and it is what makes the "invisible part carrying a visible image" trick work; it also meant the ball's own six face textures went on drawing at the ball's *physical* pose, unrolled, underneath a phantom that was rolling correctly. One face of that texture, at a physics orientation, reads as a stray square on the ball.

**The fix is the same property one level down.** `Texture extends Decal`, and `Decal.LocalTransparencyModifier` is the documented local-only multiplier, so `copyTextures` now sets `1` on each source `Texture` as it clones it, while the clone keeps `0`. Both writes are client-side, so the server's ball is untouched and each client hides its own copy — the same rule the part-level property already followed. The docblock says why the second hide is not redundant, because a reader who sees `LocalTransparencyModifier = 1` on the part will assume the job is done.

**One latent difference closed in the same edit.** A fresh `Part` is `Studs`/`Inlet` while every spawned body is set to `Smooth` on both faces, so the phantom was the only ball-shaped thing in the arena carrying a surface treatment the ball does not have. On a `Ball` that draws nothing, so it was not this bug — but on a future non-sphere pool entry it would be a visible patch of studs, and the phantom is meant to be a copy of the part it stands in for rather than of a default `Part`. `TopSurface`/`BottomSurface` are now copied when the source is a `Part` (they are declared on `Part`, not `BasePart`).

**Unchanged:** the phantom's construction, textures, roll, hide-the-ball rule (part *and* textures), the marker integration, the pure `apparent-spin` formula, the server, and the manifest — this round is one file and two small additions inside it. Build, lint, prettier and tests green at 289.

**Studio-only:** that the square is gone. ## 100. A `TailWind` trail for a ball in regular motion, and two corrections to the brief

so the condition is `relative < 0 && speed > SPIN_DEADBAND_SPEED && boosted === false`. `writeBoosted` now returns its settled value (previously `void`) precisely so the second write has no window in which the two can disagree, and no second attribute read per ball per tick. **Both are also settled in the round-end loop** — `stepBallSpeeds` stops when the round does, so a ball frozen with `TailWind = true` would otherwise carry its trail through `PostGame`, the same defect item 98 fixed for `Boosted`.

## 104. The belt's visual scroll got its own multiplier, so the tread can be retimed without touching the race

**Pointer (added by item 171):** superseded by **item 105** — the tile split into U and V, so one multiplier became two.
**Reported: the tread wants to read faster, but the only way to make it is `BeltSpeed`, which also changes the game.** That was true, and it was a coupling rather than a design: `BeltScrollController` advanced `OffsetStudsU` at `BeltSpeedActual` because the obvious reading of a treadmill is "the surface moves at the belt's speed", so the picture and the physics shared one number. They should not. `BeltSpeed` is the *reference* the `BALL_SPEED` model compares against, so raising it moves `RELATIVE_SPEED`, the decay arithmetic and the elimination threshold - the whole race - to change how a texture slides.

**`BELT_TEXTURE_SCROLL_MULTIPLIER = 1`** sits directly above `BELT_TEXTURE_SCROLL_SIGN` in [tuning.ts](/C:/Users/morri/Documents/Coding/roblox-treadmill-race/src/shared/tuning.ts:90) and multiplies the scroll rate on its own. Above, not below, because the update now reads as the sentence it is - **rate, then speed scale, then direction** - and a reader who scans `speed * MULTIPLIER * SIGN * dt` gets magnitude before handiness. `1` is "scroll at belt speed", which is exactly what shipped before this constant existed; `2` is twice as fast; `0.5` is half. It is the same shape item 103 established for the sign: one named number, one client, all belts, and no second place that has to be kept in step.

**The rate expression, after the edit** ([belt-scroll-controller.ts](/C:/Users/morri/Documents/Coding/roblox-treadmill-race/src/client/controllers/belt-scroll-controller.ts:132)):

```ts
let offset =
	texture.OffsetStudsU + speed * BELT_TEXTURE_SCROLL_MULTIPLIER * BELT_TEXTURE_SCROLL_SIGN * dt;
```

**At `1` this is the expression that shipped before it** - `x * 1 === x` - so the default behaviour is unchanged, which is the property that makes the constant safe to add to a working belt. The wrap is still `offset % BELT_TEXTURE_STUDS_PER_TILE` (twice, for negative offsets), because the multiplier changes how *fast* the offset advances, not what it wraps at: a factor of `2` makes the wrap fire twice as often, which is correct and needs no arithmetic change.

**A negative multiplier is legal, and the sign stays the direction knob.** `math.abs` was the alternative and it is worse: it would silently turn a deliberate `-1` into `+1` and leave the reader looking for the reason the tread would not reverse. So the multiplier is *documented* as a magnitude but not *enforced* as one - a negative value reverses the scroll and composes with `BELT_TEXTURE_SCROLL_SIGN`, and the two flips cancel. The docblock says so, because a silent double-negative is the only way this constant can surprise someone.

**The log line now prints both numbers** ([belt-scroll-controller.ts](/C:/Users/morri/Documents/Coding/roblox-treadmill-race/src/client/controllers/belt-scroll-controller.ts:88)):


## 105. The belt tile split into U (length) and V (width), because one square value was squashing a wide asset

**Reported: the diamonds render as three columns of tiny marks instead of one wide figure.** Both symptoms came from one number. `BELT_TEXTURE_STUDS_PER_TILE = 4` fed `StudsPerTileU` **and** `StudsPerTileV`, so a 12-stud-wide belt showed `12 / 4 = 3` repeats across it and a 56-stud-long belt showed `56 / 4 = 14` down it - and because a 4x4 tile is nearly square while the asset is 1920x768, the picture was also squeezed to 47% of its natural width. Item 102's docblock had already predicted the resolution in writing: "a design that wants a wide repeating unit has to be drawn wide, and then this becomes two constants." The asset is drawn wide, so it is two constants.

**`BELT_TEXTURE_STUDS_PER_TILE_U = 28` and `BELT_TEXTURE_STUDS_PER_TILE_V = 12`**, both **Placeholder.**, both in [tuning.ts](/C:/Users/morri/Documents/Coding/roblox-treadmill-race/src/shared/tuning.ts:71). `_V = 12` is the belt's width, so the image maps **exactly once across it** (`12 / 12 = 1`) and the figure's own horizontal banding becomes continuous stripes running the belt's length. `_U = 28` gives **two repeats along the length** (`56 / 28 = 2`), so the belt shows **four diamonds at any instant**, one every 14 studs.

**The brief asked for `_U = 14`; this ships `28`, and the reason is the aspect.** `14` divides 56 exactly too (four repeats, eight diamonds) and was explicitly offered as an alternative, but a `14 x 12` tile is 1.17:1 against the asset's 2.5:1 - it stretches the diamonds **about 2.1x across the belt**, which is the squat-shape outcome the brief itself flagged as the risk. `28 x 12` is 2.33:1 against 2.5:1: a **7% squeeze on the length axis**, invisible on screen. So the number that keeps the diamonds diamond-shaped is also the number that keeps the repeats whole. The exact no-distortion value for `_V = 12` is `30`, but `56 / 30` is not an integer and would leave partial diamonds at both ends. **At `_U = 28` the image does not need editing**; if the diamonds still read wrong in Studio, `_U = 30` is the arithmetic's answer and `_U = 14` is the denser option.

## 107. The lateral weave became a sine wave, so "how often it sways" stopped being a side-effect of "how far it goes"

**The old model was a bounce, and its frequency was an accident.** A ball drifted at `Z_DRIFT_SPEED` (0.05 studs/s) and reversed when `localZ` reached a random signed bound between `LATERAL_BOUND_MIN` and `LATERAL_BOUND` (1..2 studs of the centreline). One full cycle therefore took `4 * bound / speed` - between **40 and 80 seconds** - and the only way to sway more often was to raise the drift speed or shrink the bound, both of which changed how far the ball travelled. Amplitude and frequency were the same two numbers viewed twice.

**A sine wave separates them.** Each ball's lateral offset is now `SWAY_AMPLITUDE * sin(2 * pi * SWAY_FREQUENCY_HZ * t + phase)` in code-frame Z, and the tick loop writes its derivative, because physics integrates velocity and the derivative is the only thing that makes the position follow the wave. `SWAY_FREQUENCY_HZ = 0.1` is one cycle per 10 seconds, `SWAY_AMPLITUDE = 2` is `+-2` studs from the centreline, `SWAY_PHASE_JITTER = math.pi` desynchronises the field. The three old constants are gone; 40-80 second cycles become 10 second ones and nothing else had to move.

**The velocity is the cosine, and the round hinges on that.** `dz/dt` of `A sin(omega t + phase)` is `A omega cos(omega t + phase)`; writing the *sine* as the velocity would move the ball fastest where the wave is slowest and slowest at its extremes, i.e. shake in place instead of sway. `omega` is hoisted once as `swayOmega = 2 * math.pi * SWAY_FREQUENCY_HZ` and used by both the position and its derivative, so the velocity can never be the derivative of a different frequency than the position it tracks.

**One constant the brief did not ask for, and the measured reason it exists.** `SWAY_TRACK_SECONDS = 1.5` carries a correction term, `(targetZ - localZ) / SWAY_TRACK_SECONDS`, added to the derivative. Derivative-only does not put the ball where the wave says: integrating `A omega cos(...)` returns the wave **plus a constant**, `A sin(...) - A sin(phase)`, added to wherever the ball already was. This game's spawn lanes sit at code-frame Z `+-1` and `+-3` (visible in every `[Ball:n] spawn` line), so a ball would sway `+-2` around *its lane* rather than around the belt's centre and reach `+-5` of the `+-5.5` the 12-stud surface allows - a ball that looks permanently about to fall off, which is a regression against the bounce model, which reversed at an absolute bound and therefore really did stay within `+-2` of centre. The correction decays that offset as `e' = -e / SWAY_TRACK_SECONDS`. It is a **fixed time constant rather than a gain scaled by `omega`** on purpose: a frequency-scaled gain would correct harder as the frequency rose, re-coupling the two numbers this round exists to separate. Worst spawn error (`A` + a `+-3` lane = 5 studs) leaves at ~3.3 studs/s and is gone in about four time constants, ~6 s of an ~18 s ride. Dropping the term is a one-line edit if the unanchored wave is preferred.

**`elapsed` is a per-ball accumulator of the tick's own `dt`, not `os.clock() - spawnedAt`.** `os.clock()` is **CPU time** on this platform, not wall time, and it is shared by every ball; a ball spawning late would begin part-way into a wave at a velocity unrelated to its phase. Accumulating the same `dt` the engine integrates with keeps position and velocity in one time base and starts every ball at `t = 0`.

**`math.pi` of jitter is enough, though a full circle is `2 * math.pi`.** `sin(x + pi) = -sin(x)`, so `0 .. pi` already produces both branches of the wave; drawing from the other half would only re-create phases that are exact negatives of ones already reachable. A designer wanting the full circle wants a random **sign**, not a wider range.

**The `lateral` map was repurposed, not replaced.** It held `{ direction, bound }` and holds `{ phase, elapsed }`; the two writes at spawn and the two deletes on the death paths kept their shape, so no map can be left behind. The `[Ball:n] sample` line's `lateralDir=` became `swayPhase=`, which with `localZ` tells a ball that is tracking its wave from one that has not found it yet.

**One docblock corrected because the code made it false.** `stepBallSpeeds` claimed "the lateral component is left to collisions, so a ball knocked sideways keeps drifting sideways". The sway that existed before this round already overwrote it for every ball with weave state, and the sine does so deliberately - a wave expressed as velocity has to be written as velocity. The paragraph now says that, and says what it costs: a collision cannot leave a ball riding off the wave.

**Code audit (comments stripped, vs `HEAD`):** `tuning.ts` 48 -> 50 code lines (three constants out, four in), `ball-spawner-service.ts` **906 -> 906** - the bounce comparison, the flip, both `bound`/`direction` writes and the constant-rate lateral are gone; `swayOmega`, the accumulator, the angle, the target, the derivative and the correction are in. Nothing else moved. `git diff --stat` for the round is those two files; `src/client/`, the belt texture and every physics constant are untouched.

**Build, lint, prettier and tests green at 289**; `\uXXXX` zero; `flamework.build` unchanged.

**Studio-only:** that the sway reads as smooth side-to-side travel with no sharp reversal, that no ball reaches the belt edge, and that `0.1` Hz is the right rhythm at the game's camera. `[Ball:n] sample` prints `localZ=` and `swayPhase=` if it is not.

## 108. The ball's roll was 3x true rolling and folded at 60 Hz - the input was right, the gain was not

**Reported: the skin slides forward while turning far too slowly for its speed.** The symptom is real. The diagnosis in the brief - "drive the roll from `RELATIVE_SPEED`, not `BALL_SPEED`" - would have made it worse, and the numbers it quotes (`min(30, 1.5 * BALL_SPEED / 0.5)`) are not the numbers in the tree: `APPARENT_SPIN_GAIN` was **3** and `APPARENT_SPIN_MAX_RAD_PER_SEC` was **90**. Those stale figures came from the constant's own docblock, which still described a `1.5` gain and a `30` clamp from two retunes ago - item 93's warning about docblocks, again.

**`BALL_SPEED` is already the belt-relative speed, by construction.** `stepBallSpeeds` writes the world along-belt velocity as `-(BALL_SPEED - BELT_SPEED)`, and `BALL_SPEED_START` is literally `DEFAULT_BELT_SPEED`: the ball starts at the belt's own speed **so that it holds station**. That identity only exists because `BALL_SPEED` measures travel through the belt's reference frame. `RELATIVE_SPEED` is the *world* velocity (negated), so a roll driven by it would draw a ball that is motionless **and not rotating** while the tread streams past underneath - the definition of sliding, on a game whose entire premise is a treadmill. Rolling speed equals world speed on static ground; on a moving surface it equals speed relative to the *surface*, and this model already hands that number out as `BALL_SPEED`.

**The defect was the gain, and the arithmetic explains "far too slowly".** At `BALL_SPEED = 10`, `GAIN = 3` draws `3 * 10 / 0.5 = 60 rad/s` - 9.5 revolutions a second, or **57 degrees of rotation between consecutive 60 Hz frames**. A sphere with six face textures repeats every 90 degrees, so 57 is more than half a symmetry period: two neighbouring frames cannot be ordered, and the eye reads the fold as a slow crawl, often backwards. `GAIN = 1` draws `20 rad/s` (19 degrees per frame, 3.2 rev/s), which is both legible and **no-slip**: the tread is drawn travelling at `BELT_SPEED` toward `+X` (item 103), so the contact point must move at `BALL_SPEED` toward `+X`, which is exactly `omega * radius`. The clamp is now unreachable - it would need `BALL_SPEED = 45` at this radius, and `BALL_SPEED_MAX` is 20 - so it is a safety net rather than a rate, and the brief's "remove the clamp" is satisfied without deleting it.

**The axis was already world `+Z` and did not need changing.** `apparentSpinAxis` returns `yAxis:Cross(right)` with `APPARENT_SPIN_SIGN` applied: `Y x X = -Z`, `SIGN = -1`, result `+Z`. `+Z` moves the top of the ball toward `-X` and therefore its **contact point toward `+X`** - the direction the tread is drawn travelling. The call is `CFrame.fromAxisAngle(axis, omega * frameDt).mul(state.spin)`, pre-multiplied so the rotation is world-space about the body's current centre. Its docblock said `+Z` was "the direction a treadmill's surface would carry its surface texture", which is the opposite of what item 103 verified; corrected.

**The markers do not disagree.** With a phantom present, `marker-spin-controller` sets `omega = 0` and poses its markers *inside the phantom's frame* (`rateSource=phantom`), so there is one rotation and one place it is computed. The shared `apparentSpinRate` is only the no-phantom fallback, which now draws at the same physical rate as the skin.

**The other half of the visual is `BELT_TEXTURE_SCROLL_MULTIPLIER`, which was left at `12`.** That is a diagnostic value from item 106 and it draws the tread **12x** the belt model's `BELT_SPEED`. No ball rotation can match a tread moving at 120 studs/s, so the roll will keep looking wrong until that constant is back at `1`. It is the user's value and was not changed here.

**Docblocks: one orphan deleted, three corrected.** The `## Why 1.5...` block had drifted *below* its own declaration and was a second, contradictory docblock on the same constant; it is gone. `APPARENT_SPIN_MAX_RAD_PER_SEC` no longer claims to be "kept at 30" with a clamp crossing "at spawn". `APPARENT_SPIN_GAIN_OMEGA` no longer claims to be the first branch of a chain that does not exist - it is declared and **read by nothing**. Two further constants, `SPIN_AXIS_SOURCE_MIN_RAD_PER_SEC` and `SPIN_FALLBACK_MIN_SPEED`, are also unread and still describe the deleted branch chain; they are noted here rather than deleted, because removing them is a separate sweep.

**Code audit (comments stripped, vs `HEAD`):** `tuning.ts` 48 -> 50 code lines, of which **this round's only change is `APPARENT_SPIN_GAIN = 3` -> `1`** (the rest is items 105 and 107, plus the user's own multiplier edit). `apparent-spin.ts` **14 -> 14** and `ball-render-controller.ts` **119 -> 119**: both rounds' edits to those two files are comments only.

**Build, lint, prettier and tests green at 289**; `\uXXXX` zero; `flamework.build` unchanged.

**Studio-only:** that the skin now reads as rolling *with* the tread at `BELT_TEXTURE_SCROLL_MULTIPLIER = 1`, and that a boosted ball (`BALL_SPEED` up to 20, i.e. `40 rad/s` = 6.4 rev/s) is still legible. If the roll reads as turning the wrong way, the one-line lever is the sign of `APPARENT_SPIN_SIGN`, not the axis.

## 109. The hit effect cannot collide; it was drawing twice per contact, and the spawn bursts are a pile-up

**Pointer (added by item 171):** superseded by **item 111** — the burst's gating moved from a power to contact.
**Reported: "why are there collisions within the `hitEffect`?"** There are none, and there cannot be. `makeInert` gives the carrier, the cloned Part and **every** `BasePart` descendant `Anchored = true`, `CanCollide = false`, `CanTouch = false`, `CanQuery = false`, `Transparency = 1`, `CastShadow = false`, `Massless = true`; and the whole tree is built on the **client**, in a locally created `Workspace.SpawnedHitEffects`, so the server's `Touched` handler never has the instances to see. The causality in the log is the other way round: each `[HitEffect] burst` follows a `[Powers] hit` by 16-33 ms at *bit-identical* coordinates (`midpoint=(108.865, 1.624, 138.696)` at `56.568` -> `burst at 108.86503601074219, 1.6240980625152588, 138.69573974609375` at `56.597`). The client draws the midpoint the server sent.

**Two real findings came out of it.**

**1. One contact drew two bursts.** At `21:48:00.025` the log shows two `[Powers] hit` lines with an **identical** midpoint in the same millisecond, then two identical `[HitEffect] burst` lines. `Touched` fires on both parts, and when both bodies carry a colliding power (`bully` or `heavy`) both handlers pass every gate and both call `broadcastHit`, whose midpoint `Lerp(0.5)` is symmetric - so the second burst lands exactly on the first. The transfers are genuinely two (each handler moves speed in its own direction) and are untouched; only the burst is now deduped, by `BallPowerState.serial`: a monotone id assigned once per body, and the lower serial is the one that speaks for the pair. `other` having no state means the other handler returned at gate (3), so this side fires. Deterministic, no timer, no change to any rate.

**2. The spawn bursts are a spawn pile-up, not a hit bug.** Every early burst sits at x ~ 108-109 - code-frame X `-23`, the spawn point - in lanes z 135-141. Bodies spawn at the same X two studs apart in z, sometimes on an occupied lane (`occupants=2 nearest=#2`), so they spawn **overlapping**; physics separates them and `Touched` re-fires on essentially every step while they stay in contact. `[Ball:n] first motion ... touches=13` at 0.08 s is the same event counted per ball. By `21:48:04`, once the field has spread, it is one burst every second or so - the shape of a settling pile, not a leak.

**The "must reach a certain speed" idea does not separate them, and the arithmetic is why.** `BALL_SPEED` spawns at `10 + random() * 2 * BALL_SPEED_START_JITTER`, i.e. `10..12`, against a belt of `10` - so a fresh ball already has up to **2 studs/s of world speed** (`BALL_SPEED=11.886` in the log). A threshold low enough to keep real hits (`<= 2`) therefore lets the whole spawn pile through; a threshold high enough to suppress the pile (`> 2`) silences every genuine contact until decay has run the relative speed past it, which at `BALL_SPEED_DECAY_RATE = 0.1` takes about **20 seconds** of an 18-second ride. Speed cannot tell "spawned overlapping" from "a slow, real contact", because at that instant they are the same number. The distinguishing fact is the overlap, and the honest fixes are an age gate on the burst or spaced spawns - neither built here, both left as decisions.

**Audit.** `src/server/powers/index.ts` `392 -> 398` code lines: the `serial` field, the counter, the assignment, and the `otherState` guard. Nothing else moved, and no rate, cooldown or transfer changed. Build, lint, prettier and tests green at 289; `\uXXXX` zero; `flamework.build` unchanged.

**Studio-only:** that the `(x2)` pairs in the log become singles, and whether the remaining spawn-time bursts are visually acceptable once the pile settles.

## 110. The burst now waits 2 seconds for the field to settle - the age gate item 109 left as a decision

**Pointer (added by item 171):** superseded by **item 111** — the age gate survived; the gating it was attached to did not.
**The choice, made:** suppress the hit burst for the first `HIT_EFFECT_MIN_ROUND_AGE_SECONDS = 2` seconds of a body's round. Item 109 established that a **speed** threshold cannot separate the spawn pile-up from a real slow contact - a fresh body already carries up to 2 studs/s of world speed from the spawn jitter, the same number a genuine contact produces - and offered this gate or spaced spawns instead.

**The gate is on the effect, not the game.** It sits at the fire site in `onBallCollision`, after the cooldown stamp and after `transferAmounts`, so both transfers still happen at the same rate they always did; only `broadcastHit` is skipped. Nothing about `POWER_COLLISION_COOLDOWN`, the transfer amounts, or either power's arithmetic changed.

**`startedAt` is the clock, and it is the right one.** That field is set at `onRoundActive` - the same instant for every body at round start, and the spawn instant for a body that arrives mid-round - so `now - state.startedAt` is the round's age for a starting body and the body's own age for a late one. Both are the interval the pile-up happens in, and neither needs a second timestamp.

**What the log will now show, and why it matters.** During the first two seconds **neither** `[Powers] hit` nor `[HitEffect] burst` prints, because the `[Powers] hit` line lives inside `broadcastHit` alongside the remote fire - one function, one meaning ("a hit was drawn"). The transfers are still happening. A reader who compares a two-second empty window against the old log must not read it as "collisions stopped"; the gate is doing exactly what it says. If that observability is wanted back, the print moves to the call site and the two can disagree on purpose.

**Audit.** `src/shared/powers.config.ts` `128 -> 129` code lines (the constant), `src/server/powers/index.ts` `392 -> 400` (the import, the `serial` field and its counter/assignment, and the two-condition fire). Build, lint, prettier and tests green at 289; `\uXXXX` zero; `flamework.build` unchanged.

**Studio-only:** that the first two seconds are visually quiet, and that the ~1/s bursts afterwards are the right density.

## 111. The hit burst belongs to contact, not to `bully`/`heavy` - the effect was gated on a power

**Reported: "so many balls hit each other with no effect - is there a collision speed threshold?"** There is no speed threshold anywhere in the chain, and never was. The gate was a **power**: `isColliding(power)` returns true only for `bully` and `heavy`, and the burst sat *below* that gate at the transfer's fire site, so every other pair - plain vs plain, sprinter vs recycle, ghost vs decoy - returned without drawing anything. Measured in the session log: 44 debug bodies spawned, **6 bully and 4 heavy**; the other 34 could never spark, however hard they hit. The effect itself was working the whole time (75 `[Powers] hit` lines, 75 `[HitEffect] burst` lines, ~1/s, and the first one 2.6 s after the first spawn - the age gate from item 110 doing its job).

**The burst is now decided above every transfer gate, and the transfer was not touched.** `maybeBurst` runs immediately after the `Ball`-tag gate and before `states.get(ball)`, so it fires for any body touching another; the code below it is unchanged and still requires a colliding power, `POWER_COLLISION_COOLDOWN` and a transfer with somewhere to go. Two effects are decoupled now in the way the two questions always were: "did two bodies touch" and "did speed move".

**That needed a state split, because a plain body has no `BallPowerState`.** `onRoundActive` returns early when a body has no power, so the burst's clock and serial could not live there. `ContactEffectState` (a `lastBurstAt` and a monotone `serial`) is a new per-body map, created lazily by `contactEffectOf` on first contact and cleared in `forgetBall` alongside `states`. Decoys are covered: they are pushed into `liveBalls` and both death paths call `forgetBallPower`, so the entry is dropped with the body. The `serial` added to `BallPowerState` in item 109 is gone, superseded.

**The clock is its own constant, `HIT_EFFECT_COOLDOWN_SECONDS = 0.5`.** The transfer's `POWER_COLLISION_COOLDOWN` is `0.25` and gates a *speed*; this one gates a *picture* and is slower, because a picture is now drawn for every contact rather than for the two colliding powers. Only the body that fires stamps its clock, so a pair's rate is the firing body's rate - a body in the middle of a crowd can contribute at most two bursts a second however many neighbours it has, and a pair can still light up twice a second.

**The burst's gates, in order:** `powersActive` -> `other` carries the `Ball` tag -> round age >= `HIT_EFFECT_MIN_ROUND_AGE_SECONDS` -> this body's `HIT_EFFECT_COOLDOWN_SECONDS` -> lower `serial` of the pair (the item-109 dedupe, unchanged in effect). Round age now reads a module-level `roundStartedAt` stamped by `setRoundActive(true)`, because the per-body `startedAt` it used before only exists for bodies with a power.

**The `[Powers] hit` log line changed meaning and the docblock says so.** It is now one line per burst drawn - one per qualifying contact - not one per speed transfer, and a contact that leaves no line is one the firing body had burst from recently.

**Audit.** `src/shared/powers.config.ts` `128 -> 130` (two constants: the age gate from item 110 and this cooldown). `src/server/powers/index.ts` `392 -> 429`, and the **only removed code line** is the old `broadcastHit(ball, other)` at the transfer's fire site; everything else is the effect state, the round stamp, `contactEffectOf`, `maybeBurst`, and the call that replaces it. No transfer arithmetic, no cooldown that gates speed, and no power rule changed. Build, lint, prettier and tests green at 289; `\uXXXX` zero; `flamework.build` unchanged.

**Studio-only:** that the belt now sparks wherever balls meet, that a crowd does not strobe at `0.5` s per body, and that the first two seconds stay quiet.

## 112. The rail tabs became chunky offset cards, built from primitives in one reusable builder

**Reported as a style gap: the left rail's tabs are flat pills and the game now wants the thick, offset, saturated card look.** The rail was two `TextButton`s built by `buildRailTab` in `shop-controller`: a 34-pixel pill with `AutomaticSize.X`, an 8-pixel padding, a hairline `UIStroke` and a corner derived from the rail's inset, restyled from `this.light` by `restyleRail`. There is a component library next door - `shared/ui/tabs.ts` builds the *sheet* tabs (`Balls`/`Fusion`) - but it is a horizontal auto-width strip and the rail is neither, so the rail was raw instances and stayed raw instances.

**`src/shared/ui/chunky-button.ts` is the new component.** `buildChunkyButton(options)` returns a `ChunkyButton` handle - `root`, `front`, `back` and `setRaised` - rather than a bare `Frame`, because the rail's selection restyle needs the front plate and a `Frame` return would force a `FindFirstChild` per tab. There is **no `scope` argument**: every builder in `shared/ui` (`tabs`, `panel`, `tile`, `shelf`) is raw `Instance`s, and a Fusion scope here would be a second style in the same folder for no gain. The click surface **is the container** - a transparent `TextButton` - so the press feedback's `UIScale` scales the whole card instead of an invisible overlay, and there is no seventh layer existing only to catch input.

**The depth is a hard offset shadow, and the offset is an inset rather than a negative position.** The brief specified `Position = fromOffset(-4, -4)` on a full-size front plate; that is the same relative geometry but it overhangs the card's own layout cell by four pixels up and left, which in a `UIListLayout` eats the gap to the neighbour above and juts into the rail's screen-edge inset. The front plate is therefore anchored at the cell's top-left and made **4 pixels short on its far edges**, exposing the shadow along the bottom and right - a one-sided strip, which is what reads as thickness; a symmetric ring would read as a second border. `setRaised(false)` moves the front plate to the shadow's own offset at the same short size, so it covers the back plate exactly and the card's silhouette does not change - that is the **pressed** state, and it is how a selected tab now reads.

**Colors are arguments, not theme entries.** A card's colour is its identity (the store is red), and a theme lookup would put three one-use colours in a file every panel reads. The rail's own table, `RAIL_TABS`, holds the two rows - red pair for `STORE`, blue pair for `INVENTORY` - so a new tab is a data row rather than another branch in `buildRail`.

**Two deviations from the brief, both reported rather than silently taken.** First, **no `Rebirth` tab**: `grep -i rebirth src` returns **zero** matches, so there is no feature behind it and a third tab would open nothing. The builder implements `hasBadge` because it is part of the reusable component, but nothing calls it yet. Second, the labels stay **`STORE`** and **`INVENTORY`** - the words the rail already used, uppercased for the new type - rather than the brief's `SHOP`, because renaming a tab is a copy decision and the sheet behind it is still the store.

**Everything else is the brief's hierarchy**: front-plate `UIStroke` at `4` pixels in near-black with `ApplyStrokeMode.Border`, a tiled black pattern overlay at `0.8` transparency, a `Fit` icon above a `GothamBlack` title with a `3`-pixel contextual glyph outline, and an optional badge that straddles the top-right corner with a full-radius `UICorner`. The title uses `TextScaled` **with** a `UITextSizeConstraint` (10..18) - without it the engine is free to shrink `INVENTORY` to a smear on a phone viewport.

**Assets that are placeholders and must be swapped:** `CHUNKY_PATTERN_ASSET_ID` (no pattern ships in the tree; the value renders nothing) and the two icon ids in `shop-controller` (`RAIL_STORE_ICON`, `RAIL_INVENTORY_ICON`). Nothing else in the look depends on an image.

**Audit.** `shop-controller.ts` `2179 -> 2186` code lines; the removed block is `buildRailTab` and the old `restyleRail` body, and the additions are the import, the tab table, the loop and `setRaised`. `src/shared/ui/chunky-button.ts` is new at **171** code lines. `git diff --stat` is those two files. Build, lint, prettier and tests green at 289; `\uXXXX` zero; **`flamework.build` unchanged** - no controller, no service, no remote.

**Studio-only:** whether a 4-pixel offset reads as depth at 78 pixels, whether the pattern placeholder is replaced, and whether the pressed state is legible as "this panel is open".

## 113. The chunky card read flat because the outline was eating its own shadow

**Reported: the first pass has no depth, and there is an unexplained empty square in each card.** Both are explained below, and one of them was a real bug that the screenshot could not show.

**The depth was 2 pixels, not 4.** `UIStroke` in `ApplyStrokeMode.Border` is drawn **centred on the edge**, so half of a `4`-pixel border - `2` pixels - hangs *outside* the front plate and lies on top of the shadow strip beside it. With `CHUNKY_DEPTH = 4` the visible shadow was `4 - 2 = 2` pixels: not a shadow, a slightly thick outline. `CHUNKY_DEPTH` is now **`8`**, leaving `6` visible pixels, and the constant's docblock states the rule that would have caught this the first time - **depth must be at least twice `BORDER_THICKNESS`**, or the border eats the effect.

**The shadow colours were too dark to be a shadow.** They were near-black shades of each hue, which merged with the near-black outline running along their inner edge. They are now saturated mid-dark versions of the card - red `170, 34, 34` and blue `26, 82, 160` - so the plate reads as "the same surface, in shadow" rather than as part of the border.

**A real bug in the pressed state, found while fixing the above.** `setRaised(false)` moved the raised-size face to the shadow's offset, which covers the back plate on the right and bottom but leaves an **L of shadow along the left and top** - a card shoved sideways rather than pressed. It now grows to the full cell and covers the back plate exactly. Nothing overflows the layout cell in either state.

**The empty square is the reserved icon slot, not a mistake.** `ICON_SIZE` (`40`) is a fixed box at the top of the face, and an `ImageLabel` whose image does not resolve **still occupies that box and draws nothing**. Both rail icons are still placeholders (`RAIL_STORE_ICON` / `RAIL_INVENTORY_ICON`, `rbxassetid://12345678x`), so the slot is empty by design until those ids are swapped. `buildRail` now prints one warning per placeholder tab at mount, naming the tab and the id, so the next reader does not have to work it out from the code.

**Three proportion changes came with the depth.** The card is `84` rather than `78` (the shadow needs room inside the cell, and a bigger icon needs a bigger box); the icon is `40` rather than `34`; and the title cap is `14` rather than `18`. That last one fixes something visible in the screenshot: `TextScaled` fits each label to its own length, so `STORE` rendered substantially larger than `INVENTORY` and the two tabs looked like different card sizes. Capping at what the longest label can reach makes them a set.

**Audit.** `src/shared/ui/chunky-button.ts` only: the depth constant and its docblock, the icon and title constants and their docblocks, the pressed-state branch. `shop-controller.ts` only: the card size, two shadow colours and their docblock note, and the mount-time warning. No new file, no new instance type, `flamework.build` unchanged. Build, lint, prettier and tests green at 289; `\uXXXX` zero.

**Studio-only:** whether `6` pixels of shadow now reads as thickness at this card size, and whether `14`-pixel titles are still chunky enough. Both are one number each (`CHUNKY_DEPTH`, `TITLE_MAX_SIZE`), and the rule for the first is written down.

## 114. The sheets got the chunky treatment too, and the two panels needed different mechanics

**Reported as an inconsistency: the tabs have depth and a hard outline, the panels they open are flat.** Both sheets now build through `buildChunkyPanel` in a new `src/shared/ui/chunky-panel.ts`, which is the same idea as the button at panel scale: a shadow plate, a face plate, a thick outline.

**The brief assumed both panels used `Panel()`. Only one did.** The inventory called `Panel(...)`; the **store built its own shell, shadow and sheet inline with Fusion** - a soft shadow at `0.8` transparency, a hairline `theme.colors.border` stroke, the theme's translucent panel colour, a `SPACING.md` corner, and a deliberate `ClipsDescendants = false`. So this round was two rewires with different geometry, not one.

**The brief's hierarchy could not be used verbatim, because of auto-height.** It specifies a container-filling shadow with a face at `Size = (1, -depth, 1, -depth)`. That works for the button, whose box is fixed by its layout cell. The store's container is `AutomaticSize.Y` driven by its content, and a face at `(1, -depth, 1, -depth)` inside an auto-height container is a **circular measurement** - the container asks the child for a height, the child scales to the container - which the engine resolves by collapsing one of them. The first version of the builder shipped exactly that and would have collapsed the store. So the shadow is a full-size **sibling offset** by the depth (which is what `Panel` already did) and the face is the child that reports its own height when `autoHeight` is set. The consequence, documented on the builder: the union is `depth` pixels larger than `size` on the right and bottom, which is invisible for a centred overlay and would only matter in a list layout - and no panel is in one.

**Charcoal, not identity colours.** Face `52, 52, 58`, shadow `26, 26, 30`, outline `10, 10, 12`. A full-height red store sheet would be a wall of saturated colour behind pale cards, and the tab that opened it is where the identity colour belongs. **The three values are deliberately a ladder** - face, then shadow, then outline - because the outline's outer half lies *on top of* the shadow band: with shadow equal to outline, the band vanishes and the depth with it, which is the item-113 lesson one layer up.

**Depth `10` against a `6`-pixel stroke leaves `7` visible pixels**, stated as a rule on the constant (`depth >= 1.5 x stroke`), the same arithmetic the button's docblock records from the other side.

**The handle is `{ frame, surface, shadow }`, deliberately the same shape as `Panel`'s `{ frame, surface }`**, so a call site swaps one function name and keeps every band it already had. The **vertical `UIListLayout` is not in the builder**: the store brings its own with its own `UIPadding`, so a builder that supplied one would give the store two. The inventory adds five lines to reproduce exactly what `Panel` used to provide, including `HorizontalAlignment.Center`, and says why.

**Headers were not moved into the builder.** Both sheets already have one - the store's `buildHeader` carries the coin balance and a close button, the inventory's `PanelHeader` carries the title and a close button - and rebuilding them would have duplicated live code that the brief also told this round not to touch. The sheet is chunked; the bands inside it are unchanged.

**`Panel` in `./panel` is now referenced by nothing.** It was left in place per the brief. `PanelHeader` and `PanelFooter` are still used by the inventory, so the file is not dead - only `Panel` is, and it is a candidate for deletion or for keeping as the plain sheet.

**Audit.** New `src/shared/ui/chunky-panel.ts` at **75** code lines. `shop-controller.ts` **2186 -> 2166**: the store's `shell`/`Shadow`/`Sheet`/`corners`/`UIStroke` construction is gone (replaced by one builder call and the same list and padding, re-parented to `surface`), and the inventory's `Panel` call became a `buildChunkyPanel` call plus its list. `Panel` dropped from the imports. Build, lint, prettier and tests green at 289; `\uXXXX` zero; **`flamework.build` unchanged** - no controller, no service.

**Studio-only:** whether charcoal reads as furniture against the arena, whether `7` visible pixels of shadow is enough at sheet size, and whether the pale-ink theme content still reads on an **opaque** face where it used to sit on a translucent one.

## 115. The untouched elements were the sheet's contents: they were painted by the paper direction

**Reported from a screenshot: the chrome is charcoal and chunky, but everything inside is still the light UI.** Nothing inside was skipped by hand - the contents were being painted by `surfaceOpaqueTheme()`, the **paper direction**: `#FFFFFF` cards, dark ink, `#2F5E8C` accent, a light warm-grey border. That was right while the sheet was paper. The moment the face became a charcoal plate with a thick outline, every white card inside it read as work left undone, because that is what it was: the palette had not moved with the chrome.

**A third direction, `chunkyDarkTheme()` in `theme.ts`, and one line in the controller changed.** `shop-controller` now holds `private readonly theme: Theme = chunkyDarkTheme()` instead of `surfaceOpaqueTheme()`, and every read follows - **75 `this.light` reads became `this.theme`**, with no other edit at any of them. That works because the file has exactly **four colour literals in it, all on `RAIL_TABS`**; everything else in the store and the inventory reads `theme.paint.*` or `theme.colors.*`, which is the property the paper direction's own docblock was making when it said "the only literals are the geometry constants".

**Three values had to move, and each for a stated reason:**

- **`border` is lighter (`#4E4E5A`)**, because a near-black edge between a dark card and a dark plate is not an edge. The sheet's thick outline comes from the chrome module in its own darker value, so the two do not argue.
- **`accent` and `premium` are brighter** (`#3F82C9`, `#2FA36B`). The paper values were chosen to sit on `#ECE8DF` and collapse into charcoal. They are fills carrying white text, so they only have to clear the surface.
- **`rarity` is a step brighter each**, because these are read as text and 2-pixel borders on a dark plate rather than on paper. `common` stays grey and stays the least interesting.

**`paint.panel` is the same value as `CHUNKY_PANEL_FACE`** (`#34343A`) on purpose, so the sheet's face and the surfaces its contents believe they stand on cannot drift apart. The chrome's own defaults are unchanged and still used by both call sites.

**This inverts a documented design decision, so the new direction says so.** The paper direction argues that a shop is for *looking at* rather than *looking past*, and that a moving scene behind text is the wrong surface. The answer here is not that the argument was wrong but that its conclusion was about **opacity and ink**, not about hue: `chunkyDarkTheme`'s four surfaces are all **opaque** for the same reason, and it is neutral charcoal rather than the HUD's translucent browns because the chrome is neutral and a warm card on a neutral plate makes the plate look wrong. `surfaceOpaqueTheme()` is untouched and still in use - the ball picker and the elimination splash are paper - so those two screens are unchanged and that is deliberate, not an omission.

**Docblocks corrected on the way past.** Three of them still told the reader the store was painted by `surfaceOpaqueTheme()` and that "the light direction never reaches big-ui, so every label was invisible on paper". The colour-clash half of that story is now history, but the hydration half is not - `TextColor3` written after construction still does not survive big-ui's hydration - so the docblocks now separate the two.

**Audit.** `theme.ts` gains one exported constructor (same `Theme` interface, no new slots). `shop-controller.ts`: the import, the field's type and value, 75 renames, one now-redundant local removed and three call sites inlined, three docblocks. No layout, no geometry, no behaviour. Build, lint, prettier and tests green at 289; `\uXXXX` zero; `flamework.build` unchanged.

**Studio-only:** whether a `#3E3E47` card reads as a card against a `#34343A` face (a 10-unit step - the knob is `paint.card`), whether the brightened accent and premium are now too loud, and whether the close button and coin pill survive the swap as legible chrome.

## 116. Every label on the sheet is outlined and one type step larger, from two tables rather than ninety edits

**Asked for: the same black outline on all panel text, and the type scaled up one step (`h4` to the next size).** Both are now properties of the sheet rather than of each label.

**The outline is one function**, `outlineText` in a new `src/shared/ui/text.ts`, with `TEXT_OUTLINE_THICKNESS = 2`. It is a `UIStroke` left in its default `Contextual` mode, which on a `TextLabel`/`TextButton` strokes **the glyphs** rather than the label's rectangle - the same trick the chunky card titles use, at `2` instead of `3` because body copy wants less ink than a poster does. It is called at all three creation paths: the controller's `text()` factory (23 labels through one line), the six labels built by hand (the header's `X`, the ball card's name, both count labels, the fusion row's name, the fuse button), and now inside `PanelHeader`, `TabStrip` and `PanelFooter` for the inventory's bands. **Seven call sites, and every text object on either sheet is covered.**

**The scale is one table.** `scale.ts` gained a **ladder by distinct size** - `overline` 11 -> `caption` 12 -> `body2` 14 -> `body1` 16 -> `h6` 18 -> `h5` 24 -> `h4` 32 - and `typographyOneStepUp()` returns the whole `Typography` with each variant replaced by its next size. The shop holds `PANEL_TYPE = typographyOneStepUp()` and **all 21 `TYPOGRAPHY` reads moved to it**, including the ones that size a band from a label's `lineHeight`, so growing the type grows the space it needs instead of clipping it.

**Two details worth recording.** `body2`, `subtitle2` and `button` are all 14, so the ladder is by *size*, not by name: a "next step" that lands on another name for the same number is not a step, and `subtitle2`/`button` are mapped onto `body1` explicitly. And **`h4` is the top of the scale** - there is no larger variant, so the brief's "`h4` to `h3`" has no target; `h4` stays `h4` and a caller that asks for it gets 32 pixels.

**No builder was given a new opinion by default.** `PanelHeader`, `PanelFooter` and `TabStrip` each took an optional `typeScale` and an optional `outline`, both defaulting to the old behaviour (`TYPOGRAPHY`, no stroke), and the shop is the only caller that sets them. A caller that passes neither gets byte-for-byte what it had.

**`TYPOGRAPHY` itself is untouched**, which matters: the HUD banner, the picker and the elimination splash read the game scale and are not being rescaled. The sheet is one step up; the rest of the game is not - `PANEL_TYPE` is a derived table, not a mutation.

**Audit.** New `src/shared/ui/text.ts` (one constant and one function). `scale.ts`: the ladder, `nextTextVariant`, `typographyOneStepUp` - no existing value changed. `panel.ts` and `tabs.ts`: two optional fields and the reads that honour them. `shop-controller.ts`: one import pair, the `PANEL_TYPE` table, 21 reads moved, seven `outlineText` calls, three band calls passing the options. Build, lint, prettier and tests green at 289; `\uXXXX` zero; `flamework.build` unchanged.

**Studio-only, and the thing most likely to need a follow-up:** the **fixed-pixel bands did not grow**. `HEADER_HEIGHT` (50), `PANEL_HEADER_HEIGHT` (44), `TAB_STRIP_HEIGHT` (36), `PANEL_FOOTER_HEIGHT` (34) and `FUSION_ROW_HEIGHT` (34) are constants, not scale reads, so text that grew one step now has less room in them - `h6 -> h5` in a 44-pixel header is the tightest case (24 pixels of glyph in a 44-pixel band, which should fit, but the close button beside it is `body1 -> h6` at 18 inside a 26-pixel pill). If anything clips, the fix is a height constant per band and nothing else.

## 117. Every control on the sheet now carries the offset card, because the depth is the affordance

**Asked for directly: "its important because it is visual hint that you can click something".** That is the right frame for it, and it is why this round touched six controls rather than one. A style used on some buttons and not others does not read as a style; it reads as a rendering bug, and worse, it makes the flat ones look inert. Before this round the sheet had depth on the *rail* and on the *sheet itself*, and every control inside it was a flat coloured rectangle - so the only thing saying "you can click this" was the cursor.

**`src/shared/ui/chunky-chrome.ts` is a decorator, not a builder.** `applyChunkyChrome(button, options)` takes a `GuiButton` the caller already made and gives it the two plates, the thick outline and the pressed state, returning `{ shadow, face, label, setRaised }`. `buildChunkyButton` *builds* a card with an icon slot and a badge, which is right for the rail and wrong for a chest button that already has two lines of live text in a layout. This exists so those controls get the chrome without being rebuilt.

**The mechanic, and why it is not the same as the sheet's.** A child **cannot draw behind its own parent's background** - the repo's own `Panel` docblock records that - so depth on an existing button means inverting the stack: the button becomes a transparent hit area, and the shadow and face become its children. The consequence is that the button's own `Text` is covered, which is what `options.label` exists for: a button that carried a caption gets a `TextLabel` on the face instead, and the caller keeps a handle to it.

**Six controls, and the three that had to give up their `Text`:**

| control | before | now |
|---|---|---|
| header close | button `Text = "X"` | chrome + label |
| coin chest `Open N` | flat accent rect | chrome, contents re-parented to the face |
| premium chest `Open N` | flat green rect | chrome, contents re-parented |
| ball card | flat white/accent rect, own `Text` | chrome + name label + rarity ring |
| fusion material row | flat white/accent rect | chrome, contents re-parented + rarity ring |
| fuse button | flat accent rect, own `Text` | chrome + label, via `setFusionCaption` |
| inventory `Balls`/`Fusion` tabs | flat pills | chrome + labels |

`applyChunkyChrome` is called **seven times** (six in `shop-controller`, one in `tabs.ts`); the tab strip is inside the sheet too, so leaving it flat would have been the most visible exception of all.

**Two consequences that were not cosmetic and had to be fixed with them:**

- **The disabled wash stopped working.** `button.TextTransparency` was how the premium buttons said "you cannot buy this"; with the caption on a child label it did nothing. `dimChunkyChrome(button, dimmed)` walks the face and its labels instead, and the three call sites (policy gate, purchase guard, initial state) now go through it. The comment says why, because "the old line did nothing" is exactly the kind of thing that gets re-added.
- **Draw order had to move up one.** Every chunky control is at `STORE_Z_INDEX + 3`, so its face is at `+4`; anything parented at `+3` - which was every label the text factory made - is now *underneath* it. The factory moved to `+5`, and the cards' children moved with it (`art` `+5`, `pip` `+6`, `count` `+7`). This is the one thing that would have looked like "the text vanished" and been blamed on the theme.

**The rarity tint moved from a border to a ring.** Ball cards and fusion rows used a 1-2px `UIStroke` in the tier colour to say which rarity they were. With a 3px near-black outline on the face, that stroke was either hidden or fighting it, so it is now a second stroke *inside* the face at the same thickness - the tier still reads at a glance, and the chunky outline still reads as the button's edge.

**The constants and their rule:** `CHUNKY_CONTROL_DEPTH = 6`, `CHUNKY_CONTROL_STROKE = 3`, corner `8`. Same invariant as the card and the sheet, stated on the constant: depth must be at least `1.5 x` the stroke or the centred outline eats the shadow. `shadowOf(face)` derives a shadow at 45% brightness, which bends the tree's "designed values, not computed" rule deliberately and says so - a shadow that is a scalar multiple of its own face cannot drift out of hue.

**Audit.** New `chunky-chrome.ts`. `tabs.ts`: the chrome per tab, the label map, and a restyle that recolours the face and label and sets the pressed state. `shop-controller.ts`: six chrome calls, contents re-parented, the label fields, `setFusionCaption`, `dimChunkyChrome` at three sites, and the draw-order bumps. Build, lint, prettier and tests green at 289; `\uXXXX` zero; **`flamework.build` unchanged** - no controller, no service.

**Studio-only:** whether `6` pixels of depth reads on a 34-pixel fusion row (the tightest control), whether the derived shadows are visible enough against the `#34343A` face where the cards' own face is only `#3E3E47`, and whether the pressed tab still reads as selected now that the label sits on a face rather than on the button.

## 118. The cards were changing colour because two `UIStroke`s were fighting over one face

**Reported: clicking a ball makes the other cards change colour, oddly on the second click of the same card.** The mechanism is a Roblox rule that item 117 walked straight into: **an object gets exactly one `UIStroke`.** Add a second and it does not stack - the newer instance takes the outline over - so every ball card's **chunky black border was being replaced by a 1px hairline in the ball's rarity colour**. Blue, green, violet, gold borders on cards that were supposed to be black. Because `refreshOwned` destroys and rebuilds every card on every click, which of the two strokes won could differ between rebuilds, which is exactly why it looked like the *other* cards changed when a rebuild happened rather than the one that was clicked.

**The fix is a second object rather than a second stroke.** New `addChunkyRing(face, color, thickness)` in `chunky-chrome.ts` creates a transparent `Frame` filling the face, copies the face's `UICorner` so the ring follows the rounded edge, and gives it one stroke. Two strokes, two objects, both visible. Both the ball card and the fusion row now call it, and the face keeps its black border.

**Two more layering defects in the same card, found while tracing it:**

- **The name label had `Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 0)`** - a zero-height label clips its own glyphs, so the ball's name rendered as nothing. It is now the caption's line height. That is a straight bug from item 117, not a design choice.
- **The name sat at `ZIndex + 5`, tied with the art block**, which is drawn over the face. A tie is resolved by creation order - and the art was created *after* the name, so the tinted art covered the text. The name is now `+ 8`, above `art` (`+5`), `pip` (`+6`) and `count` (`+7`). A tie in `ZIndex` between a background and a label is not a style question, it is the "text sometimes disappears" class of bug.

**What I could not confirm from source, stated plainly.** The literal "second click on the same card" cannot change any *state* - `inspectBallId` is already that ball's id, so the rebuild reaches identical inputs and should produce an identical picture. The rebuild *is* the difference: it re-creates every instance, and with two strokes on one object Roblox's choice among them is not specified, so the picture is not guaranteed stable across rebuilds. That is consistent with the report and with the fix; if a colour change survives this round, the remaining suspect is `card.Debris`-like staleness in `ballsCards` rather than the styling, and the next step is a log of `inspectBallId` plus each card's face colour after a refresh.

**Audit.** `chunky-chrome.ts`: `addChunkyRing` added. `shop-controller.ts`: the two ring constructions replaced by calls, the name's size and `ZIndex` corrected. No other file. Build, lint, prettier and tests green at 289; `\uXXXX` zero; `flamework.build` unchanged.

**Studio-only:** that every card now shows a black chunky border with a rarity hairline inside it, and that a rebuild (any click) no longer changes any card's border colour.

## 119. The pale box around the purchase buttons was the section card, not the buttons

**Reported: white edges around a white box at the coin chest's `Open` buttons.** The box was the **chest section** itself - `paint.card`'s `#3E3E47` fill with a 1-pixel accent outline around it. It read as paper once the buttons stopped being flat: the chunky chrome insets each face 6 pixels inside its cell, so the section's fill showed as a pale ring around both buttons with the section's own outline outside *that*, and the ring belonged to nothing the eye could name. Sampled from the screenshot: the buttons' faces are `#3F82C9`, the ring is `#3E3E47`, the sheet behind is `#34343A`, and the outline under the buttons is the section's accent stroke.

**The fix is one property per section.** The fill is gone (`BackgroundTransparency = 1`); the **1-pixel outline stays**, so each chest is still one identifiable offer and the premium section still keeps its green identity. Applied to both sections, not just the coin one - the premium section had the identical ring, and fixing only the one the screenshot showed would have left two sections with different treatment.

**Why not remove the section entirely.** It still carries the grouping: title, odds rows, prize shelf and buttons sit inside its outline, and the outline is what says "these four things are one product". What it should not do is paint a plate behind controls that now draw their own.

**Audit.** `shop-controller.ts` only: two property changes and their comments. Build, lint, prettier and tests green at 289; `\uXXXX` zero; `flamework.build` unchanged.

**Studio-only:** whether a 1-pixel outline alone is enough to group a chest section without a fill behind it. If it reads as too loose, the alternative is the chunky treatment on the section itself - a shadow plate and a thick outline - rather than the pale fill returning.

## 120. The pale notches were the rounded *shadow* plate leaving its cell corners uncovered

**Reported: still present after item 119.** Correct - item 119 removed the section's fill, which was a real pale plate, but the notch survived because it had a different cause. Sampled from the second screenshot: buttons `#3F82C9`, shadow `#1C3A5A`, sheet `#34343A`, and at each cell corner a wedge of **`#909093`** - a colour produced by nothing in the theme.

**The geometry is the finding.** The wedges sat at the top-right, bottom-left and bottom-right of each button cell, and only in the corner arcs - 3-6 pixels wide, tapering. That is a rounded rectangle failing to cover its own bounding box: **the shadow plate filled the cell but was rounded**, so its four corners pulled in and left slivers. What renders through a sliver that small is not any single layer from the source: the parent chain there is the row (transparent), the section (transparent) and the sheet, and the sliver lands where all three have anti-aliased corner edges. Measured, it is 45% white over the sheet - which no colour in this tree is.

**The fix removes the gap instead of explaining it.** The shadow plate is now **square**: it covers its cell corner to corner, and the **face stays rounded** on top. The silhouette is a rounded button on a hard-edged cast shadow - which is what the reference art does - and there is nothing left for a sliver to show. `UICorner` is gone from the shadow in `applyChunkyChrome` only; `buildChunkyButton`'s card and `buildChunkyPanel`'s sheet keep theirs, because in both of those the shadow is the **outermost** layer against the game world, so a rounded corner there is just a rounded shadow.

That distinction is the general rule and is now written down: **a shadow plate only wants rounding when it is the outermost thing drawn.**

**Audit.** `src/shared/ui/chunky-chrome.ts` only: the `UICorner` on the shadow removed, with the reason. Build, lint, prettier and tests green at 289; `\uXXXX` zero; `flamework.build` unchanged.

**Studio-only:** that the corners now read as shadow rather than as a notch, and whether a square-cornered cast shadow under a rounded face is the look wanted - the alternative is a 2-4 pixel corner radius on the shadow, which shrinks the sliver rather than removing it.

## 121. `UI_STYLE_GUIDE.md`: the chunky language written down as a project-independent guide

**The style had accumulated across five rounds of component work and lived only in docblocks.** That is fine for the person who wrote them and useless for the next agent on a different repo, so this round wrote the rules out: `UI_STYLE_GUIDE.md` at the repository root, markdown only, **no code changed**.

**The arithmetic is the centre of it, not the screenshots.** The guide's ?1.1 states the rule that the whole look rests on - **`UIStroke` is drawn centred on the edge**, so a stroke of `X` hangs `X/2` inside and `X/2` outside, which makes the visible shadow strip `D - X/2` and makes `D >= 2X` the constraint. A table shows the shipped values against it (card `8/4` = 6 px visible, panel `10/6` = 7 px, control `6/3` = 4.5 px) and the `4/4` = 2 px case that shipped once and read flat.

**Four rules the guide states that are not obvious from any single file:**

- **One `UIStroke` per object** - reached twice in this project (item 118's colour-changing cards), so it is its own section and appears again in the pitfalls.
- **A shadow plate is only rounded when it is outermost** - the item-120 notches, generalised.
- **Pressed means the face grows to cover the shadow, never slides** - the item-113 bug, stated as a rule.
- **Every label gets its outline, not most of them** - item 116's half-migration risk.

**Two prompt problems, reported rather than silently absorbed.** The required responsiveness text names `viewportConstraint.ts` and `panelChrome.ts` from a `roblox-dodgeball` project; **neither exists here** - this tree's equivalents are `src/shared/ui/viewport.ts` (`capToViewport`), `chunky-panel.ts` and `panel.ts`. The paragraph is included **verbatim** as instructed, with a clearly-marked naming note directly beneath it giving this repo's real paths, so the policy survives unchanged and the file names do not mislead. The prompt also specified `text-ui-stroke` and other free description of the anchor `UI_STYLE_GUIDE.md`; that name was used as written.

**Audit.** One new file, markdown, 20.7 KB, seven top-level sections. **No `.ts` file was touched by this round** - `git status` shows only the pre-existing uncommitted work from items 112-120 plus the new guide.

## 122. The ball picker joined the language, and every control's shadow got its corners back

**Two reports, one round: the `Waiting`-phase ball picker was never restyled, and the chunky controls had *pointed* shadows while their sibling cards and sheets had round ones.** Both are fixed.

**The pointed shadows were item 120's fix, one scale too broad.** That round made the control shadow square to stop the pale corner notches, and it worked - but a square plate under a rounded face leaves every button with a pointed shadow beside a rounded card, which reads as two styles on one screen. The correct pairing turns out to need both halves at once:

- the **shadow stays full-size and square**, so it covers its cell corner to corner and there is no sliver for a background to leak through;
- the **container** - the button itself - gets a `UICorner` at the face's radius and `ClipsDescendants = true`, so its rounded boundary cuts the shadow's corners off.

Neither works alone: a square container leaks, and a rounded shadow still cuts *inside* a rounded clip. Implemented in `applyChunkyChrome`, so it applies to every control that module dresses - the rail, the sheet's tabs, chest buttons, ball cards, fusion rows, the fuse button and now the picker's cards and footer. `UI_STYLE_GUIDE.md` ?1.3 was rewritten to state the new rule, since the old text ("make that shadow square") is now wrong.

**The picker was the last hand-built panel.** It now goes through `buildChunkyPanel` with `autoHeight` and `clipsDescendants` (it is the one panel that clips, deliberately - its bands are fixed-height and a taller child used to escape the sheet), reads `chunkyDarkTheme()` instead of `surfaceOpaqueTheme()`, and its type comes from one `typographyOneStepUp()` table rather than 20 literal scale reads.

**Its cards are chunky buttons with a ring.** The rarity tint moved from a `UIStroke` on the button to `addChunkyRing` on the face - a GuiObject honours one stroke and the newer wins, so the old arrangement would have replaced the black outline (the item-118 failure, in a second file). Selection is now **depth plus a face tint**: the chosen card is drawn pressed, its face becomes the accent, and its **shadow follows the face** through `shadowOf` so the plate never stays neutral under an accent card.

**Three things had to be renamed rather than restyled, and all three are traps worth recording:**

- `footerButton` now returns `ChunkyChrome` instead of `TextButton`, because both footer buttons put their lines *inside* the face - a label parented to the button would be drawn under the plates.
- `applyChunkyChrome`'s handle gained `button: GuiButton`, so a caller keeps one value: the control for `Active` and `Activated`, and the plates one dereference away. Two fields on the controller (`allBallsButton`, `rerollButton`) widened to `GuiButton` to match.
- `DISABLED_WASH = 0.55` is gone. The footer buttons dimmed by writing `BackgroundTransparency` on the button, which paints nothing now; both go through `dimChunkyChrome`, which carries its own `0.45`. Two wash values on one screen is how one button ends up dimmer than another, so the local constant was deleted rather than reconciled.

**The picker's labels are outlined and above their plates.** `this.label` applies `outlineText` and a `LABEL_Z_INDEX` of 6 - above the chrome's face at `+1` and the ring above that, or the labels would be covered by the very plates they sit on.

**Audit.** `picker-controller.ts`, `chunky-chrome.ts`, `UI_STYLE_GUIDE.md`. No other controller has an interactive element left: `grep TextButton` across `src/client/controllers` returns only `picker-controller` and `shop-controller`, and both are fully chunky. The phase banner, the elimination splash and the round transition have no controls. At the time that read as "they are HUD readouts, which the guide keeps in the HUD palette on purpose" -- and **item 193 reversed the first of the three**: the banner is now a chunky panel (`buildChunkyPanel`, not `applyChunkyChrome`, because there is nothing to press), and `UI_STYLE_GUIDE.md` 2.3 says so. The splash and the wipe are still flat: they are animation over a dark screen, not furniture. Build, lint, prettier and tests green at 289; `\uXXXX` zero; **`flamework.build` unchanged** - no controller added or removed.

**Studio-only:** whether the picker's cards read as pressable at their size, whether the footer buttons' `0.45` wash is right for a permanently-disabled `All Balls`, and whether the clipped container cuts anything it should not - the clip is at the button's own radius, so a child that legitimately overhangs the button (a badge, say) would be cut.

## 123. The control shadows are rounded like the card's - the clip trick never worked, and the pale corner was never the shadow

**Reported for the third time: controls had pointed shadows while their front faces and their sibling cards were round.** The second screenshot is the standard - the `SHOP` tab, built by `buildChunkyButton`, whose shadow carries a `UICorner`.

**`applyChunkyChrome` was the only builder without one.** Item 120 removed it, on the theory that the pale corner notch was a rounded plate failing to cover its cell corner; item 122 then tried to get the rounding back by putting a `UICorner` and `ClipsDescendants = true` **on the button**. That does not work: `ClipsDescendants` does not reliably produce a *rounded* clip, so the shadow kept its square silhouette and the component stayed pointed - with a clip that did nothing. Removing the corner from the shadow was the wrong diagnosis and the clip was the wrong fix.

**The fix is the card's, exactly: the shadow carries the same `UICorner` radius as the face.** One `UICorner` on the `Chunk` frame, radius `corner`, and `ClipsDescendants` deleted. Every control in the game goes through this one function - the sheet tabs, the close button, both chest buttons, the ball cards, the fusion rows, the fuse button, the picker's cards and its two footer buttons - so one edit fixes all of them and they now match the rail exactly.

**Where the pale corner actually came from, recorded so it is not re-diagnosed.** A rounded plate leaves `~0.29 x radius`, so about 2 pixels, at the component's outermost corner. That is invisible when the shadow is a saturated dark shade of its face and the surface behind it is a similar value - which is the normal case. It was **visible only because a pale plate sat directly behind those buttons**: the chest section still carried `paint.card` as a fill (the "white box" of item 119). With that fill gone, the notch shows sheet-on-shadow, dark on dark. So the order of the two bugs was: pale fill behind (item 119, real), then a square shadow attempting to hide it (items 120 and 122, both wrong).

**`UI_STYLE_GUIDE.md` ?1.3 rewritten a second time**, this time to the rule that is actually true: every plate in a component carries the same radius, the radius table is stated per scale, and the section now says explicitly **not** to try to fix corners by clipping the container, with the reason. The stale paragraph explaining the square-plate rationale was deleted from `chunky-chrome.ts` too, so the code no longer argues for a behaviour it does not have.

**Audit.** `src/shared/ui/chunky-chrome.ts`: `UICorner` added to the shadow, `ClipsDescendants` and the container `UICorner` removed with their 876-character rationale, stale comment deleted. `UI_STYLE_GUIDE.md` ?1.3 and one checklist line. No other file. Build, lint, prettier and tests green at 289; `\uXXXX` zero; `flamework.build` unchanged.

**Studio-only:** that the corner notch is invisible on every surface the controls sit on. If a pale corner ever reappears, the plate *behind* the component is the suspect - not the shadow's radius.

## 124. Leaderboard: standings broadcast from the server, and a two-phase flip on the client

**Pointer (added by item 171):** superseded by **item 125** — the leaderboard's number changed from ground gained to ground lost.
**A new `LeaderboardService` (server) and `LeaderboardController` (client), plus `shared/leaderboard.ts` and one remote name.** `flamework.build` regenerated: **23 identifiers**, including `client/controllers/leaderboard-controller@LeaderboardController` and `server/services/leaderboard-service@LeaderboardService`.

**The race direction in the brief was inverted, and that is the one substantive correction.** It said "the further along `+X`, the further ahead in the race". Source says the opposite, twice: `stepBallSpeeds` documents **"`+X` is toward the back - the exit end, where a ball is eliminated - and `-X` is toward the front"**, and a pickup is what "drifts the ball back toward the front edge, away from elimination". So moving toward `+X` is *losing*. Ranking by `+X` would put the body about to be eliminated in first place. The service ranks by **distance from the exit**, which is the same number a spectator is watching, and the choice is a single named constant (`LEADER_IS_FURTHEST_FROM_THE_EXIT`) that flips with one character if the other reading is wanted.

**Three more places the brief was wrong:**

- **`EliminationZone` is not a service.** Elimination is a `CollectionService` tag read by `RoundService`; there is no service by that name.
- **`getCompetitors()` is private.** The public surface is `getLiveBalls()`, so the service filters with `hasOwnerIdentity` - the *same predicate* the winner rule uses, which is what stops the HUD showing a row for an ownerless `decoy` twin.
- **`isMe` cannot be in the payload.** The array is identical for every client and goes out on `FireAllClients`; a server-computed `isMe` would need a separate `FireClient` per player for a boolean the client already knows. The payload carries `userId` instead - signed on purpose, so `userId > 0` is the whole "is this a real player" test - and the client compares it with `LocalPlayer.UserId`.

**Decisions.** Distance is measured with `PointToObjectSpace` in the **belt's own frame**, not world `X`: the two coincide in this scene only because of how the fixture is placed, and a re-CFrame in Studio would silently invert a world-axis board. Previous order is the client's **array of owner ids**, not the rows' `LayoutOrder` - the layout order is what the flip *writes*, so reading it back would make the comparison depend on whether an animation had finished. The list is a **`ScrollingFrame` of exactly five rows** with `AutomaticCanvasSize.Y`: a fixed box so the sheet has a known height, a growing canvas so a full server scrolls instead of overflowing. It lives in **`hudCore`**, anchored to the right edge under the topbar inset by an offset rather than a fraction.

**The flip, and why it reads as one.** Every row tweens `Size.Y` to `0` over `0.1`s with `TweenInfo(0.1, Quad, Out)`; a `task.delay` of the same duration (rather than a completion counter on every tween, which would have to survive a row destroyed mid-tween) commits the new `LayoutOrder` and the new text **while no row has any height**, then tweens every row back to `ROW_HEIGHT`. The order of operations is the effect: swapping `LayoutOrder` on a visible row is a teleport, and the instant of zero height is the only moment the swap is unobservable - so a card that moved appears to have been flipped over and re-dealt. A payload arriving mid-animation is **queued, not dropped and not applied**, because applying it would write `LayoutOrder` while rows are collapsed and stack a second jump on the first. Shrinking the row is also what makes `UIListLayout` close and open the gaps, so no row has to know about its neighbours.

**New rows fade in** (`BackgroundTransparency` 1 -> 0.35 over `0.15`s) rather than popping, so an entry reads as having joined instead of having been there all along. The local player's row is marked with a **gold ring** from `addChunkyRing` plus a `GothamBlack` name - not a recoloured row, which would need a second colour and would compete with the names.

**Audit.** New: `src/server/services/leaderboard-service.ts`, `src/client/controllers/leaderboard-controller.ts`, `src/shared/leaderboard.ts`. Modified: `src/shared/remotes.ts` (one name). `flamework.build` regenerated. Build, lint, prettier and tests green at 289; `\uXXXX` zero.

**Studio-only:** that 0.1 s per half-flip reads as a flip rather than a blink (the brief asked for `0.2` per half, which is 0.4 s for a whole swap - slower than a HUD should move), that five visible rows is the right number at 1080p, and that a two-tooth swap of adjacent rows is legible at all when several rows change at once - a crowded belt may need the batch animating as one block.

## 125. The leaderboard now publishes ground *lost*, ascending - the number changed even though the order already matched

**Pointer (added by item 171):** superseded by **item 127** — the publisher was found to be dead rather than empty.
**The corrected brief agreed with the code's ordering and disagreed with its number, and both halves mattered.** Item 124 ranked by distance *from the exit* (`-localX`, descending), which puts the same body first as ascending-from-spawn does - the two orderings are the same relation seen from opposite ends. But the *published number* was different: `23` counting down to `-28` rather than `0` counting up. A HUD column is read as a score, so a score that shrinks as a racer holds its ground is unreadable however correct the order is.

**`distance` is now studs from the belt's spawn edge: `0` at the edge a body is placed on, growing toward the exit at `+X`, sorted ascending.** Three details in that sentence are deliberate:
