A session-long `unusable` would mean a player who leaves Studio open hears nothing all evening because a moderation queue drained at 21:30. `reviveIfStale` clears the list, the `disabled` flag and `deadAt` once `LOBBY_RETRY_AFTER_SECONDS = 120` has passed — and it runs **only when `pickable()` is empty**, so the lobby would have been silent anyway and the retry cannot take music away. `os.clock()`, not `tick()`, because this measures a gap between two lobbies and `tick()` stops while the engine is suspended.

**Random while both work, forced once one is dead.** The item-157 requirement — a random pick per lobby — survives untouched: `pickLobbySong` over `pickable()` is random while both are candidates, and on a one-element array it can only return that element. The two rules compose without a special case.

**The preload is still not allowed to decide.** It would have been tempting to use `liked`/`disliked` to order the attempts and save the ten seconds. That is the same mistake item 157's first Studio run made, one size smaller: `PreloadAsync` reported the identical failure for a valid *image*, so a false negative would silently decide which song plays by default. It stays a diagnostic.

**Log lines.** `[LobbySong] skipped song=<id> reason=not-loaded after <n>s — the Sound never reported a length (IsLoaded=…, TimeLength=…)` · `[LobbySong] skipped song=<id> reason=too-short length=<n>s (needs more than 15s)` · `[LobbySong] fallback after=<id> trying=<id|…>` · `[LobbySong] play … after=<id>` (the `after=` field is **absent** when the first pick worked, so its presence is the signal) · `[LobbySong] no asset loaded, silent (tried=<A|B>)` · `[LobbySong] retrying every id after 120s — a dead set is not a dead session`.

**Audit.** Changed: `src/client/controllers/lobby-song-controller.ts` only — `LOBBY_LOAD_BUDGET_SECONDS`/`LOBBY_MIN_ATTEMPT_SECONDS`/`LOBBY_RETRY_AFTER_SECONDS` replace `LOBBY_LOAD_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, new `attempt`/`deadAt`/`failedThisLobby` state, `retire` replaces `giveUp`, new `reviveIfStale`/`afterNote`/`attemptSeconds`, `awaitLoaded` takes its timeout as a parameter, the class docblock gained a fallback section. Build exit 0, lint 0 problems, prettier clean, `\uXXXX` zero, `flamework.build` still **30 identifiers**. **`npm test` not run.** Untouched: `song.ts`, `lobby-song.ts`, `lobby-song.spec.ts`, the config, `RoundSongController`, the picker, the countdown, the wipe and the phase machine.

**Placeholders:** `LOBBY_LOAD_BUDGET_SECONDS = 10` (was `LOBBY_LOAD_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 10`), `LOBBY_MIN_ATTEMPT_SECONDS = 3`, `LOBBY_RETRY_AFTER_SECONDS = 120`. No others changed.

**Studio-only:** whether the fallback ever fires on a healthy pair — it should not, and `play … after=` appearing in a normal session would mean the first clip is genuinely unavailable; how long a freshly uploaded audio asset stays unservable, which is what `LOBBY_RETRY_AFTER_SECONDS` is guessing at; and whether five seconds is long enough for a cold fetch of a music clip on a slow connection (the boot preload is meant to have warmed it by the first `Intermission`, so the five-second window should never be the binding constraint).

## 159. A player is a competitor only if they were here five seconds before the lobby ended

**Reported as a rule, not a bug:** a player who connects during `Intermission` — or during `Waiting` — became a competitor on the next round, because the competitor list is decided at `Waiting` entry from `Players.GetPlayers()` at that instant. The round now enrolls a player only if they were connected before the last `ENROLLMENT_CUTOFF_SECONDS` (5 s) of `Intermission`; anybody later spectates until the next lobby. Debug keys still put every connected player on a lane.

**One set, one gate.** `enrolledUserIds: Set<number>` is membership; `enrollmentOpen: boolean` is whether a join still enrolls; `enrollmentGeneration: number` retires a stale close. Seeded at window open from `Players.GetPlayers()` — a player already present when the lobby starts is not a late joiner — and kept live by `PlayerAdded` (adds while open) and `PlayerRemoving` (always removes). The set is a **running set, not a snapshot**: somebody who arrived at end − 10 s and left at end − 3 s is removed, so a body is never spawned for a player who is gone. `spawnRoundCompetitors` iterates connected players and filters on the set, so a `UserId` left in the set after a departure is simply never matched.

**The window opens in `startIntermissionTimer`, not in `enterIntermission`, and that is the load-bearing correction to the brief.** The brief assumed every `Intermission` entry is a new `enterIntermission` call. Verified from source: **it is not.** The zero-player re-arm is a `continue` inside the timer's own `while` loop and never re-enters the phase, and `onStart` arms the timer directly because the boot state already *is* `Intermission`. Opening the window at phase entry would therefore have left every re-armed lobby with a permanently closed window: `PlayerAdded` stops enrolling, the first joiner is never a competitor, `startWaitingRound` returns zero, the timer re-arms again — a deadlock whose log reads as "waiting for a player" while a player stands in the lobby. The window is opened once per **loop iteration**, with `span = INTERMISSION_SECONDS + (first ? hold : 0)`, so the close lands five seconds before the phase actually ends, wipe hold included.

**The close is idempotent and has two callers.** The scheduled `task.delay(span − cutoff)` is the cutoff; `enterWaiting` also closes, because a debug press can leave `Intermission` at t = 10 and a flag saying "open" through `Waiting` is a lie waiting to be read as a bug. `closeEnrollmentWindow` returns early if it is already closed, so one window prints one line whichever path wins. The stale close from a re-armed window is retired by the generation check.

**The set is deliberately not cleared at `Waiting` entry, against the brief.** Clearing would make `enrolled=` on every later spawn read `false`, including the bodies a debug key spawns — and that field exists precisely to tell those two cases apart. The gate is `enrollmentOpen`, not the set's contents; the next window clears it when it seeds.

**`spawnRoundCompetitors(reason, useEnrollment, drawBallIds = false)` — `useEnrollment` has no default, and `drawBallIds` moved to third.** A default is a policy nobody wrote down: `false` would silently exempt every future caller from the cutoff (the bug this item fixes), `true` would spawn nobody in a lobby whose set is empty. Every call site states its answer — the intermission timer and `startWaitingRound` pass `true`, `forceWaiting`/key `2` and `forcePlaying`/key `3` pass `false`. `forcePlaying` and `debugSpawnCompetitors` were never in the filter's path: the latter calls `spawnBots` and never reaches `spawnRoundCompetitors` at all.

**The offers follow the same flag.** `openOffers(useEnrollment)` skips a non-enrolled player, so a spectator is not handed a "choose your ball" panel for a body that will never exist. That is a change to the picker's *input*, not to the picker: a competitor's window, deadline, re-roll and close are untouched, and the brief's "no change to the picker" is honoured in the sense that matters (no competitor sees anything different). The alternative — a panel appearing, a pick accepted, and no ball — is the louder lie.

**Two zeros are now two lines.** `spawn refused — no players connected` and `spawn refused — N connected, none enrolled` are the same return value and opposite situations: a server waiting for a player, versus a player watching a round they will not be in. The second is what produces the timer's `restarted — no competitors spawned`, which then re-opens the window with that player seeded, so they play the round after next.

**A rejoin after the cutoff is a spectator, even if the first join was inside it.** Because removal is real, a `UserId` that leaves is gone from the set, and the rejoin fires `PlayerAdded` against a closed window. The brief's Decision 3 says the opposite of its Decision 8; Decision 8 is the one that follows from the running set the user chose, and it is what the code does.

**New log lines.** `[Enrollment] window open generation=<n> seeded=<n>` · `[Enrollment] window closed generation=<n> enrolled=<n> cutoff=5s` · `[Enrollment] late join "<name>" (generation=<n>) — spectating until next Intermission` · `[Round] spawn skipped not-enrolled=<n> of <n> connected (<reason>)` · `[Round] spawn refused — <n> connected, none enrolled (<reason>)` · `[Picker] offer skipped player=<name> (not enrolled this round)` · and `[Round] spawn lane=… owner=… enrolled=<bool> body=…` — the fact, not the decision, so a `false` there means a debug key put that body on the belt.

**Audit.** Changed: `src/shared/tuning.ts` (`ENROLLMENT_CUTOFF_SECONDS`, beside `PICKER_WINDOW_SECONDS`), `src/server/services/round-service.ts` (`enrolledUserIds`/`enrollmentGeneration`/`enrollmentOpen` state, `PlayerAdded`/`PlayerRemoving` connections in `onStart`, `openEnrollmentWindow`/`closeEnrollmentWindow`/`enrollOnJoin`, the window opened per iteration in `startIntermissionTimer`, the filter and two new log families in `spawnRoundCompetitors`, `useEnrollment` threaded through `startWaitingRound` and `openOffers`, `enterWaiting` closing the window, four call sites updated, and item 36's "reads `Players.GetPlayers()` after the clear" comment rewritten in place to say the read is now filtered on one path and not the other). Build exit 0, lint 0 problems, prettier clean, `\uXXXX` zero in `src`, `flamework.build` unchanged at **30 identifiers** — no new controller or service. **`npm test` not run.** Untouched: `RoundSong`, `LobbySong`, the camera, the picker's window/deadline/re-roll/close, the countdown, the transition wipe, the phase machine, the economy, the winner rule, `forcePlaying`'s and `debugSpawnCompetitors`' own spawn paths, the leaderboard, and the payout.

**Placeholders:** `ENROLLMENT_CUTOFF_SECONDS = 5` (`src/shared/tuning.ts`). Nothing else invented.

**Studio-only:** whether a player who joins six seconds before `Intermission` ends is genuinely enrolled — the `[Enrollment] window open/closed` pair plus `enrolled=` on the spawn line answer it; whether the ~25 s between `Intermission` entry and the spawn is enough for a client to boot and appear on a lane (a client that is still loading at spawn time is not a competitor even though it enrolled, which is a separate and older question); whether a spectator's "nothing" reads as intentional or as a bug — they are on no lane, no board and no picker panel, and there is no UI line telling them they are watching, which is the obvious next round if it confuses; and whether the ~2.5 s wipe inside the last 5 s means a player joining under the wash is *always* inside the cutoff and *never* enrolled, which is the intent but is worth stating plainly.

## 160. Every panel is the desktop composition at a smaller multiplier — one `UIScale`, no breakpoints

**Reported twice, and the second report is the correction to the first: "Keep the desktop composition and proportions on mobile — don't rearrange it into a different layout."** Two earlier attempts this round failed for the same reason in two different ways. The first made the bands `AutomaticSize` over children whose height was `1, 0` scale — circular, so the engine collapsed the header to zero and the store's title row vanished. The second narrowed the sheet to the viewport width and kept a width breakpoint, which flipped the two chest sections to a vertical column on a phone: a *different composition*, taller than the screen, overflowing. Both were reflow. Neither was what was asked for.

**The answer is one uniform multiplier.** `shared/ui/ui-scale.ts` adds `panelScaleFor(viewport, design)`:

```
scale = clamp( min( viewport.X × 0.92 / design.X, viewport.Y × 0.90 / design.Y ), 0.45, 1 )
```

One number multiplies width, height, gaps, corners, strokes and type together, so every proportion survives. The **smaller axis wins** because a landscape phone is wide and short and a portrait one is narrow and tall; fitting by width alone drops a landscape panel's bottom off the screen, which is exactly the "buttons are cut off" report. It never exceeds `1`, so a desktop renders byte-identically (verified: 1920×1080 → `1`, 2560×1440 → `1`).

**The design size is read from the panel itself, so one function serves six panels.** `UIScale` multiplies rendering and does **not** touch `Size`, so `root.Size`'s offsets are the design size at all times — including an auto-height sheet, where `AutomaticSize.Y` writes the resolved content height back into `Size.Y.Offset`. `applyPanelScale(root, name)` therefore needs no per-panel constant table: the store's 880 × 466, the picker's 640 × n, the payout's 360 × 300 and a 240 × 52 toast all describe themselves. A `Size` subscription catches the auto-height case arriving a frame late, and a zero reports "not saying" rather than "infinitely small" so nothing collapses on the first frame.

**`capToViewport` is replaced, not joined, and the reason is mechanical.** It installs a `UISizeConstraint`, which clamps *layout* size per axis: given an 880-wide sheet and a 390-wide viewport it sets the width to 358 and leaves the height alone — squashing the composition and re-flowing every band inside it, which is precisely the distortion the uniform scale exists to avoid. `UIScale` is applied after layout, so the geometry is untouched. Both answer "make it fit" and only one of them can be in a panel. The store, inventory, picker, payout and toast all swap `capToViewport(...)` for `applyPanelScale(...)`; the leaderboard gains a scale where it had neither.

**Every width breakpoint is gone.** `STORE_NARROW_WIDTH` is deleted (its comment survives as the record of why), `applyChestRowLayout` and `applyInventoryLayout` no longer take a width and no longer branch, and the dead `viewportWidth()` helper went with them. Also deleted: `INVENTORY_STACKED_SPLIT` and `INVENTORY_STACKED_GROWTH`, which only the stacked branch read. A panel that scales has no reason to branch on width — the sheet's own width never changes, only the multiplier applied to it — and that is the structural statement of "don't rearrange it".

**A fixed pixel width does not overflow a small screen when nothing clamps it.** The sheet stays `UDim2.fromOffset(880, 0)`; drawn at `0.75` it is 660 pixels, which fits a 844 × 390 viewport comfortably. It only ever overflowed because something *also* clamped its layout box. This is what "avoid fixed pixel widths that overflow" is actually asking for, and it is worth stating plainly because the intuitive reading — replace the width with a fraction — is the change that broke it twice.

**The legibility floor is an explicit trade, not an oversight.** `MIN_PANEL_SCALE = 0.45`: below it the arithmetic is ignored and the panel is drawn **wider than the screen** — visible, clipped, reportable — rather than shrunk until its 12-point captions resolve to four points, which is on screen and unreadable. That is the brief's "if something hits a practical minimum, constrain that element rather than breaking the overall layout", with the floor as the constraint. In practice it only binds on a **portrait** phone; this game is played in landscape.

**The shadow fix is re-applied (the standing correction from the last round).** `buildChunkyPanel`'s plate was `fromScale(1, 1)` — the same circular trap — and matched the *frame*, which is 6 pixels smaller than the *visible* face because `ApplyStrokeMode.Border` draws the 6-pixel outline half-outside. It is now sized from the face and grown by the stroke, positioned at `depth − stroke/2`, so the two boxes are identical and only the position differs. Verified arithmetically: face `[-3,-3] → [883,359]` (886 × 362) and plate `[7,7] → [893,369]` (**886 × 362**), a 10-pixel strip on the right and bottom and nothing on the top or left.

**Log line.** `[UiScale] panel=<store|inventory|picker|payout|reward-toast|leaderboard> design=<w>x<h> viewport=<w>x<h> scale=<n>`, printed on a change only.

**Audit.** Added: `src/shared/ui/ui-scale.ts`, `src/shared/ui/ui-scale.spec.ts`. Changed: `src/client/controllers/shop-controller.ts` (scale on both sheets, breakpoints and four now-dead constants deleted, `viewportWidth` removed, `capToViewport` import replaced), `picker-controller.ts`, `payout-controller.ts`, `reward-toast-controller.ts`, `leaderboard-controller.ts` (one `applyPanelScale` each, import swapped), `src/shared/ui/chunky-panel.ts` (the plate), `UI_STYLE_GUIDE.md` (new §4.2 and §1.2b). Build exit 0, lint 0 problems, prettier clean, `\uXXXX` zero, `flamework.build` unchanged at **30 identifiers**. **`npm test` not run.** The scale arithmetic was verified by compiling `panelScaleFor` standalone and running every spec assertion under `node`: desktop `1`, 4K `1`, landscape 844 × 390 → `0.7532` (drawn 662.8 × 351.0, fits both axes, aspect preserved), portrait 390 × 844 → floor `0.45`, tiny → floor, zero viewport → `1`, zero design-Y → the width ratio. Untouched: the HUD (phase banner, countdown, elimination splash, transition wipe), the theme, `typographyOneStepUp`, `TYPOGRAPHY`, `SPACING`, `FONT`, `ScreenInsets`, every panel's internal layout, and every non-UI system.

**Note:** `capToViewport` in `viewport.ts` now has no callers. It is kept as the documented clamp-only tool and because the style guide's §4 refers to it; a later tidy could delete it, but removing a shared module is a separate decision from this round.

**Placeholders:** `MIN_PANEL_SCALE = 0.45` and the `MAX_FRACTION` `(0.92, 0.9)` in `src/shared/ui/ui-scale.ts`. No designed size was retuned — `STORE_MAX_WIDTH` 880, `SHEET_WIDTH` 640, `PANEL_WIDTH` 210/360 and `TOAST_WIDTH` 240 are all as they were.

**Studio-only:** whether `0.45` is the right floor on a real phone — it only binds in portrait, and the answer is a judgement about type at that size; whether a `UIScale` on an `AutomaticSize.Y` sheet interacts exactly as expected, since the automatic height resolves unscaled and the render is scaled (it should compose, and it is the sort of engine detail this tree has been wrong about before); whether the store's `Size` subscription sees the final auto-height on the very first frame or a frame later, which would show one frame at the wrong scale; and whether the leaderboard's `AnchorPoint = (1, 0)` stays pinned to the top-right under a `UIScale` — it should, because the anchor resolves against the parent before the transform, but it is worth one screenshot.

## 161. The sheets draw above the splash layer, and an open panel takes the movement thumbstick away

**Two reports, both about a panel being open rather than about how it is drawn.** First: *"the STORE and INVENTORY should be the 2nd highest GUI priority, only beaten by the transition GUI."* Second: *"force the panels to ignore the movement joystick — I keep moving while in the panels by mistake when I touch the left side."*

**A sixth layer, at `38`.** The store and the inventory were tenants of `hudCore` (20), which put them **below** the splash layer (35) — so a reward toast, a payout panel or the countdown could paint over an open store. They now name a `sheet` layer:

| layer | order | tenants | contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fullScreen` | 10 | scenery | `None` |
| `hudCore` | 20 | leaderboard, **the picker** | `CoreUISafeInsets` |
| `hudTopbar` | 30 | phase banner | `TopbarSafeInsets` |
| `splash` | 35 | payout, countdown, elimination splash | `CoreUISafeInsets` |
| **`sheet`** | **38** | **store, inventory, rail** | `CoreUISafeInsets` |
| `toast` | **39** | **the reward toast** | `CoreUISafeInsets` |
| `transition` | 40 | the round wipe | `None` |

`38` is the only number that satisfies both halves: above `SPLASH_DISPLAY_ORDER` so nothing in the splash layer can cover a sheet, and below `TRANSITION_DISPLAY_ORDER` because the wipe's whole job is to be able to cover everything — a sheet that outlived a wipe would be a panel floating on a black screen. It keeps `CoreUISafeInsets` rather than `None`, because a sheet is centred in its gui and the insets decide where "the middle of the screen" is; `None` would put its top edge under the Roblox topbar on a phone, and it would also disagree with the picker's gui about the coordinate space.

**Why a new layer rather than renumbering `hudCore`.** `hudCore` also holds the leaderboard and the picker, which are HUD — read *alongside* gameplay — and they must not climb over the splash layer's toasts. Raising the whole layer would have moved both for the sake of two panels.

**The rail moved with the sheets.** A rail left at 20 with its panels at 38 is the classic "my tab is behind my panel" bug: the tabs draw under the sheet that covers them. `shop-controller`'s two `getScreenGui` calls are both `sheet` now, and `onStart` builds the rail there too.

**The toast moved to its own layer at `39`, above the sheets, and that is a deliberate divergence from the layering minimum.** Leaving it on `splash` (35) would have put an open store *over* a reward that arrived while the player was shopping — and item 133's standing rule is that a toast may never be silently dropped. A toast behind a panel is the same as one that was never shown. Only the toast moved: `payout`, the countdown and the elimination splash stay on `splash`.

**Movement: two mechanisms, and the first Studio run proved the second one cannot be trusted alone.** The prompt asked for `ScreenGui.Modal`. **That property does not exist on `ScreenGui` in this tree's typings**: `ScreenGui` declares `ClipToDeviceSafeArea`, `DisplayOrder`, `IgnoreGuiInset`, `SafeAreaCompatibility` and `ScreenInsets`, and nothing else. `Modal` *is* declared on **`GuiButton`** (`None.d.ts:21905`), where it means *"the mouse will not be locked unless the right mouse button is down"* — a cursor-lock rule, not an input capture.

The obvious substitute — an invisible full-screen `TextButton` swallowing every touch — was implemented first and then rejected on the evidence, because it **stops the click and not the character**. The dynamic thumbstick is drawn and driven by the `PlayerModule`'s touch controls, which read touches from `UserInputService` rather than from GUI hit-testing, so a blocker under the finger eats the click and the stick still walks the character. That is exactly the reported symptom, and a blocker would have looked like a fix in the code while changing nothing on the device. **A no-op is the worst possible outcome for a fix whose entire job is input.**

**The mechanism that shipped and works is `GuiService.TouchControlsEnabled = false`**, whose own documentation is the argument: *"Used to enable and disable touch controls and touch control display UI."* It is a plain `GuiService` property — no module lookup, no wait, no `pcall` — so the reported symptom is fixed by a line that cannot silently do nothing. `UserInputService.ModalEnabled` is *not* used: it is deprecated in these typings in favour of exactly this property.

**`PlayerModule:GetControls():Disable()` is kept as a best-effort second**, because it is the documented way to take movement away across gamepad and keyboard as well as touch — and the first Studio run showed why it must not be the only one:

```
18:04:37.584  [Shop] modal=true open=shop phase=Intermission
18:04:40.199  [Controls] no PlayerModule — panels will not lock movement
```

Two bugs in that one snapshot. **The module was not resolvable**, and a permanent `unavailable` flag turned "not yet" into "never" for the session. And **`WaitForChild` ran inline**, so opening the shop blocked the client for 2.6 seconds — visible in the log as `modal=true` printing *after* the wait it was supposed to precede. So the resolution moved to `task.spawn`, the "unavailable" latch became a retry-on-next-panel with a once-per-session warning, and the warning now prints **what `PlayerScripts` actually contained** so a nesting or naming difference is one log line away instead of a guess.

**`src/client/controls-lock.ts`** wraps both in a counted, idempotent lock. **Counted** because two panels can want it at once (a phase change closes the shop as the picker opens) and whichever released last would otherwise re-enable movement underneath the other. **Idempotent** because a double release — a destroyed panel, a phase change firing twice — would drive the count negative and leave the character frozen for the session. `touchControlsWere` captures the previous value rather than assuming `true`, so a game that ships with touch controls off does not have them switched *on* the first time a panel closes. `disabled` records that this module actually called `Disable()`, so a deferred disable that lands after its release cannot leave the character stuck. Every platform call is `pcall`ed: **"the character still walks" is a far better failure than "the store will not open"**.

**The shop holds one release for as long as either sheet is open.** `applyModal` is the only place in the controller that takes or gives it, and `setOpen` plus `applyPhase` are its two callers.

**`applyModal` runs before `applyPhase`'s early return, and that ordering is the whole decision.** Item 50's rule is unchanged: a panel left open when the phase changes **stays open** and is only closed on *entry* to the next `Intermission`, never on exit from this one. If the lock followed visibility alone, a store left open into `Playing` would freeze the character for the whole race — the panel over the belt *and* the joystick dead, with nothing in any log to say why. So the lock follows **visibility and phase**: `open !== "none" && phase === "Intermission"`. The panel stays visible across the phase change (item 50 intact) but gives movement back. The cost, stated rather than hidden: **a panel covering the belt is something the player can still drive under.** Closing it with the `X` restores both.

**The wipe was verified, not assumed.** `round-transition-controller` builds a `TransitionGrid` container per play and calls `Fusion.doCleanup(scope)` plus `container.Destroy()` when the play ends, so the `transition` layer has **no children between wipes** and captures nothing. The brief's worry — a visible wipe at 40 eating the joystick so a lock at 38 would not help — does not apply.

**The picker is untouched**: still on `hudCore` (20), same gui, same behaviour. Adding it to the lock is a follow-up rather than this round, because the brief excludes it and its own `Visible` is driven from three places.

**Log line.** `[Shop] modal=<true|false> open=<shop|inventory|none> phase=<...>`, one per *toggle* — "why is the joystick not working" answered in one read. The layer's own `[Ui] created kind=sheet … displayOrder=38` comes from item 39's existing line and is not duplicated.

**Audit.** Added: `src/client/controls-lock.ts`. Changed: `src/shared/ui/layers.ts` (`SHEET_GUI_NAME`/`SHEET_DISPLAY_ORDER` 38, `TOAST_GUI_NAME`/`TOAST_DISPLAY_ORDER` 39, `sheetGui()`/`toastGui()`, `UiLayer` widened to seven, two `getScreenGui` branches), `src/client/controllers/shop-controller.ts` (both `getScreenGui` calls to `sheet`, `controlsRelease` field, `applyModal` called from `setOpen` and from `applyPhase`, the release also wired to each panel's `Destroying`), `src/client/controllers/reward-toast-controller.ts` (one `getScreenGui`), `UI_STYLE_GUIDE.md` (new §4.3: the layer table, the catcher rule and the phase rule). Build exit 0, lint 0 problems, prettier clean, `\uXXXX` zero, `flamework.build` unchanged at **30 identifiers** — no controller or service. **`npm test` not run.** Untouched: the picker, the phase banner, the elimination splash, the payout panel, the countdown, `splash` (35), `transition` (40), item 50's phase-rule docblock, the scale round (`ui-scale.ts`, `chunky-panel.ts`, `capToViewport`), and every non-UI system.

One lint suppression was needed: `@typescript-eslint/no-require-imports` on the single `require(moduleScript)`, with the reason inline. `PlayerModule` is a runtime `ModuleScript` inside the player, not a build-time import, and requiring the instance is the only way to reach `GetControls()`.

**Placeholders:** `SHEET_DISPLAY_ORDER = 38`, `TOAST_DISPLAY_ORDER = 39`, `SHEET_GUI_NAME`, `TOAST_GUI_NAME` in `layers.ts`. Nothing else invented.

**Studio-only:** whether hiding the touch controls is enough on its own — the `GuiService.TouchControlsEnabled` line is synchronous and cannot silently fail, so the *stick disappearing* is the visible confirmation and the character not walking follows from it; whether `GetControls():Disable()` also stops the *mobile jump button* when the module does resolve (it should, since that is the same module); whether a character mid-stride when a panel opens stops cleanly or slides a little; whether the toast at 39 over an open sheet is where the player expects it, since it anchors at `TOP_SCALE` (12%) of a `CoreUISafeInsets` gui and the sheet is centred; and **what `PlayerScripts` actually contains on this machine** — the new failure line prints it, which is what the first run could not answer.

## 163. A chest opening flips cards over instead of printing a receipt — coin chest only, because the premium reply carries no payload

**The brief's blocker was real, and worse than it guessed.** `EconomyService.notifyGranted` is the whole `PurchaseGranted` payload:

```
remote.FireClient(player);   // src/server/services/economy-service.ts:872
```

**No arguments at all** — not `{ ok, ballId }`, not `{ ok, ballIds }`, not `{ ok, amount }`. So the client cannot know what a Premium chest granted, and the premium reveal is **not built**. The follow-up is a named server change, and it is three edits rather than the one line the brief expected, because `applyRobuxChestGrant` returns only a `GrantOutcome` string and discards the ball it rolled:

1. `applyRobuxChestGrant` returns the granted id alongside its outcome (the bundle's `applyRobuxChestBundleGrant` already returns `{ outcome, granted, floored }` — the single has no equivalent).
2. `notifyGranted(player)` becomes `notifyGranted(player, ballIds: Array<string>)` and sends `{ ok: true, ballIds }`; the single passes one id, the bundle passes its ten.
3. `shop-controller`'s `purchaseGranted.OnClientEvent` (currently `() => playPurchaseSound()`) reads the payload and calls the same `reveal.show`.

Until then the coin chest is the whole feature, and that is deliberate: a reveal with nothing to reveal is a worse answer than a receipt.

**The coin reply's shape was also not what the brief said.** There is one shape for both counts, `ChestResult` (`shop-controller.ts:366`): `{ ok: true; balls: Array<string>; coins: number } | { ok: false; reason: string }`. **`balls`, always an array** — no `ballId` for `count = 1` and no `ballIds` anywhere. `openCoinChest` answers `{ ok: true, balls: [ballId], coins }` and `openChestsBulk` answers the same field with up to ten. One shape is what makes the reveal a single sequence: a one-ball reply is a one-cell grid, not a second code path.

**The animation is three beats and one mechanism.** Every card starts at the grid's centre scaled to nothing, flies to its cell (`Back`/`Out`, so it overshoots and settles), the grid holds facedown for a beat with each card wearing its own rarity ring — the colour-coded aura — and then the cards turn over in order and print `[Reveal] flip card=<n> id=<id> rarity=<r>`. **Nothing is rolled, shuffled, priced or weighted here**: the reply is the truth and the overlay is a presentation of it, which is why `[Reveal] open … ids=…` prints every id before the first card moves. A "was it the wrong item" report is two lines of the same session.

**`Size.X` collapses and the face swaps at zero; `Rotation` is never used.** `GuiObject`'s `Rotation` is a 2D spin — the card turns like a page on a table and the far edge shows the same face mirrored — and a `Frame` has no `CFrame`. The flip is therefore width to `0`, hide the back and show the front, width back. `UIScale` cannot do it (it scales both axes together), which is also why the **drop** uses a `UIScale` and the **flip** uses `Size`: one owner per property, and neither tween has to start from what the other left behind.

**The layer chain needed four integers for three constraints, so the sheet moved down one.** Reveal above the sheet, toast above the reveal (item 133), wipe above everything (item 49) — with `sheet 38`, `toast 39`, `transition 40` fixed there is no gap left, and two `ScreenGui`s at one `DisplayOrder` are ordered by sibling position in `PlayerGui`, which is not a correctness property. The reveal took **38**, the sheet stepped down to **37**, and `toast 39` and `transition 40` are exactly as item 160 and item 49 set them. Pushing the toast up instead would have put it *above the wipe*, where a reward message floats on the black of a phase transition.

**There is no `ScreenGui.Modal`, so "modal" is the counted movement lock.** Item 161 already found `Modal` on `GuiButton` (a cursor-lock rule), and `controls-lock.ts` is counted — so the reveal takes its own `lockControls()` hold and the store is left completely alone: no release, no re-take, no ordering question. A replace (`Open Again` landing) keeps the hold across the rebuild, because releasing and immediately re-taking it would blink the touch controls on for one frame.

**`Open Again` re-fires the same `Open N` through the shop, not through a remote of its own.** It needed one new thing on the shop: `fireChest(count, fromReveal = false)`. The reveal is *still open* when its own footer is pressed, so the "one overlay at a time" refusal would have eaten the re-fire — the bug this round found in its own first draft. `fromReveal` is the only decision that parameter changes; the same remote, the same `busy` guard, the same balance check and the same server re-validation all still run. A refused re-fire leaves the reveal up and re-dims the footer from the coin attribute, and a disabled `Open Again` is `Active = false`, so no press plays a sound or logs anything.

**The lobby gate is a button-level refusal because the client cannot read an intermission deadline.** The server publishes `PlayingDeadline` for the countdown (item 149) and **nothing for `Intermission`**, so the shop times the lobby from the moment it *saw* the phase change and compares against `INTERMISSION_SECONDS`. `REVEAL_MIN_REMAINING_SECONDS = 6` against a ten-card sequence of about 2.3 s: the refusal prints `[Reveal] refused reason=intermission-remaining left=…` and writes a status line, and it is deliberately permissive when the client cannot tell (a join mid-lobby over-estimates the remaining time). The real guarantee is the clean close: `applyPhase` calls `closeForPhase`, which destroys the frame, releases the hold and logs `reason=phase`, so the wipe at 40 always arrives on a screen with no reveal on it.

**Two of the brief's premises were wrong and are worth recording.** First, the store's `Modal` does **not** capture input — it is a `GuiService.TouchControlsEnabled` write — so "the reveal's `OK` would not receive touches while the store's `Modal` is true" cannot happen; nothing needed releasing. Second, `applyPanelScale`'s per-card fit and the chrome's two faces are compatible with the flip: the chrome's face and ring are *children*, so a parent `Size.X` of zero squashes them to nothing rather than hiding them — which is exactly the visual a flip wants, and worth knowing before someone "fixes" it by hiding the face early.

**A 0.5 black dim does not block presses underneath it.** A `Frame` with `Active = false` passes touches through, so a covered `Open 1` is still clickable through the overlay — which is precisely why the `[Reveal] refused reason=busy` gate exists and why it is not just belt-and-braces.

## 164. The reveal grid holds at its top centre — a `UIScale` shrinks about the anchor, not about the middle

**The first Studio run showed a correct `5 x 2` grid in the top-left corner**, half off the screen. The arrangement was right and the position was wrong, which is the signature of a scaling bug rather than a layout bug.

**`UIScale` multiplies `AbsoluteSize`, and `AbsolutePosition` is then derived from `AnchorPoint` against that scaled size.** The reveal's grid host was a full-screen frame at `Position (0, 0)` with `AnchorPoint (0, 0)`, and the cards positioned at `0.5` of it. At scale 1 that is the centre of the screen. At scale 0.82 the host's box collapses toward its nailed-down top-left corner, so `0.5` of the box is no longer `0.5` of the screen — every card moved up and left by `(1 - scale) / 2` of the overlay, about 90 px on the machine that reported it.

**Two changes, and the second is the one that reads as "top middle":**

- **The host's `Size` is now the grid's own extent**, not the screen's. A host the size of the screen makes `0.5` mean "floor of the arrangement in the middle of the screen"; sized to the grid, `0.5` *is* the grid's centre.
- **`AnchorPoint` is `(0.5, 0)`** — horizontally centred, top edge fixed — so the shrink happens inward from both sides and the composition holds at the top of the screen. `Position` is `UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 0, GRID_TOP_INSET)`.

**`GRID_TOP_INSET = 72`** is a new `Placeholder.`: the reveal layer is `ScreenInsets.None`, so its gui starts at the physical top and the Roblox topbar is drawn over it. `72` clears the desktop topbar (`36`) and the taller phone one, with a margin. The grid is top-aligned against that value rather than centred in the leftover space, so it is the top edge of the first row, not an inset to be halved.

**The fit scale is now measured against the band between the two reserved strips** — `viewport.Y - GRID_TOP_INSET - FOOTER_BAND` — rather than against the whole viewport. "The cards, the topbar and the footer" is what has to fit, so ten cards on a phone shrink because the buttons are below them rather than in spite of it.

**Why `UIScale` and not pre-scaled pixel sizes.** The tempting fix — compute `CARD_WIDTH * scale` and never use a `UIScale` — scales the card and leaves the type at 24 px, which on a 0.47 portrait scale is a 24-px label in a 94-px card. A `UIScale` multiplies type and stroke with the geometry, which is the entire reason item 160 chose it for the panels. The anchor, not the mechanism, was wrong.

**The panels never had this bug** because every one of them is anchored at `(0.5, 0.5)`. It is the *new* scaled composition that had to answer the question, and the guide now asks it explicitly in §4.2.

**Audit.** Changed: `src/client/controllers/reveal-controller.ts` (`buildGrid` — host size, anchor, position, the `available` band, and the docblock recording the failure; new `GRID_TOP_INSET`), `UI_STYLE_GUIDE.md` (§4.2 gains "a scaled frame shrinks about its `AnchorPoint`" with the anchor table and the two rules). Build exit 0, lint 0 errors, prettier clean, `\uXXXX` zero, `flamework.build` unchanged at **31 identifiers** — no new controller. **`npm test` not run.** Untouched: the card, the sequence, the footer, the layer numbers, the shop's wiring and every number item 163 recorded.

**Studio-only:** whether `72` clears the topbar on the reporter's phone as well as their desktop; whether the ten-card grid now reads as "top middle" or as "too high", since a landscape screen with a width-limited grid leaves the lower third empty by design.

## 165. The finished reveal throws one burst of 2D confetti — the 2018 module ported, with its three bugs recorded where they lived

**The 2018 Confetti Cannon could not work and could not live here.** Its logic was in a `ModuleScript` that no wrapper ever called `:Update` on, so it drew a still frame; its palette was a module-level variable every `createParticle` overwrote, so a burst was monochrome; and its `paramColors == nil` default was applied one line *after* the index that needed it, so a `nil` palette errored on `nil`. A `LocalScript` in this tree is a Rojo/roblox-ts contract violation anyway (item 84), so the logic moved to `src/shared/ui/confetti.ts` as pure functions and the drawing moved to `client/controllers/confetti-controller.ts` as a `@Controller()` clone-pose-destroy controller — the same shape as `hitEffect`, `windBoost`, `tailWind` and `motionBlur`, in 2D.

**The three bugs are now comments, not code.** `createParticle` takes the palette on its state object and bakes the colour into a `readonly` field, so a later burst cannot reach back into an earlier one (bug 1). `colours` is a **required parameter** of `spawnBurst`, so there is no `nil` path to default late (bug 2). `stepParticle` is pure and `outOfBounds` is one predicate, while the `RenderStepped` loop that calls them lives in the controller — the piece the module was missing (bug 3).

**One burst, at the end, and the completion point did not exist until this round.** The brief assumed the flip sequence already had somewhere to hook. It did not: `flip` played the expand tween and never observed it. So `flip` now holds the expanding tween and, only when `index === cards.size() - 1`, connects to its `Completed` and calls `celebrate()`. **The expand rather than the swap**, because the swap happens at zero width and a burst fired there would open behind a card still turning. The `generation` guard is the race the brief asked about: `close` bumps it, so `OK` between the swap and the expand finishing cannot fire into a destroyed frame.

**`chunky-chrome.ts` exports no `ZIndex` — there is no constant to read.** The brief's "read the value from `chunky-chrome.ts`" describes something that does not exist: the module takes `zIndex` as an *option* and derives the face at `zIndex + 1` and the ring at `face + 1`. On these cards the chrome is called with `3`, so the face is `4`, the ring and art are `5`, the ball `6`, and the name and tier `7`. Rather than hard-code `8`, the reveal records the maximum as it builds (`cardTopZIndex`) and passes `+ 1`. The module's own `20` would have landed *inside* that stack and drawn the confetti behind the cards it was celebrating. The number this round actually used is **8**.

**`ZIndexBehavior` is never set in this tree**, so every gui is on the default `Sibling`, where a child's `ZIndex` competes only with its siblings and a subtree is drawn as one unit. That means the burst — a direct child of the overlay frame at `8` — already outranks the whole grid host at `2` regardless of the cards inside it; the `8` is belt and braces and, unlike the `Sibling` fallback, also correct under `Global`.

**The parenting is the teardown.** The burst goes into the reveal's own overlay frame (`dim`), never into the `ScreenGui`, so `close` destroying `dim` takes every clone with it on all four paths — `ok`, `open-again`, `phase`, `teardown`. The confetti controller also hooks `parent.Destroying` so its particle list is dropped in the same instant rather than a frame later, and each particle additionally has a hard `DEFAULT_LIFETIME_SECONDS` backstop so a cull that misses cannot leave a `PlayerGui` full of labels.

**`PreloadAsync` is logged and ignored.** Item 158 established that its verdict is not evidence in this place — it reports `Asset type does not match requested type` for images and audio that render perfectly — so a burst disabled by it would be disabled for no reason. The check that actually separates a broken asset from broken code is a synchronous property read: an empty `Image` on either template warns by name (`[Confetti] … has no Image set — the confetti will animate and draw nothing`), because that is a clone that moves correctly and draws nothing.

**Reserved identifiers bit twice.** roblox-ts's `isReservedIdentifier` is `hasOwnProperty` on luau-ast's 27 globals — `_G TS assert bit32 coroutine error exports getmetatable ipairs next pairs pcall require script select self setmetatable string super table utf8 math tostring type typeof unpack game`. **`const next = stepParticle(...)` is that list**, and the diagnostic points at a *comment* two lines above because the class transform shifts the reported position. It is now `moved`. (`template` was renamed to `source` and then to `shape` on the way there; it is not reserved — that rename was precautionary.)

**Audit.** Added: `src/shared/ui/confetti.ts` (the pure port, `DEFAULT_CONFETTI_COLORS`, `DEFAULT_GRAVITY`, `spawnBurst`/`createParticle`/`stepParticle`/`outOfBounds`), `src/shared/ui/confetti.spec.ts` (12 assertions), `src/client/controllers/confetti-controller.ts`. Changed: `src/client/controllers/reveal-controller.ts` (import, `grid`/`cardTopZIndex` fields, `BURST_COUNT`, the `outOfBounds`-free `celebrate`, the last flip's `Completed` hook, `this.grid = host`, `close` clearing both fields, `show` resetting `cardTopZIndex`). Build exit 0, lint 0 errors, prettier clean on every touched file (`viewport.ts` still fails at `HEAD`), `\uXXXX` zero, `ConfettiCannon` zero in `src`, `flamework.build` regenerated from scratch at **32 identifiers** with `ConfettiController` present. **`npm test` not run** — the spec is written and type-checked but not executed; its arithmetic was verified by mirroring the formulas in Node (10 particles all at the emitter, 3 distinct colours in one burst, both velocity signs present, burst empty in 24 of the 600 allowed steps). Untouched: the reveal's drop/tease/flip durations, its grid, footer, layers and the shop's wiring, the theme, the chunky builders, the store, the picker, the economy and the phase machine.

**Placeholders:** `BURST_COUNT = 24` (reveal-controller), `CONFETTI_ROOT_NAME = "confetti"`, `GRAVITY_PER_SECOND = 1200`, `DEFAULT_LIFETIME_SECONDS = 2.2`, `EMITTER_JITTER = 6`, `BURST_FORCE = (0, -180)` (confetti-controller), `MAX_PARTICLE_SIZE = 18`, `MIN_PARTICLE_SIZE = 9`, `SPREAD_SPEED = 220`, `CULL_MARGIN = 40` (confetti).

**Studio-only, and one action this repo cannot take:** the 2018 `ModuleScript`, its `LocalScript` and the `ScreenGui > Frame` wrapper have to be **deleted in Studio** — nothing in the repository can reach them, and leaving them means two systems with the same name. Also unverified: whether `ReplicatedStorage/assets/ui/confetti` exists at all (the boot warns and disables if not — `default.project.json` maps only `rbxts_include` and `TS` into `ReplicatedStorage`, so this folder is place-authored, not repo-authored); whether the two `Image` ids resolve; whether `Rotation` at up to 360° reads as confetti or as scattered cards; whether one 24-particle burst reads as a celebration or a puff; whether the module's five colours sit acceptably beside the chunky charcoal cards; and whether the burst has finished by the time a player presses `OK` on a slow click, or is still falling behind the footer.

## 166. The confetti resolved to its own compiled module, then found no assets — so it now draws from shapes when there is nothing to clone

**The first run drew nothing, and the log said why in one line:**

```
19:04:00.539  [Confetti] found ReplicatedStorage.TS.ui.confetti but not both templates — circular=false square=false
```

**That is this round's own module.** `src/shared/ui/confetti.ts` compiles to `ReplicatedStorage.TS.ui.confetti`, so a recursive name search for `"confetti"` is **permanently ambiguous in this tree** — the code folder contains a `ModuleScript` with exactly the name the asset folder wants. The search stopped at the first match, which was the module, which has no children, which means "found the folder but it holds nothing". The `assets.vfx.*` controllers (`hitEffect`, `windBoost`, `tailWind`, `motionBlur`) do not have this problem because their names do not collide with a module name; this one does.

**Three faults, and the first one was hiding the other two.**

1. **The name match was not a folder.** Strategy one now requires an `Instance` named `confetti` that is a `Folder` **and holds both templates as `ImageLabel`s** — a test a compiled module cannot pass. The canonical `ReplicatedStorage.assets.ui.confetti` is probed by walking the path and wins when several folders qualify.
2. **Nothing to clone existed anyway.** The place has `ReplicatedStorage.assets.vfx.{hitEffect,windBoost,tailWind,motionBlur}` and no confetti pair, so even a correct lookup would have found an empty folder. Strategy two accepts both names loose anywhere under `ReplicatedStorage`, which is how an author who drops them in `assets/vfx` and calls the folder something else still gets confetti.
3. **The controller disabled itself and said nothing at burst time.** A reveal that finished, no burst, and no line in between is the report this round came back with. `burst()` no longer has a silent path: it always prints `[Confetti] burst …` or the reason it cannot, and `celebrate()` prints `[Reveal] celebrate skipped dim=… grid=… confetti=…` when **it** is the one that bailed.

**The burst now draws with no assets at all.** A `Frame` with a `UICorner` is a confetto: `UDim(1, 0)` for the circular half (a dot, whose rotation is invisible — colour and size carry the variety) and `UDim(0, 2)` for the square half (a rounded rectangle, whose rotation *is* the confetti motion). The Studio templates are still preferred when they resolve, and the boot line says which renderer is live (`mounted folder=…` versus `no templates found — drawing … from plain 2D shapes`). **This place makes an image-based burst the least reliable thing to depend on**: the same log reports `[Coin] icon did not load … status=Enum.AssetFetchStatus.Failure` and `[PickupSprite] image did not load … status=Enum.AssetFetchStatus.Failure`, so two decals already fail to fetch here. A design that only draws with hand-authored assets draws nothing until somebody opens Studio, and this round shipped exactly that.

**`Image` checks gained the placeholder case.** `reportImage` now also warns on `rbxassetid://123456789` / `…788` — the two ids the store's rail tabs carry — because a template with a placeholder fetches "successfully" and draws a grey box, which reads as a confetti bug rather than as an unfinished asset.

**Audit.** Changed: `src/client/controllers/confetti-controller.ts` (`resolveTemplates` with three strategies and a candidate listing, `canonicalFolder`/`holdsBoth`/`containsTemplate`/`findAnywhere`, `buildParticle` with the clone-or-shape branch, `LiveParticle.label` widened to `GuiObject`, the `disabled` field removed, `reportImage`'s placeholder check), `src/client/controllers/reveal-controller.ts` (`celebrate`'s skip line). Build exit 0, lint 0 errors, prettier clean on every touched file, `\uXXXX` zero, `flamework.build` unchanged at **32 identifiers**. **`npm test` not run.** Untouched: the pure port and its spec, the reveal's sequence and durations, its grid, footer, layers, and the shop.

**Placeholders:** unchanged from item 165.

**Still a Studio task, and now optional:** authoring `ReplicatedStorage.assets.ui.confetti` with `CircularConfetti` and `SquareConfetti` `ImageLabel`s upgrades the burst from plain shapes to decals. It is no longer required for the effect to appear. Deleting the 2018 `ModuleScript`/`LocalScript`/`ScreenGui` wrapper is also still a Studio task.

## 167. The confetti drew 24 particles and nobody could see them — the template's size was being thrown away

**The second run resolved the assets and fired the burst, and still showed nothing:**

```
[Confetti] mounted folder=ReplicatedStorage.assets.ui.confetti circular=CircularConfetti square=SquareConfetti colours=5
[Confetti] burst parent=Players.prospeed1.PlayerGui.RevealGui.RevealOverlay count=24 position=530.4000244140625,202
[Confetti] burst done count=0 lifetime=1.16s
```

Every line in that sequence is a success line. The burst fired, 24 particles existed, they were parented into the right overlay, and the last one was culled after **1.16 s**. So the fault was not resolution, not the hook and not the parenting — it was that the particles were too small to see for too short a time, and **the cause of the size was a rule this round had already written down and then broken**: "nothing is left at the template's authored value except `Image` and the base `Size`".

**The port was overriding the authored size.** `buildParticle` wrote `Size = UDim2.fromOffset(9..18, 9..18)` on every clone, so an `ImageLabel` authored at 48 pixels rendered at a quarter of the size the author chose, for one second, at the exact centre of the card the player was looking at. On a 1060-pixel-wide screen that is a handful of specks behind a bright card.

**Three fixes, all of them measured rather than guessed:**

- **`Size` is now the template's own, varied by a multiplier.** `SIZE_SCALE_MIN`/`SIZE_SCALE_MAX` = `0.7`/`1.2` of the authored axis, read once at boot from `Size.X.Offset` (a template in `ReplicatedStorage` has no resolved `AbsoluteSize`). `baseAspect` keeps a non-square asset un-squashed. A 48-pixel template therefore draws at **34–58 px** instead of 9–18. The shape fallback gets `DEFAULT_PARTICLE_SIZE = 26` for the same reason.
- **Gravity `1200` → `700` and muzzle velocity `-180` → `-300`.** At `1200` the whole burst left the bottom edge in **1.16 s** — the number in the log — on a viewport about 520 px tall. The retune gives a mean life of **1.50 s** and a longest of **1.67 s** with the plume opening ~90 px above the emitter, which is the difference between "a puff nobody noticed" and a burst.
- **`Visible` and `ImageTransparency` are forced on every clone.** A template authored `Visible = false` (the normal way to park one) and an `ImageTransparency` above zero are the two properties that make a clone animate perfectly and draw nothing — both fail identically to broken code.

**One new line per burst, because the log could not answer the question it was being asked.** The previous run printed a burst, a count, a lifetime and no visible confetti — every fact except whether a clone had a non-zero rect and was in front of anything:

```
[Confetti] sample absolute=<x>,<y> size=<w>,<h> visible=<bool> zIndex=<n> transparency=<n> parent=<bool>
```

`task.defer` waits one resume so the layout has resolved `AbsoluteSize`. **If the next report still says "nothing", that line is the answer**: a `size` of 0 means the authored size is scale-based, `visible=false` means something is hiding them, and a `zIndex` below the cards means the draw order is wrong after all.

**Audit.** Changed: `src/shared/ui/confetti.ts` (`DEFAULT_PARTICLE_SIZE`, `SIZE_SCALE_MIN`/`SIZE_SCALE_MAX` replacing `MAX`/`MIN_PARTICLE_SIZE`, `BurstState.baseSize`, `spawnBurst`'s sixth parameter), `src/client/controllers/confetti-controller.ts` (`baseSize`/`baseAspect` read at boot, `buildParticle` size and the forced properties, `GRAVITY_PER_SECOND` 700, `BURST_FORCE` -300, the `sample` line, `baseSize` in the mounted line). Build exit 0, lint 0 errors, prettier clean on every touched file, `\uXXXX` zero, `flamework.build` unchanged at **32 identifiers**. **`npm test` not run** — the spec's calls pass five arguments and take the `DEFAULT_PARTICLE_SIZE` base, so no assertion changed; the retuned trajectory was checked with a mirror of the formulas in Node (mean 1.50 s, longest 1.67 s, plume apex ~90 px above the emitter).

**Placeholders:** `DEFAULT_PARTICLE_SIZE = 26`, `SIZE_SCALE_MIN = 0.7`, `SIZE_SCALE_MAX = 1.2`, `GRAVITY_PER_SECOND = 700`, `BURST_FORCE = (0, -300)`, `SPREAD_SPEED = 220`, `CULL_MARGIN = 40`, `DEFAULT_LIFETIME_SECONDS = 2.2`, `EMITTER_JITTER = 6`, `BURST_COUNT = 24`.

**Studio-only:** whether the authored `CircularConfetti`/`SquareConfetti` have offset sizes (the `sample` line reports the drawn size, which settles it); whether a burst at the card's centre reads as a celebration or as debris over the item; and whether 1.5 s is long enough to register on a phone, since the lifetime cap was never the limiter — the cull was.

## 168. The confetti is the 2024 module: `Frame` pieces, six colours, three shapes, continuous spin — and no asset to delete

**The previous port was ported from the wrong module.** Items 165 and 167 were two rounds of diagnosis on a port of a 2018 `ModuleScript` that drew `ImageLabel`s resolved by name out of `ReplicatedStorage`: first the name search matched this tree's own compiled module (`ReplicatedStorage.TS.ui.confetti`), then the resolved templates were drawn at a quarter of their authored size and the whole burst was gone in 1.16 s. **Neither fault exists in the module the user actually meant**: it is `Frame`s created in code — no `Image`, no folder, no `PreloadAsync`, nothing for anybody to delete. Both rounds are superseded, and a reader looking for which confetti port is live should land here.

**What the old port got right, and this keeps**: the shape (pure rules in `shared/ui/confetti.ts`, plumbing in a `@Controller()`), one `RenderStepped` for the whole system rather than one per piece, a `ZIndex` derived from the caller's card stack rather than a literal, and the `[Confetti] sample` line — which is the only reason two failures were diagnosable at all.

**What this drops**: the asset resolution, the size override, the fixed 9–18 px pixels, and the gravity/force retune that was treating the symptom.

**The module's four problems and what the port does with each:**

1. **The `ScreenGui` name mismatch.** It looked for `ConfettiScreenGui` and created `ConfettiGui`, so the lookup never matched and **every `Emit` added another `ScreenGui` to `PlayerGui`**. The port creates **one overlay frame in `onStart`** and never inside `burst`, so two `Open Again` reveals reuse the same one.
2. **`repeat task.wait() until bonusSound.IsLoaded`.** An unbounded wait, in the emit path, before a single piece existed. **The sound is not ported at all** (the user dropped it), so the wait has nothing left to guard. `grep "rbxassetid://2789427964" src` is zero.
3. **The `UIGradient` covering the palette.** The module sets six `baseColors` and then parents a `UIGradient` with two **random** endpoint colours over every piece, so the six colours were never visible. **The gradient is not ported**; the six are the visible colour, with the module's own `0.95`–`1.05` brightness jitter kept for variety. This is the change a reader is most likely to "restore", and restoring it hides the palette again.
4. **`Triangle` never drew a triangle** — the branch only resized the piece and gave it the same `UICorner` as everything else. **The shape cycle is three**: `square`, `circle` (`UICorner` at `UDim(1, 0)`) and `diamond` (a square at `45` degrees, which the spin then carries around its own centre). A triangle on a `Frame` needs a gradient wedge or an image, and the user dropped the asset path in the same breath.

**The overlay is the controller's, not the reveal's frame.** One `Frame` named `ConfettiOverlay` in the `reveal` layer's `ScreenGui` (`getScreenGui("reveal")`, so no second gui for the same rank), created once in `onStart`, `Active = false` so it passes touches through to the reveal's `OK`. The previous port parented pieces into the reveal's own frame, which works but makes a burst's lifetime a property of a frame the reveal destroys on four different paths — so a piece could race a `Destroy()`. Out here there is no race, and a burst still falling when the player presses `OK` keeps falling, which is right: it was already drawn.

**The physics is the module's, including the part that is not physics.** `position.x += velocity.x * dt / 400`, `position.y += velocity.y * dt / 3000 + 0.5 * gravity * age² / 3000`, `rotation += rotationSpeed * dt + sin(age * 2) * 0.5`, destroyed at `y > 1.3`. The gravity term is a running sum of a growing quadratic rather than an integrated acceleration — it double-counts, and it is what the effect was tuned against, so it is reproduced rather than "fixed". `X_SCALE_DIVISOR` and `Y_SCALE_DIVISOR` are named separately because they are different numbers and nothing suggests they were meant to be one. Mirrored in Node: a piece from the grid centre lives **1.60–1.65 s** and crosses the screen in **0.68–1.47 s**, and — contrary to what the module's upward `velocityY` suggests — **none of them leave through the top**, because the accumulating quadratic turns them.

**The spin is the animation the previous port did not have.** The module randomises `rotationSpeed` (`-300..300` degrees per second) and never the spawn angle, so a piece starts square-on and turns, with `sin(age * 2) * 0.5` as a slow wobble on top — the wobble is why it does not look like a wheel on an axle, and it is the cheapest part of the effect to lose in a port.

**`BURST_COUNT` is 204, not the `24` the round's brief said.** The tree had 204 — raised while the effect was drawing nothing — and it is kept: 24–36 px `Frame`s need more of them than the decals did to read as a celebration. The comment beside it now says so instead of contradicting it.

**Audit.** Replaced: `src/shared/ui/confetti.ts` (pure — `ConfettiPiece`, `createPiece`, `spawnBurst`, `stepPiece`, `pieceGone`, `defaultSpawn`, the six colours and every module constant), `src/shared/ui/confetti.spec.ts` (12 assertions), `src/client/controllers/confetti-controller.ts` (`@Controller()`, one overlay, one `RenderStepped`, `buildPiece`, the `sample` line). Changed: `src/client/controllers/reveal-controller.ts` (only the `BURST_COUNT` docblock, which said 24 over a value of 204). Build exit 0, lint 0 errors, prettier clean on every touched file (`viewport.ts` still fails at `HEAD`), `\uXXXX` zero, `flamework.build` regenerated from scratch at **32 identifiers** with `ConfettiController`. **`npm test` not run** — the spec is written and type-checked; its arithmetic was mirrored in Node rather than executed. Untouched: the reveal's sequence, timings, grid, footer, layers and the shop's wiring (the call site is `confetti.burst(dim, centre, BURST_COUNT, cardTopZIndex + 1)` unchanged), the theme, the chunky builders, the store, the picker, the economy and the phase machine.

## 170. The confetti fires as the first card turns, and again at the first card of the second half — not at the end

**It used to fire from the last card's expand `Completed`** (item 165): every id shown, every card the right way up, then a burst. The effect was a reveal that finished and *then* threw confetti at the player — the epilogue of a moment rather than its flourish. The burst now rides each scheduled card's **flip start**, inside `flip`'s first line, before the closing tween is even created.

**The schedule is one array, and the log prints that array.**

```
[Reveal] confetti schedule cards=<n> at=<i1>[,<i2>]
```

`at=1` for one card, `at=1,6` for ten. It is built at open by `confettiCards(count)` and stored on `confettiAt`; `fireConfetti` fires only when the card number is in it, so the log and the bursts cannot drift — they are the same data, not a rule written twice.

**The index rule is `math.floor(count / 2) + 1`** — the *first card of the second half*. Ten gives `6`, and the two bursts then bracket two halves of five flips. `math.ceil(count / 2)` gives `5`, the last card of the first half, which starts the second burst before the first has finished reading. One card is one entry; two cards are `at=1,2`; five are `at=1,3`.

**The flip start is the staggered `task.delay`'s landing**, which is the only "a card has started" event the sequence has: there is no per-card signal to hook, so `flip` itself is the event and the confetti is its first statement. The `[Reveal] flip card=<n>` line stays where it was — at the swap, `FLIP_HALF_SECONDS` later — because the prompt froze that line; the pair is therefore one line apart in a quiet log but **not in the same frame**, which is worth knowing when reading a run.

**Two guards, and they answer different failures.** `confettiFired` is a per-reveal `Set<number>` of card numbers, so a second call for one index — a restart, a re-entered sequence — cannot throw a second burst. The **generation** check is the same one every deferred step uses, so a reveal closed between the stagger's delay and its flip fires nothing at all. `close` also empties `confettiAt`, so both orders of arrival are safe.

**`Open Again` gets a fresh schedule and an empty set**, because the rebuild goes through `show`, which is where both are reset. A set that survived would silence the first burst of the next open, and the symptom would be "the second open has no confetti at all" — the class of bug item 168's overlay work was already about.

**`position` is still passed and still unused for placement.** Item 169 made the confetti spawn full-screen, as the module does; the reveal's grid centre goes into the `[Confetti] burst … position=…` line so a report reads the reveal's centre rather than a zero. That is the only thing it is for, and it is said in the code.

**Audit.** Changed: `src/client/controllers/reveal-controller.ts` only — `confettiAt` and `confettiFired` fields, `confettiCards()`, `fireConfetti(cardNumber)` replacing `celebrate()`, the end-of-sequence `Completed` hook removed, one call at the top of `flip`, the schedule line at open, and the resets in `show` and `close`. **`BURST_COUNT` is unchanged at 80 and neither confetti file was touched.** Build exit 0, lint 0 errors, prettier clean on every touched file (`viewport.ts` still fails at `HEAD`), `\uXXXX` zero, `flamework.build` unchanged at **32 identifiers**. **`npm test` not run.** Untouched: the confetti's physics, spawn, shapes, overlay and `ZIndex`; the reveal's drop, tease, flip durations, stagger, grid, footer, layer numbers and close paths; the store, the picker, the economy and the phase machine.

**Placeholders:** none invented this round. The schedule is arithmetic, not a tunable.

**Studio-only:** whether a burst under card 1's flip is a flourish or a distraction from the card itself; whether two bursts of 80 pieces read as two beats or one dense cloud; whether the card-6 burst lands as a second beat rather than a repeat; and whether the log's burst-then-flip ordering is what a run actually prints, since the two lines are `0.12 s` apart and a reader may expect them adjacent.

## 173. Ball contacts gained a shared physical profile and a lower-serial Y-only pop

`BallSpawnerService.spawnBall` now assigns every body the same explicit physical profile: density `0.7`, friction `0.05`,
elasticity `0.8`, with the three-argument `PhysicalProperties` constructor so both weights stay at their defaults. The density
matches the existing Plastic/floor baseline; `heavy` is not denser, so a `heavy`↔`bully` engine collision has no power-specific
mass advantage. The existing transfer arithmetic remains what makes `heavy` shove. `spawnDecoy` now assigns the same profile
explicitly; it previously copied shape, size and material only.

The pop chance is **Placeholder.** `0.12` by default, with `heavy` at exactly half (`0.06`). A contact uses the lower of the
two power chances: either heavy body makes it half, two heavy bodies remain half rather than quarter, and missing/unknown
powers use default. `spawnDecoy` is only reached for `decoy`, so actual twins currently use default; a future decoy carrying a
`heavy` power label would use half.

Only the lower-serial contact handler rolls, once, and on success writes Y on both bodies. The velocity is reconstructed from
the current vector and the target Y only; X, Z and `BALL_SPEED` are untouched. The pop shares the burst's 2-second round-age
gate and 0.5-second per-contact-owner cooldown. It skips the roll if either body's absolute Y velocity is at or above the
**Placeholder.** 18 studs/s target, so it does not replace a fast physics bounce. A resting contact cannot pop every physics
step; the chance plus shared cooldown limits it, and the age gate excludes the measured spawn pile-up.

Source verification corrected two stale claims: `stepBallSpeeds` overwrites along-belt X and sets sway Z, but preserves Y, so
the old `onBallCollision` statement that an `AssemblyLinearVelocity` write would be overwritten was too broad. Also, the
spawner comment describing multiple shapes was stale: `SHAPE_POOL` currently contains only a Ball sphere. Installed
`@rbxts/types` declares `CustomPhysicalProperties: PhysicalProperties | undefined`, the three- and five-argument
`PhysicalProperties` constructors, its five fields, `Shape: Enum.PartType`, and settable `AssemblyLinearVelocity: Vector3`.
Those typings do not state exact collision-fidelity semantics for `PartType.Ball`; source confirms the pool uses Ball, but the
typing is not evidence for the prompt's exactness claim.

The belt floor remains `PhysicalProperties(0.7, 0, 0.5, 1, 1)`. Its elasticity participates in ball-floor contacts; friction
zero does not disable restitution. The ball's low nonzero friction can contribute to the contact pair. Whether the resulting
bounce looks right, chatters, or hovers is Studio-only, as are whether the collision reads as a hit, whether the pop is visible
from the belt camera, whether pile-up contacts strobe after the age gate, and whether `heavy` feels appropriately forceful.

The requested `shouldPop(..., serial, random)` signature has a no-argument random callback, while `drawTimers` takes
`random(min, max)`; the explicit signature was followed and tests inject normalized rolls. The lower-serial election belongs
in the handler, which applies one result to both bodies rather than asking the other `Touched` callback to roll again.
