## 174. Ball elasticity raised to 0.95, and the floor lowered to hold its contact where it was

`BALL_PHYSICAL_ELASTICITY` is `0.95` (**Placeholder.**), up from `0.8`. It reaches every spawned ball and every decoy through
the one module-scope `BALL_PHYSICAL_PROPERTIES` in `BallSpawnerService`; nothing else was re-plumbed.

**The floor, verified in source rather than from item 173's prose.** It is created in `TreadmillService.ensureSurface`, once per
belt bind (stored in `this.surfaces` keyed by belt, rebuilt when its parent is gone), and its properties were inline:
`new PhysicalProperties(0.7, 0, 0.5, 1, 1)` — density `0.7`, friction `0`, elasticity `0.5`, weights `1, 1`. So the record was
right about the values and the floor is per-belt, not one shared part; because the literal was the only copy, editing it plus a
constant covers every belt.

**The pair rule, verified against the Roblox `PhysicalProperties` docs (2026-11-10), not from memory.** The datatype resolves a
pair's friction and elasticity with the same pairwise weighted average,
`(a.V * a.Weight + b.V * b.Weight) / (a.Weight + b.Weight)`, with weights clamped `[0, 100]`. Consequences, all arithmetic
rather than judgement:

| pair | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ball-ball | `(0.8 + 0.8) / 2 = 0.80` | `(0.95 + 0.95) / 2 = 0.95` |
| ball-floor, floor left at `0.5` | `(0.8 + 0.5) / 2 = 0.65` | `(0.95 + 0.5) / 2 = 0.725` |
| ball-floor, floor at `0.1` | — | `(0.95 + 0.1) / 2 = 0.525` |
| ball-floor, floor at **`0.35`** (shipped) | — | `(0.95 + 0.35) / 2 = 0.65` |

Ball-ball is exact regardless of the default weight, because both bodies share the profile and equal weights cancel. The floor
pair depends on the ball's default weight, which the docs do not publish numerically for the three-argument constructor; the
docs' own `CustomPhysicalProperties` sample writes `1` for both weights and every stock material behaves that way, so the
equal-weight mean is the reading used here.

**Floor decision: (a), with `0.35` rather than the prompt's `0.1`.** `BELT_SURFACE_ELASTICITY` is a new **Placeholder.** in
`tuning.ts`; `TreadmillService` passes it and logs it on the existing `floor created` line (no new line). `0.35` holds the
ball-floor pair at exactly the `0.65` that shipped, so the only contact whose feel changed is ball-ball. `0.1` would give
`0.525` — about 19% less restitution than today — making every landing deader than at `HEAD`, which is a second unrequested
change to the same contact. Friction stays `0` (the `BALL_SPEED` model depends on it), density stays `0.7`, and the weights stay
explicit `1, 1` so the profile reads in one line.

**Three arguments were dropped or corrected.** (1) The prompt's `BALL_COLLISION_POP_UPWARD_SPEED (18)` is stale — the constant
is `30` in source, from a later tune; item 173's paragraph above still says `18` and is left as history. (2) The prompt's
suggested floor of `0.1` overcorrects, per the table. (3) `heavy` density was left alone: symmetric separation is the decision,
and a heavier `heavy` would have changed the engine's shove in the same round as the bounce, making neither readable.

**Expected but unverified.** Symmetric elasticity should make two balls leave each other faster, so the spawn pile-up should
*quiet* — each contact resolves in fewer re-touches — but it can also send a ball into a third body, so the `Touched` rate after
the initial two seconds is the thing to watch against item 109's measurement. Landing at `0.65` should be unchanged. Whether
`0.95` reads as "fighting" or "on springs" is the designer's call; it is one constant.

**Validation:** `npm run build` passed. `npm test` passed with **401 tests** across 29 files; no test asserted any physical
property or belt-surface value, so none changed. `npm run lint` exited 0 with the same 55 pre-existing Prettier warnings in
`src/shared/ui/viewport.ts`. The touched files pass `prettier --check`; the full-tree check still fails only on that file.
`\uXXXX` search under `src/` returned no matches and `flamework.build` is unchanged.

## 175. Contacts shove sideways, through the sway's own writer rather than against it

**The observation, and what the Studio log proved.** "I don't see much sideways push" is arithmetic, not tuning. `stepBallSpeeds`
sets the lateral (world Z) component of every ball's velocity each tick — the sway owns that axis since item 151 — so a
collision's lateral separation lasts exactly one physics step, about `1/60` of a stud, and is then replaced. The pasted log
shows the burst and pop lines firing at roughly the expected rate while no Z motion results, because both effects are
vertical (the pop) or purely visual (the burst). Raising elasticity in item 174 could not fix this either: it raises the
*speed* a pair separates at in every axis, but the Z component of that speed is still erased before it moves anything.

**The fix is an impulse, not a velocity.** A new module, `server/lateral-shove.ts`, holds a per-body vertical-free horizontal
impulse. `onBallCollision`'s new `maybeShove` records one impulse of `BALL_COLLISION_SHOVE_SPEED` on each body, opposite
directions along the flattened contact normal; `stepBallSpeeds` reads it, projects it onto the belt's `across`, **adds it to
the sway's lateral rate** and decays it by `BALL_COLLISION_SHOVE_DECAY_SECONDS`. The axis keeps exactly one writer, and the
shove cannot be erased because it is not a velocity — it is an input to that writer, the same relationship `BALL_SPEED` has
with X.

**The numbers, both Placeholder.** `5` studs/second peak and a `0.3` s time constant. The continuous displacement is
`speed * decay` = **1.5 studs**; the discrete per-tick sum the game actually produces is about **1.54**, which the spec
asserts at 5% and documents. One and a half ball diameters on a 12-stud belt, with lanes two studs apart: visible at the belt
camera, unable to carry a body into the neighbouring lane's resting spot. The sway's own position correction
(`SWAY_TRACK_SECONDS = 1.5`) walks the ball back to its wave, so a shove reads as a knock and a settle, not a lane change.

**Deliberate choices.** (1) The shove does not roll. The pop is a flourish and is chance-gated (currently `0.5` in the log);
separation is the consequence of a contact, so half the hits would still read as nudges if the two shared a roll. (2) It
shares the burst's round-age gate, its per-body cooldown and its lower-serial election, and runs before `maybeBurst` stamps
that clock — one `Touched` pair, one shove. (3) Impulses accumulate only up to one impulse's speed, so a body hit by three
neighbours inside a window refreshes rather than multiplies. (4) The along-belt part of the contact normal is dropped by the
writer's projection, so a dead-on rear-end contact barely shoves sideways and X stays the model's. That is deliberate: a
head-on pair has no sideways normal, and inventing one would read as a random flick. (5) `powers` stores a world-space normal
and the spawner projects it, so `powers` still needs no belt frame and the module makes no axis-aligned assumption.

**Cleanup.** `forgetLateralShove` is called from both spawner death paths, alongside the existing `lateral`/`startSpeeds`
deletes, so the map tracks the live set exactly as the other per-ball maps do.

**Tests.** New `src/server/test/lateral-shove.spec.ts` — 11 cases over the pure helpers (`shoveDirection`, `shoveStep`,
`clampShove`) and the map state machine. Two corrections came out of running it: `Vector3` components are 32-bit floats, so
the first tolerances (`1e-9`) were asserting float width rather than direction and now use `1e-6`; and the distance test
compares a **discrete** sum against `speed * decay`, which is 2.8% high at 60 Hz by `x / (1 - e^-x)`, so it asserts "above
the integral and within 5%" instead of within 1%.

**Validation:** `npm run build` passed. `npm test` passed with **412 tests** across 30 files (11 new). `npm run lint` exited 0
with the same 55 pre-existing Prettier warnings in `src/shared/ui/viewport.ts`. Every touched file passes `prettier --check`;
the full-tree check still fails only on that file. `\uXXXX` search under `src/` returned no matches; `flamework.build` is
unchanged — the new file is a plain module, not a controller or service.

**Studio-only:** whether 1.5 studs reads as a shove or as a wobble at the actual camera; whether adding a decaying lateral
term to the sway's write makes a shoved ball re-enter its wave smoothly or visibly fight it; and whether the pile-up gains
chatter now that balls are knocked across each other's paths. The `[Powers] shove` line reports the speed and direction
recorded, so a run distinguishes "not recorded" from "recorded and invisible".

## 176. Ball effects face the belt's start, and the burst is sized from the ball

**The direction, from the source rather than from a prompt's claim.** `stepBallSpeeds` writes the along-belt velocity as
`right.mul(-relative)` with `right = belt.CFrame.RightVector` and `relative = BALL_SPEED - BELT_SPEED`. A speed only decays,
so `relative` is negative for most of a ride and `-relative` is positive: the **elimination** direction is `+RightVector`,
and **start-ward is `-RightVector`**. The log confirms it on this scene: `rightVector = (0, 0, -1)` with belt-local X running
`-135` at spawn to `+168` at the exit. So `vfxForward(beltCFrame) = beltCFrame.RightVector.mul(-1)`, and it is written
against the belt's basis rather than world axes because this fixture's belt axis has changed between rounds (an earlier one
ran along X). That difference is precisely what makes a world-axis sign silent and wrong.

**One definition, in `shared/vfx-scale.ts`.** `vfxForward` is the single helper; both trails call `vfxFrameFor(position,
forward, authoredRotation)`, which is `CFrame.lookAlong` with the asset's own `UpVector` as `up`. Decision and cost: a plain
`lookAlong`/`lookAt` with the default up would force world up and discard the asset's roll in every case, so the authored
`UpVector` is passed instead. The residual cost is that an up vector is only meaningful perpendicular to the look direction,
so whatever part of the asset's up lies along the new forward is projected away — for an asset authored flat (up `+Y`,
forward horizontal) that is a **no-op**, and the test asserts both that and the tilted case.

**The belt, on the client.** New `src/client/belt-frame.ts`: one cached `GetTagged(TAGS.treadmillBelt)` walk, invalidated by
the belt's `Parent` going nil (the same rule `marker-spin-controller` uses), asked once per ball per frame. Before any belt
replicates — a real window, the log shows `[BeltScroll] … found=0` before bind — it returns `undefined` and each trail keeps
its previous authored-rotation frame rather than guessing a direction that would snap when the belt arrived. Two older
copies of that walk (`ball-render-controller`, `marker-spin-controller`) answer a different question and were not touched.

**Item 97 rewritten, not deleted.** Its rule had two halves. "Never read the ball's rotation" is still right and still why a
trail does not tumble; "take the asset's rotation whole" is what produced arbitrary headings, and both trails now carry the
override in place.

**The burst size.** `broadcastHit` gained a second remote argument: the **larger** of the two bodies' radii (a contact has two
bodies, and an effect smaller than the biggest thing in the contact reads as a bug; the average would be smaller than one by
construction). A second argument rather than a changed first one is the mixed-deploy-safe shape — Lua ignores extra
arguments, so an older client draws an unscaled burst rather than nothing, and a new client against an older server reads
`nil` and also draws unscaled. `effectScaleForRadius` is the same formula a trail uses, extracted so the arithmetic is not
written twice (item 101's lesson). The per-particle `Size` ramp is untouched, and `scaleEffect` is deliberately called
**before** the loop that rewrites it — the ramp is particle growth (studs), a different property that composes with the
clone's scale; reversing the two blocks would silently drop the scaling of `Size` while keeping `Speed`, `Acceleration` and
the attachment offsets.

**`VFX_SCALE_MULTIPLIER` reported, not changed.** It is `0.1`. `effectScaleForRadius` is
`radius / BASE_BALL_RADIUS * multiplier`, so a **20-stud** ball (radius `10`, twenty design radii) draws at
`20 * 0.1 = 2.0` — twice the authored size, on a ball twenty times the size the pack was drawn for. At `1` the same effect
draws at `20.0`, i.e. the authored geometry mapped exactly onto the ball, which is what "authored against a 1-stud ball"
means. `1` is the semantically correct value and `0.1` is a deliberate shrink; the choice is visual, so the number was left
alone for the designer. It is shared by both trails and now the burst, so it is one decision for three effects. **On this
20-stud ball `0.1` is very likely too small** — the trails are drawn at a fifth of the ball's width.

**Stale constants corrected.** `BALL_COLLISION_SHOVE_SPEED` / `_DECAY_SECONDS` had been retuned to `10` / `1` (10 studs of
displacement) for the 20-stud ball, and their docblocks still stated `5` / `0.3` / 1.5 studs. The arithmetic was rewritten
and the old pair recorded as history. Two `lateral-shove` tests that hard-coded a 240-step loop were changed to iterate
`10 * decay` worth of time, because a fixed count silently stopped covering the tail when the constant grew — that is what
had broken them.

**Tests.** New `src/shared/vfx-scale.spec.ts` (12 cases): `vfxForward` on the identity frame, on the scene's
`rightVector = (0,0,-1)` belt, and as the invariant `Dot(RightVector) = -1` under yaw — the identity case alone would pass a
world-axis implementation. `vfxFrameFor` covers position, `LookVector` facing forward (asserted on `LookVector`, which is a
part's **-Z**), authored tilt with its along-forward component removed, the flat-asset no-op, the degenerate parallel-up
fallback, and the no-belt path. `effectScaleForRadius` covers the design radius, linearity (asserting the reported `2.0` at
20 studs), and the `1` fallback for no size.

**Validation:** `npm run build` passed. `npm test` passed with **424 tests** across 31 files (12 new; two `lateral-shove`
cases rewritten, named above). `npm run lint` exited 0 with the same 55 pre-existing Prettier warnings in
`src/shared/ui/viewport.ts`. Every touched file passes `prettier --check`; the full-tree check fails only on that file, which
is untouched. `\uXXXX` search under `src/` returned no matches and `flamework.build` is unchanged — the new client module is
a plain module, not a controller.

**Studio-only:** whether the start-ward heading reads as "pointing home" or as backwards, which depends on how each asset was
authored around its own `-Z`; whether `lookAlong` makes a flat-authored asset stand up; whether a burst at `2x` is legible at
20 studs; and whether `VFX_SCALE_MULTIPLIER` should be `1`. The burst's log line now prints `radius=` and `scale=`, so a run
shows what was drawn without inferring it.

## 177. One scale tuner per ball effect, each in its own config file

**The state this replaced, verified from source.** Every ball effect scaled through one number, and the three effects did not
share a reference cleanly:

| effect | controller | config today | call | reference length | value | at a 20-stud ball |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `windBoost` trail | `wind-boost-controller` | none (local `ASSET_NAME`) | `effectScaleFor(ball)` | `BASE_BALL_RADIUS` 0.5 | `0.1` | `2.0x` authored |
| `tailWind` trail | `tail-wind-controller` | none (local `ASSET_NAME`) | `effectScaleFor(ball)` | `BASE_BALL_RADIUS` 0.5 | `0.1` | `2.0x` authored |
| `hitEffect` burst | `hit-effect-controller` | none (local `EFFECT_ASSET_NAME`) | `effectScaleForRadius(radius)` | `BASE_BALL_RADIUS` 0.5 | `0.1` | `2.0x` authored |
| `motionBlur` | `motion-blur-controller` | `MOTION_BLUR_SCALE` in `shared/motion-blur.ts` | `scaleEffect(clone, …)` | **the asset itself** | `1` | n/a — not ball-relative |
| ball phantom | `ball-render-controller` | — | matches the ball by construction | the ball | — | 20 studs |
| markers | `marker-spin-controller` | — | offsets are attributes relative to the body | the ball | — | scales with it |
| pickup sprite | `pickup-sprite-controller` | — | `PICKUP_SPRITE_STUDS` | studs | `2.6` | unchanged |

**`motionBlur` needed no ball tuner, and this is the fact the prompt wanted checked rather than assumed.** Its controller calls
`scaleEffect(clone, MOTION_BLUR_SCALE)` **directly** — not through `effectScaleFor` — because the effect is drawn around an
`EliminationZone` tens of studs across and was authored *in place*. `1` therefore means "the authored geometry, unchanged",
which is a real and statable reference, but it is the asset rather than a length, and the number already lives beside the ramp
constants it belongs with. A fourth config file holding only that number would have created a second home for it, so it was
left alone and its docblock rewritten to say what its reference is.

**What changed.** `effectScaleFor(ball, multiplier)` and `effectScaleForRadius(radius, multiplier)` take the multiplier as a
**required** parameter — not defaulted, because a default is one effect's number silently applying to another, and a required
parameter means a forgotten call site fails to compile rather than drawing at whatever was last decided. `VFX_SCALE_MULTIPLIER`
is **deleted from `tuning.ts`**, not zeroed: it had no reader once each effect passed its own. `BASE_BALL_RADIUS` stays, and
every config's docblock names it as the shared divisor.

**Three config files under `src/shared/config/`**, following `transition.config.ts`'s shape: named exports, a `**Placeholder.**`
on each tuned number, a docblock stating *what the number multiplies and what the reference length is*. Each holds its effect's
asset name as well, so "what is this effect and how big is it" is one file rather than half a controller plus a config —
which also makes the two trail files non-identical despite sharing a formula. `tailWind.config.ts`'s header says explicitly why
it is not the wind-boost file: the two reach the same arithmetic because item 101 found two hand-copied implementations had
drifted tenfold, but they are two assets driven by two attributes, and merging the numbers would re-create the coupling this
item exists to break.

**No retuning.** All three multipliers are `0.1`, which reproduces the exact size each effect drew before the split (`20 x 0.1
= 2.0` at a 20-stud ball). That equality is a consequence of the preserve rule, not a design statement — the point is that the
three are now three separate reads, which the spec asserts by moving one and checking the others.

**Where the prompt was wrong.** (1) `economy.config.ts` is **not** in `src/shared/config/` — that folder held only
`transition.config.ts`; `economy.config.ts` sits at `src/shared/`. (2) The trails' asset names were already local constants,
not config values, so "whether they move" was a free choice rather than a migration. (3) The claim that the burst's number is
"radius-relative while the trails' are width-relative" is **not true of the arithmetic**: `effectScaleFor` divides
`ball.Size.X / 2` by `BASE_BALL_RADIUS`, so it is radius-relative on exactly the same divisor. What actually differs is the
*provenance* of the radius — a live `BasePart` versus a number in the remote payload — and the config docblock says that
instead of the stated distinction. (4) Item 101's docblock could not simply gain a sentence: its argument was specifically that
the number should be shared, so it was rewritten in place to say what changed and why.

**Tests.** `vfx-scale.spec.ts`'s `effectScaleForRadius` block now passes multipliers and gained an independence case: three
effects at a 20-stud ball, all `2.0` (asserting the no-retuning rule), then one pushed to double its multiplier with the other
two checked unchanged. The old assertions referencing the deleted constant are gone. `motion-blur.spec.ts`'s comment about
`VFX_SCALE_MULTIPLIER` was updated; its assertion (`MOTION_BLUR_SCALE === 1`) is unchanged.

**Validation:** `npm run build` passed. `npm test` passed with **425 tests** across 31 files (one net new). `npm run lint`
exited 0 with the same 55 pre-existing Prettier warnings in `src/shared/ui/viewport.ts`. Every touched file passes
`prettier --check`; the full-tree check fails only on that file. `\uXXXX` search under `src/` returned no matches;
`flamework.build` is unchanged — three config modules and no controller or service added.

**Studio-only:** whether three separate tuners at values that reproduce today's sizes look unchanged (they should — that is
the point of preserving), whether the burst wants a different number from the trails now that it can have one, and whether
`MOTION_BLUR_SCALE`'s `1` means anything visible. All four effects print their scale on their existing lines
(`[WindBoost] … scale=`, `[TailWind] … scale=`, `[HitEffect] … scale=`, `[MotionBlur] … scale=`), so a run shows each value
without inferring it.

## 178. Each trail gets a heading offset; the burst and the blur get none, for different reasons

**What survives into each clone, from source.**

| effect | posed by | rotation kept | rotation discarded |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `windBoost` | `vfxFrameFor(pos, forward, assetRotation)` | the asset's **`UpVector` only** (its tilt / roll, as `lookAlong`'s `up`, minus any component along the new forward) | the asset's **yaw**, and its position |
| `tailWind` | same | same | same |
| `hitEffect` | `clone.CFrame = carrier.CFrame`, `carrier.CFrame = new CFrame(position)` | **nothing** — the frame is at the **identity rotation** | the asset root's entire rotation |
| `motionBlur` | `motionBlurCloneFrame(zone.CFrame, zone.Size.X, assetRotation)` | the **whole authored rotation**; position comes from the zone | nothing (position only) |

So the earlier statement "rotating a trail asset in Studio about the vertical axis does nothing" is correct and is a
property of `vfxFrameFor`: yaw is the component it replaces. Rotating about any other axis changes the `UpVector`, which *is*
kept, so a pitch/roll edit visibly tilts the effect — which is the opposite of intuitive and worth recording.

**`vfxHeadingOffset(frame, degrees)`** is `frame.mul(CFrame.Angles(0, math.rad(degrees), 0))` — **post**-multiplied, so the
axis is the frame's own up. Pre-multiplying would rotate the world-space position too and slide the effect off the ball. Sign,
as a literal rather than a claim: an identity frame's `LookVector` is `-Z`; `+90` leaves it on `-X` and `-90` on `+X`
(`R_y(+90)` maps `+Z` to `+X`). On a belt whose start is `+Z`, `0` = home, `180` = away, `±90` = across, which are the four
headings worth trying. **Zero returns the same frame instance**, not a recomposed near-identity, so "no offset" needs no
branch anywhere.

**Applied by the caller, not inside `vfxFrameFor`.** `frameFor` composes the frame and then turns it; `vfxFrameFor` keeps
answering only "which way is home and which way is up". That is the same split item 177 made for scale, and it also keeps the
pre-belt fallback path (asset rotation, no forward) free of a heading measured from a direction that does not exist yet.

**Two effects deliberately get no offset.**

- **`hitEffect` has no heading to offset.** Its clone is placed at the contact at the **identity rotation** — the assignment
  `clone.CFrame = carrier.CFrame` discards the asset root's rotation, and the comment beside it said the clone "keeps the
  asset's own `CFrame`", which was **wrong about the rotation half**; found while answering this question and corrected in
  place. A number measured from belt-ward has nothing to measure from here. What a designer still controls is everything
  *inside* the asset: child parts, attachment offsets and each emitter's `EmissionDirection` survive the clone, so those are
  the things to rotate in Studio. Making the burst belt-ward is a composition change, not a tuner.
- **`motionBlur` already honours a Studio rotation.** Its clone keeps the whole authored rotation, because its position comes
  from the `EliminationZone` and its rotation from the asset (item 142). So rotating that asset is the lever, it works, and a
  code offset would be a second conflicting knob over the same property. Its mount line already prints
  `assetRotation=` for exactly this reason.

**Where each offset lives, and why not in `vfx-scale.ts`.** `WIND_BOOST_HEADING_OFFSET_DEGREES` and
`TAIL_WIND_HEADING_OFFSET_DEGREES` are in their own config files beside the scale multiplier and the asset name, shipping at
`0`. A shared rotation table in `vfx-scale.ts` would re-create, for heading, exactly the coupling item 177 removed for scale:
one number again, one effect's tuning moving another's. `vfx-scale.ts` keeps the *function*; each effect keeps its *number*.

**Log lines.** The offset was added to the existing mount lines as `offset=Ndeg` on `[WindBoost]` and `[TailWind]` — no new
line. `[HitEffect]` and `[MotionBlur]` print no offset because they have none.

**Tests.** Six new cases in `vfx-scale.spec.ts`: zero returns the same frame (`toBe`, which is what catches a future rewrite
to `mul(CFrame.Angles(0, 0, 0))`); `+90` maps `-Z` to `-X`; `-90` maps it to `+X`; `180` reverses; position and up are
unchanged by a turn; and a 30-degree tilt keeps its own up under a 45-degree turn (the assertion that fails if the rotation is
pre-multiplied or about world up). A seventh pins both shipped offsets at `0`. Two spec corrections came from running it:
`Vector3` has no `Distance` member in the installed typings (`sub(...).Magnitude` instead).

**Validation:** `npm run build` passed. `npm test` passed with **432 tests** across 31 files (seven new). `npm run lint` exited
0 with the same 55 pre-existing Prettier warnings in `src/shared/ui/viewport.ts`. Every touched file passes `prettier --check`;
the full-tree check fails only on that file. `\uXXXX` search under `src/` returned no matches; `flamework.build` is unchanged.

**Studio-only:** whether `90`/`180`/`-90` land each trail pointing where the designer expects, and whether the kept `UpVector`
makes a yaw offset read as a turn rather than a wobble; whether the two trails want the same number or different ones (they
are separate for that reason); and whether the burst wants a belt-ward composition at all, which this round did not add.

## 180. A round holds at most one competitor per bound spawner, players first

**The counts as they were, from source.**

| path | what it spawned | the expression | total with 1 player / 8 lanes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `spawnRoundCompetitors` | one body per connected (or enrolled) player | `math.min(players.size(), lanes)` | 1 |
| `debugSpawnCompetitors` → `spawnBots` (key `4`) | one bot per bound spawner | `nextDebugOwners(spawner.getBoundSpawnerCount())` | 8 |
| `forcePlaying` (key `3`, fresh) | players, then bots | `min(players, lanes)` **+** `lanes` | 9 |
| `forcePlaying` (`Playing` restart) | same | same | 9 |
| `forceWaiting` (key `2`, Live) | players (via `startWaitingRound`), then bots | same | 9 |
| `forceWaiting` (key `2`, Studio) | players, then `spawnStudioBots` | `min(players, lanes)` + `lanes` | 9 |
| intermission timer | `startWaitingRound("intermission elapsed", true)` → players + `spawnStudioBots` | `min(players, lanes)` + `lanes` (Studio, solo only) | 9 |

**No per-round count constant exists**, and this was verified rather than repeated: `tuning.ts` has no `DEBUG_COMPETITORS`
and no competitor-count constant of any kind; the only related number is `DEFAULT_MAX_LIVE_BALLS = 50` in
`shared/attributes.ts`, which is a scene attribute on each spawner and a global body cap, not a round size.

**One function, `remainingCompetitorSlots(liveCompetitors, spawnerCount)`** in a new pure module
`src/server/competitor-slots.ts` — `math.max(0, spawnerCount - liveCompetitors)`. It could not live in `RoundService`
because that file cannot be imported in the Jest runtime (its dependencies reach `DataStoreService`), which is the same
reason `round-outcome.ts` and `debug-balls.ts` are modules. Both callers are methods of `RoundService`, so both reach it by
`import` with no cycle.

**Where the bound is applied, and why there rather than in `debugSpawnCompetitors`.** Both bounds sit in the two functions
every path funnels through: `spawnRoundCompetitors` (players) and `spawnBots` (bots). `spawnBots` is the one funnel for
**five** callers — key `4`, key `2` on Live, both key `3` branches, and `spawnStudioBots` — so bounding it there covers all
of them; bounding `debugSpawnCompetitors` would have left the other four exactly as they were, which was the defect. In
`spawnRoundCompetitors` the new bound is a **second** `math.min` term beside `min(players, lanes)`, which stays.

**Decoys do not consume a competitor slot.** The live count is `getLiveBalls().size()`, and `liveBalls` is filled by
`trackBall`, which only the player and bot paths call. A decoy is created by `BallSpawnerService.spawnDecoy`, is tracked by
nobody, is filtered out by `getCompetitors()`, and cannot win — so a `decoy` ball makes a round spawn its **full** complement
of real bodies. It still costs a `MaxLiveBalls` slot, which is unchanged.

**The auto-bots order, verified.** In Studio `forceWaiting` calls `startWaitingRound` → `spawnRoundCompetitors` →
`spawnStudioBots` (which fills to the cap) and then does **not** call `spawnBots` at all (`IS_STUDIO ? 0 : …`). On Live
`spawnStudioBots` returns `0` and the later `spawnBots` sees whatever `startWaitingRound` left. So the auto-bots always run
**first** and the second spawn finds the remainder — the reverse, which the prompt warns about, is not reachable from any
call site. When the remainder is zero it now prints
`[Round] debug spawn refused — no competitor slots (<reason>): live=N spawners=M` and returns `0`.

**Where the prompt was wrong.** (1) **Parts 3 and 4 contradict each other**: `debugSpawnCompetitors` *is* key `4`'s handler
(`DEBUG_SPAWN_REMOTE_NAME` → `debugSpawnCompetitors()`), so "cap `debugSpawnCompetitors`" and "key `4` bypasses the cap
regardless" cannot both hold. Acceptance criteria 3–5 (7 / 4 / 0 for 1 / 4 / 8 players) are explicit and testable and are
what the stated problem asks for, so they were implemented; key `4` is therefore bounded by the round's capacity, which
still gives one per spawner on an **empty** round — the case criterion 6's "one per spawner" describes. Key `4`'s real
remaining exemption is from the **player-count** bound: it fills every free slot rather than being limited by how many
humans are connected. (2) The claim that two bodies land on one lane "because the spawn point's `X` is belt-derived while
only `Z` comes from the spawner" is only half the mechanism: `spawnForRound` is **round-robin from lane `0`**, so a bot
spawn after a player body starts at lane `0` again. Bounding the count does not fix that — with one player and seven bots the
bodies still occupy lanes `0..6` with the player, leaving lane `7` empty — and the fix is lane choice, which was out of
scope.

**Tests.** New `src/server/test/competitor-slots.spec.ts`, six cases: empty belt, partial fill (1/4/7 live), exactly full,
over-full (`9` and `50` live), zero lanes (including with live bodies), and a property sweep asserting the result is always
in `0..lanes` for every pair up to `12`. No existing test asserted a count, so none changed.

refusal instead of adding a ninth; and that a solo Studio `Waiting` still fills the field to the cap rather than stopping

## 181. The decoy twin spends a slot, so eight lanes means eight bodies

**The report, and what the log proved.** "I see an extra ball spawn. there should be 8 ball" — and the count was correct:
`[Round] debug spawn (debug key 3 restart): 7 competitors …, live=8` beside `[Round] spawn lane=0 owner=BestDefault …
enrolled=true`. Eight competitors. What was nine was the **bodies**: the third press drew `decoy_ball`, and
`[MarkerSpin] state bodies=9` with `body="Workspace.SpawnedBalls.Decoy"` names the ninth. Item 180 had decided a decoy twin
does not *hold* a competitor slot — true, it has no owner and cannot win — while missing that it must still *spend* one from
the lane budget. A `decoy` ball costs two bodies.

**The fix is a body budget, not an owner count.** `nextDebugOwners` walked the drawn ids and charged each `decoy` id **two**,
stopping before the budget is exceeded. Eight free slots with one decoy in the draw now yields seven owners and eight bodies.
The cost predicate is `spawnsDecoy` — the existing definition of "this power makes a twin" — so a future power that spawns
something extra is counted by changing one function rather than by finding every counting loop.

**Two refusals, both logged.** A first drawn id that cannot fit (one slot left, a `decoy` next) returns zero with a line
naming the slot count, because half a decoy is a twin with no parent. A full round keeps item 180's `no competitor slots`
line. Neither is silent.

**A second log defect fixed in passing, same family.** `Playing → Playing (…, restart, competitors=1)` printed `restarted`,
which counts only the players' bodies — so the restart line said one beside a `debug spawn … live=8` two frames earlier. It
now prints `restarted + bots`. Two lines in one log disagreeing about how full the belt is, is the reading this tree keeps
paying for.

**Tests.** `competitor-slots.spec.ts` gained a `leadingBodiesWithinBudget` block (five cases): all-unit costs, the reported
defect (`[1,1,2,1,1,1,1,1]` in a budget of `8` takes **7** ids), a two-cost item that does not fit stops rather than
truncates, empty/budget-zero, and a property sweep asserting `owners + twins <= budget` for four draw shapes across budgets
`0..10`. The pure helper lives in `competitor-slots.ts` so it is assertable; `RoundService` only builds the cost array.

**Validation:** `npm run build` passed. `npm test` passed with **443 tests** across 32 files (five new). `npm run lint` exited
0 with the same 55 pre-existing Prettier warnings in `src/shared/ui/viewport.ts`; every touched file passes `prettier --check`.
`\uXXXX` search under `src/` returned no matches; `flamework.build` unchanged.

**Still Studio-only:** that a press drawing `decoy` now shows eight bodies rather than nine, and that a press whose only free
slot draws `decoy` logs the refusal. The player path is deliberately untouched: a player who *chose* `decoy_ball` keeps their
body and its twin even when that makes one body more than the lane count, because refusing a player their pick to satisfy a
body cap would be a worse trade than the extra twin.

**Correction (item 182): that last paragraph was wrong, and it was the remaining bug.** The Studio log separated the two cases
cleanly — presses where the player picked a non-`decoy` ball cleared **8** bodies, and presses where the player picked
`decoy_ball` cleared **9**:

```
[Picker] spawn player=prospeed1 ball=decoy_ball
[Round] debug spawn (debug key 3): 6 competitors, 1 decoy twin(s) … live=7
[Round] cleared 9 ball(s)
```

The twin was counted for bots and ignored for players, because `spawnBots` measured the **tracked competitor set** while the
designer was counting **bodies on the belt**. Leaving the player path "alone" therefore left the extra ball in.

## 182. The lane budget is charged against bodies, not tracked competitors

**One cause, both reports.** A `decoy` ball spawns two bodies. `RoundService.getLiveBalls()` is the *competitor* set, which
deliberately excludes a twin — it has no owner and cannot win — so any budget computed from it under-counts by one per decoy
already on the belt. Item 181 charged the **bot** draw for its own twins and still measured the field with the competitor set,
so the player's twin was invisible.

**The fix is a count of every spawned body.** `BallSpawnerService.getLiveBodyCount()` returns the spawner's `liveBalls`
filtered on `Parent` — the only list that contains twins. `spawnBots` uses it, so both decoys (player's and bot's) are charged
before the draw is made:

| scene | bodies before bots | lanes | slots | draw | bodies after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| player picked `decoy_ball` | 2 (body + twin) | 8 | 6 | 5 normal + 1 `decoy` | **8** |
| player picked anything else | 1 | 8 | 7 | 6 normal + 1 `decoy` | **8** |
| player picked `decoy_ball`, draw has no decoy | 2 | 8 | 6 | 6 normal | **8** |

**Why not change `getLiveBalls()` instead.** Because a twin is not a competitor and the winner rule depends on that: item 72
counts the field to decide "one left, they win", and a decoy in that count would be a competitor that can neither win nor be
eliminated. Two numbers, two questions — the competitor set for the round's *result*, the body count for the round's
*capacity* — and the bug was using the first for the second.

**Also logged now:** the debug-spawn line ends `bodies=<n>/<lanes>`, so a Studio run reads the ceiling directly instead of
adding up competitors and twins. That is the field a reader needs to confirm this fix.

**Validation:** `npm run build` passed. `npm test` passed with **443 tests** across 32 files (no test asserted a body count, so
none changed). `npm run lint` exited 0 with the same 55 pre-existing Prettier warnings in `src/shared/ui/viewport.ts`.
`\uXXXX` search under `src/` returned no matches; `flamework.build` unchanged.

**Still Studio-only:** that every press now clears exactly 8 bodies on an eight-lane belt whatever the player picked and
whatever the draw contains, and that `bodies=8/8` appears on the debug-spawn line.

## 183. The decoy twin is born five seconds into the round, not with its parent

**The third report of the same symptom, and the count was already right.** With item 182's body count, a press where the player
picked `decoy_ball` still showed a ninth body — because the twin is a **second body for one competitor**, created in the same
call as its parent. The round's capacity is eight bodies; a `decoy` ball makes two of them. No arrangement of the budget fixes
that without either dropping a real ball or refusing a player their pick, and both are worse than what the designer asked for:

> just spawn it 5 seconds after round starts

**`DECOY_SPAWN_DELAY_SECONDS = 5`** (**Placeholder.**, `tuning.ts`). `spawnBall` no longer calls `spawnDecoy` inline; it calls
`queueDecoy`, which records `{ spawner, parent, entry, power, startSpeed, dueAt }`. The spawner's existing 0.5 s `cleanup` loop
calls `spawnDueDecoys`, which creates any twin whose moment has come and drops any whose parent is gone. Properties, textures,
badges and markers are unchanged — `spawnDecoy` still owns all of them; only *when* it runs moved.

**Why the delay is measured from the ball's spawn and not from `Playing` entry.** They are the same instant for a ball spawned
at the green light, which is the reported case. For a ball spawned mid-round (key `4` in `Playing`), "five seconds after it
appeared" is the only reading that does not make the twin instantaneous.

**Why a queue and not `task.delay`.** A scheduled thread cannot be cancelled when the parent dies or the phase changes: it would
fire into a destroyed body, or into the next round after a teardown. A queue is checked by a loop that already exists, is dropped
wholesale by `setRoundActive(false)`, and skips entries whose parent has gone. The cost is up to one cleanup interval (0.5 s) of
lateness on a five-second delay.

**The decoy surcharge is gone with it.** Item 181 charged a `decoy` id two bodies in the debug draw so the opening field would
not exceed the lane count. Now that the twin is not part of the spawn, a `decoy` ball puts exactly one body on the belt like any
other, so the surcharge would leave the field one short. `leadingBodiesWithinBudget` and its five spec cases were **removed**
rather than left inert — the tree removes dead constants, and this one had no reader left. `spawnBots` is back to one owner per
free slot, and `remainingCompetitorSlots` (item 180) is the whole rule.

**What the log now says.** The debug-spawn line ends
`bodies=<on belt now>/<lanes>, twins=<scheduled by this draw>, pending=<queue depth>`, and each twin prints
`[Spawner] decoy born: parent=… delay=5s bodies=N/8`. Those four numbers are what tell "spawned nothing" from "spawned a twin
that has not been born yet".

**Consequences worth stating.** A round can therefore hold `lanes` bodies at `Playing` entry and `lanes + pendingTwins`
shortly after — that is the designer's call, not a bug: `MaxLiveBalls` is the only ceiling, as it was for key `4`. A twin whose
parent is eliminated inside the first five seconds never appears, which is the correct outcome for an imitation. A round that
ends inside five seconds drops the queue.

**Validation:** `npm run build` passed. `npm test` passed with **438 tests** across 32 files (five removed with the inert helper,
none changed). `npm run lint` exited 0 with the same 55 pre-existing Prettier warnings in `src/shared/ui/viewport.ts`. Every
touched file passes `prettier --check`. `\uXXXX` search under `src/` returned no matches; `flamework.build` unchanged.

**Studio-only:** that a press with `decoy_ball` in the field shows eight bodies at the green light and a ninth about five seconds
later, and that the twin appears beside its parent's *current* position rather than where the parent spawned.

## 184. The debug spawn fills free lanes, and every body records the lane it came from

**The bug, from source.** Two paths chose a lane index differently:

- `spawnRoundCompetitors` — `for (let lane = 0; lane < count; lane++) … this.spawner.spawnInLane(lane, owner)`. Lane = the
  loop index, so players take `0..n-1`.
- `debugSpawnCompetitors` → `spawnBots` → `spawnForRound(owners)` — `spawners[index % spawners.size()]`. **Index restarts at
  `0` on every press**, so after the players' own bodies a debug body landed on lane `0` beside the player and the last lane
  went unused. `[Ball:1] pos=(-313, 72.354, 111)` and `[Ball:2] pos=(-313, 72.551, 111)` are that: two bodies inside each
  other, `Touched` refiring every step, and the burst and sound spam that follows.

**A body now records its lane.** `SPAWN_LANE_ATTRIBUTE = "SpawnLane"`, written in `spawnInLane` — the single place that knows
the index — and **not** derivable from `Position`, because a lane is only where a body started. `spawnForRound` was rewritten to
take `laneIndices` and delegate to `spawnInLane`, so the attribute and the failure reporting have one implementation rather than
two, and the docblock that claimed round-robin kept lanes unique was replaced with what actually makes them unique.

**`laneIsOccupied(laneIndex, live)` and `freeLaneIndices(live, spawnerCount)`** in `competitor-slots.ts` — pure, over the
bodies' recorded lanes. A body with no `SpawnLane` (a `decoy` twin, or an older build) occupies nothing. `spawnBots` takes the
lowest free lanes, `min(slots, freeLanes.size())` of them, and logs a shortfall line when there are fewer free lanes than slots.
The player's lane is skipped **because it is occupied**, not because it is lane 0 — which is what makes the restart path correct
without a second rule.

**The restart ordering was already right**, verified: `forcePlaying`'s restart branch runs `clearAllBodies` →
`spawnRoundCompetitors` (which writes `SpawnLane` on the player's body) → `spawnBots`. The debug spawn therefore reads a belt
that already holds the player, and skips their lane. The same holds for the fresh `forcePlaying` path and for
`forceWaiting` → `startWaitingRound` → `spawnRoundCompetitors` → `spawnStudioBots`.

**What the log now says.** The debug-spawn line gained `lanes=`, listing the indices actually used, so the fix is visible
without comparing positions: one player must show `lanes=1,2,3,4,5,6,7`.

**Where the prompt was wrong.** Bodies did **not** record a lane, so `laneIsOccupied` could not be a read until one was added —
and a `Position` comparison, the prompt's fallback, would have reported every lane free one frame after each spawn because the
bodies ride away. The prompt's other expectation held: the restart ordering was already correct.

**Tests.** `competitor-slots.spec.ts` gained nine cases: `laneIsOccupied` at empty, one occupant (with its neighbours), a body
that has ridden away, a body with no lane, and a full belt; `freeLaneIndices` ascending on an empty belt, skipping an occupied
lane wherever it sits (`0` and `3` and a middle pair), empty on a full belt, and never returning an index past the spawner
count. One spec correction came out of running them: the fake's `GetAttribute` needs two parameters, because roblox-ts compiles
the call to a **colon call** and passes the receiver as the first argument — a one-parameter fake received the table where it
expected the attribute name and answered `undefined`.

**Validation:** `npm run build` passed. `npm test` passed with **447 tests** across 32 files (nine new). `npm run lint` exited 0
with the same 55 pre-existing Prettier warnings in `src/shared/ui/viewport.ts`; every touched file passes `prettier --check`.
`\uXXXX` search under `src/` returned no matches; `flamework.build` unchanged.

**Studio-only:** that a debug round's bodies are spread across distinct lanes (`lanes=` on the spawn line), and that the hit
burst and sound spam drops because no body starts inside another.

## 185. The power badge was culled at 120 studs, a number sized for a 56-stud belt

**Symptom:** "I can not see the name of the ball powers. It spawns then disappears."

**Cause, from source.** `updateBadge` sets `badge.MaxDistance = POWER_BADGE_MAX_DISTANCE`, and that constant was `120` with a
docblock that says so in as many words: *"The belt is ~56 studs long and the chase camera sits about 20 studs back, so 120
covers a ball at either end from either end."* The arena is now **336 x 173 studs** � a diagonal of about `377` � and the camera
has to sit well back to frame 20-stud balls. So a badge drew while its ball was near the camera at spawn and stopped drawing
once the ball rode past the cutoff. Nothing destroyed it: the `BillboardGui` stayed on the body, replicated, and was simply not
rendered.

**Fix:** `POWER_BADGE_MAX_DISTANCE` is **`600`** (**Placeholder.**) � the arena diagonal with margin for a chase camera that
trails a fast ball. The docblock now states the arithmetic instead of the 56-stud assumption, and records that the cost is draw
calls, not correctness: one `BillboardGui` with one `TextLabel` per body, on a round capped at eight bodies.

**What was checked and rules out the alternatives.** Nothing in `src/` destroys a badge except `updateBadge` with
`power === ""`, and there are exactly two writers of it (`presentPower` and `setPower` via `presentPower`), neither of which is
called with an empty power for a body that has one. `setPower` on a re-pick takes the "existing label" branch and only rewrites
`label.Text`. So the badge exists on every powered body and always did � the question was only whether it is drawn.

**Not changed, and why.** `POWER_BADGE_WIDTH` (96 px), `POWER_BADGE_HEIGHT` (20) and `POWER_BADGE_TEXT_SIZE` (14) are
screen-space sizes the badge was designed at, and `powerLabelFits` asserts the width against every power's label. If the names
are now legible but *small* at 300 studs, those three are the lever and they must move together � that is a separate judgement
about how a label should read at the new scale, not part of "it disappeared".

**Validation:** `npm run build` passed. `npm test` passed with **447 tests** across 32 files (no test asserted the distance, so
none changed). `npm run lint` exited 0 with the same 55 pre-existing Prettier warnings in `src/shared/ui/viewport.ts`; the
touched file passes `prettier --check`. `\uXXXX` search under `src/` returned no matches; `flamework.build` unchanged.

**Studio-only:** that every powered body shows its name for the whole ride, and whether the label is legible rather than merely
present at the far end.

## 186. The arena camera snaps on `Waiting` under the wipe, and debug key `2` is covered by it

**The rule: snap on `Waiting`, hold through `Playing` and `PostGame`, restore on `Intermission`.** `Playing`/`PostGame` only act as
the fallback for a client that joined late. New `src/client/controllers/treadmill-camera-controller.ts` (`@Controller()`), plus
`TAGS.treadmillCamera = "TreadmillCamera"` for a hand-placed part whose `CFrame` is the pose.

**The orientation is the part's full `CFrame`, not a derived one.** The belt is `336 x 173` with `rightVector = (0, 0, -1)`, so the
arena's long axis is not world `X`; a computed camera would have to know the fixture's yaw and would be wrong the next time the
scene is rebuilt. A designer positions and aims the part in Studio. A `BasePart` is preferred; a `Model` with a `PrimaryPart` is
accepted; anything else is skipped and the "no part" warning covers it.

**`forceWaiting` is now wrapped � this is the load-bearing change.**

```ts
this.clearAllBodies("debug key 2");
this.resetSyntheticCounter();
++this.generation;
const from = this.phase;
this.transitionAround(from, "Waiting", () => {
    const spawned = this.startWaitingRound(reason, false);
    const bots = IS_STUDIO ? 0 : this.spawnBots("auto-bots for debug key 2");
    this.enterWaiting(reason, spawned + bots);
});
```

`pendingTimerHold` behaves exactly as on the timer path with no extra code: `transitionAround` sets it **synchronously** before
its `task.spawn`, and `enterWaiting` consumes it via `consumeTimerHold()` inside the callback, so `Waiting`'s deadline is
`WAITING_SECONDS + hold` on both paths. **The spawn moved inside the callback** � outside it, bodies appeared in the previous
phase's lobby before the screen went dark.

**The generation is bumped before the wipe, not inside it.** The `Intermission` timer loop compares the generation it captured,
so bumping here retires it immediately; without it a `2` pressed just as intermission elapsed would race the timer and start two
wipes and two lobbies. `enterWaiting` bumps again, which is harmless.

**The docblock that argued for the unwrapped path was rewritten in place**, not deleted. It had said the wipe "exists to cover a
phase change the player did not ask for; a debug key is asked for, and covering the screen would hide the teardown the key exists
to demonstrate" (item 73). The replacement says that stopped being true once the camera snapped on `Waiting`: the wipe now hides a
**camera cut**, a visible cut is the one thing a camera change cannot afford, and the teardown is still visible because
`clearAllBodies` runs before the cover starts. The cost is named: ~2.5 s
(`coverSeconds() + TRANSITION_NETWORK_STEP + holdSeconds() + openSeconds()`) before a `2` press shows its phase.

**`forcePlaying` (`3`) is deliberately not wrapped.** Item 49 leaves `Waiting ? Playing` uncovered on purpose, and the camera rule
depends on that: `Playing` must not re-engage, or key `3` would put a visible cut on the one uncovered edge. `forceIntermission`
(`1`) was already unwrapped and stays so; `debugSpawnCompetitors` (`4`) changes no phase and is untouched.

**Debug keys, with the controller reading none of them:** `1` restores (enters `Intermission`); `2` engages under the wipe
(enters `Waiting`); `3` keeps the camera (`Playing` is already active and does not re-engage); `4` does nothing to the phase. Every
behaviour falls out of the phase rule.

**Restore and the two triggers.** Restore is `CameraSubject` (humanoid, else head) **then** `CameraType = Custom` � the subject
first so the engine has something to attach to on the frame the type changes. Trigger 1 is `Intermission` entry, under the wipe
item 49 wraps around `PostGame ? Intermission`. Trigger 2 is `CharacterRemoving`, chosen over `CharacterAdded` with a change check
because it fires while the old body still exists � the moment the default camera would snap back to a body about to vanish � and
because `CharacterAdded` needs a second comparison to tell the first spawn from a reset, which is exactly the case that must not
suppress anything. A reset sets `suppressedGeneration = generation`; the next `Waiting` bumps `generation` and resets the
suppression to `-1`, so the next round re-engages with no second flag to clear. **No new character yet:** restore to `Custom` with
whatever subject exists (possibly nil); `Scriptable` is never held, because holding it would strand the player looking at the
arena.

**Missing part and tag removal.** No tagged part at `onStart` warns once (`[TreadmillCamera] no part tagged TreadmillCamera �
camera stays on the player�`) and does not retry; `GetInstanceAddedSignal` picks up a part tagged later and logs
`attached late part=�`, so a Studio tag while running needs no restart. Tag removed mid-round: the controller **keeps the last
pose** and stays engaged, because the restore path is keyed on `RoundState` and a phase change still releases the camera �
releasing on the tag removal itself would move the camera for a reason the player cannot see.

**Log lines, actual:**

```
[TreadmillCamera] mounted part=Workspace.arena.treadmillCamera fov=70 character=true
[TreadmillCamera] active part=Workspace.arena.treadmillCamera phase=Waiting generation=3
[TreadmillCamera] restored (round end) to=Custom character=true generation=3
[TreadmillCamera] restored (character loss) to=Custom character=true suppressedGeneration=3
```

The wipe evidence needs no line of its own: `[Transition] covering (Intermission ? Waiting)` / `[Transition] uncovered (Waiting)`
now fire on a `2` press as well as on the timer.

**`flamework.build` regenerated** � `flamework.build` and `out/tsconfig.tsbuildinfo` deleted first, never `rm -rf out` (item 52).
The grep that proves the controller boots:

```
"roblox-treadmill-race:out/client/controllers/treadmill-camera-controller@TreadmillCameraController": "client/controllers/treadmill-camera-controller@TreadmillCameraController",
```

**Where the prompt was wrong.** (1) `forceWaiting` did call `startWaitingRound` then `enterWaiting`, but the **spawn had to move
inside the wipe**, which the prompt's suggested shape (`transitionAround("Waiting", () => { �enterWaiting� })`) did not say � as
written, bodies would have appeared in the old phase's lobby before the cover. (2) `pendingTimerHold` needed **no extra
handling**: `transitionAround` already sets it synchronously before scheduling, so `enterWaiting` consumes it inside the callback
unchanged. (3) `enterIntermission`'s re-arm does interact � not with the hold, but with the **generation race** described above,
which needed the pre-bump. (4) `TRANSITION_CONFIG.ENABLED` is `true` in the tree, verified. (5) The wipe labels have an ASCII
`-`/`?` in the compiled string (`covering (${from} ? ${label})`); unchanged, recorded here so the next reader does not think the
log is truncated.

**Not verified without Studio:** whether a ~2.5 s wipe on a `2` press reads as a transition or as a stall; whether the snap is
genuinely invisible under the wipe at the belt's scale; whether `CharacterRemoving` really fires before the replacement exists on
this platform (the code handles either); whether `CameraType = Custom` with a nil subject behaves as the docs describe; and whether
the authored part's `CFrame` actually frames the belt � the one number a designer sets by eye.

**Validation:** `npm run build` passed and regenerated `flamework.build`; `npm run lint` exited 0 with the same 55 pre-existing
Prettier warnings in `src/shared/ui/viewport.ts`; `prettier --check "src/**/*.ts"` fails only on that file. `\uXXXX` search under
`src/` returned no matches. **`npm test` was not run**, per the constraint.

## 187. Three fixes: a ghost diagnostic, a size-relative roll, and a scaled pickup

**Part 1 � the ghost: cause not established, so nothing was fixed.** Read from source, the group assignment and the pair table are
both present and correct: `presentPower` calls `ensureCollisionGroups()` then sets
`ball.CollisionGroup = collisionGroupFor(power)`, and `collisionGroupFor("ghost")` returns `GhostBall`; the five-pair table is
registered exactly as docs/powers-and-vfx.md �4 describes, including `GHOST_GROUP`/`BALL_GROUP = false`. `onBallCollision` returns
before the burst unless `other.HasTag(TAGS.ball)`, and `maybeBurst` is called from nowhere else. So candidates (1) and (3) have no
source-level defect, and (4) is ruled out by the burst being the only `[HitEffect]` producer. **What remains is (2): whether the
pair was actually applied at runtime** � the calls are `pcall`-guarded and a failure was silent.

Two diagnostics added, one line each, both of which answer that:

- `ensureCollisionGroups` now reports every step: `[Powers] collision groups: register=CompetitorBall register=GhostBall
  CompetitorBall/Default=true GhostBall/Default=true CompetitorBall/CompetitorBall=true GhostBall/GhostBall=false
  GhostBall/CompetitorBall=false GhostBallRegistered=true CompetitorBallRegistered=true`, with `:FAILED` appended to any step
  whose `pcall` returned false. Its docblock said the guard was safe because the names might pre-exist; it now also says the
  report is what makes a failure visible.
- The existing `[Ball:N] spawn` line gained `group=<CollisionGroup>` � it did **not** print one. A ghost that reads
  `group=Default` is candidate (1); one that reads `group=GhostBall` beside `�=false` applied is a physics question for Studio.

**No speculative pair change was made.** Disabling a pair on a guess could break real collisions for every ball, and the prompt's
own rule is fix only what the diagnosis proves.

**Part 2 � the roll. The phantom *is* advancing; `omegaVisual=0 angle=0` is a stale field, not a stopped skin.** In
`marker-spin-controller` the rate branch is `if (phantom !== undefined) { omega = 0; rateSource = "phantom" }`, and the whole
`state.spin` / `state.angle += �` block sits inside `if (phantom === undefined)`. So with a skin present � which every client has
� `angle` never advances **by design**, because the skin's own `state.spin` in `ball-render-controller` is the picture and a second
rotation on top would double it. The log now prints `omegaVisual` from `apparentSpinRate(ballSpeed)` on the phantom path too, so
the next run shows the rate actually in use instead of a field that cannot answer.

**The rate was `min(90, GAIN * speed / radius)` with `GAIN = 3`, which divides by the ball's own radius** � so at radius `10` and
`speed 11` it drew `3.3 rad/s` (half a turn a second), against `66 rad/s` at radius `0.5`. That is the reported creeping, and the
arithmetic is exactly the 20x ratio the designer estimated.

**The fix is the size-relative form, at the no-slip gain.** `apparentSpinRate(speed)` now divides by `BASE_BALL_RADIUS` (the
pack's design radius) instead of the body's, and `APPARENT_SPIN_GAIN` is back to `1`:

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `speed 10`, radius 10 | `3 * 10 / 10 = 3.0 rad/s` | `1 * 10 / 0.5 = **20.0 rad/s**` (`3.2 rev/s`, `19 deg/frame`) |
| `speed 20`, radius 10 | `6.0 rad/s` | `40.0 rad/s` |
| clamp `APPARENT_SPIN_MAX_RAD_PER_SEC = 90` | never binds | never binds |

`1` is not a new number: `APPARENT_SPIN_GAIN`'s own docblock argues for it as the no-slip value and records that `3` "shipped for
one round and produced the very symptom it was meant to cure" � at radius `0.5` it drew `60 rad/s`, which is `57 deg` between
frames on a six-textured sphere, aliasing into a slow crawl. **The literal 20x (`66 rad/s` at radius 10) lands back in that same
regime**, so it was rejected on the tree's own measured arithmetic rather than on taste; the shipped rate is exactly the number
that was legible when the ball was one stud. The cost is stated in the docblock: **this is no longer a rolling rate** � a 20-stud
ball drawn at the 1-stud rate is slipping � and a future ball resize needs no retuning because of it.

**Part 3 � the pickup.** Current sizes as a ratio of a 20-stud ball's width:

| thing | constant | studs | ball-widths |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| pad collider | `PICKUP_SIZE = (2, 1, 2)` | 2 | **0.10** |
| sprite | `PICKUP_SPRITE_STUDS = 2.6` | 2.6 | **0.13** |
| footprint disc | `min(padX, padZ)` | 2 | **0.10** |

New `src/shared/config/pickup.config.ts` holds `PICKUP_SCALE_MULTIPLIER = 0.2` (**Placeholder.**, item 177's shape: one
multiplier, own file, docblock stating the reference length). The sprite and the disc both go through
`effectScaleForRadius(poolBallRadius(), PICKUP_SCALE_MULTIPLIER)`:

| multiplier | scale | sprite | disc | sprite in ball-widths |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `0.05` | 1 | 2.6 studs | 2 studs | 0.13 (**reproduces the old size**) |
| `0.1` | 2 | 5.2 | 4 | 0.26 |
| **`0.2` (shipped)** | 4 | **10.4** | 8 | **0.52** |
| `1.0` | 20 | 52 | 40 | 2.6 |

`poolBallRadius()` was added to `shape-pool.ts` � the radius from the pool's first entry, because a pickup is **not attached to a
ball** and a scene scan would answer `undefined` on exactly the frames a pad is built.

**The pad collider was not changed.** Scaling `PICKUP_SIZE` makes pickups easier to hit and therefore changes the race, which is a
designer's decision. **Recommendation: scale it to match the disc** (`PICKUP_SIZE` x4 to `(8, 1, 8)`), because until then the painted
target **overhangs the actual collider by 4x** and teaches the player a target that does not exist. The sprite/docblock states that

values.

**Where the prompt was wrong.** (1) The `[Ball:N] spawn` line did **not** print a `CollisionGroup`; it does now. (2) The phantom
**is** advancing � `omegaVisual`/`angle` are fallback-branch fields that cannot answer the question, which is the trap the prompt
suspected but for the opposite reason. (3) Part 2's "20x" is not the safe read: the tree had already documented that a rate above
about `31 rad/s` aliases on this render, so `66 rad/s` would have reproduced a fixed bug. (4) Part 3's premise that the ring is a
separate size from the pad is wrong � the disc is `min(padSize.X, padSize.Z)` read at creation, so scaling it makes it overhang
the collider until the pad is scaled too.

**Validation:** `npm run build` passed; `npm run lint` exited 0 with the same 55 pre-existing Prettier warnings in

`apparent-spin.spec.ts` was rewritten for the one-argument signature (four cases: deadband, gain term, clamp, and the new

`\uXXXX` search under `src/` returned no matches. `flamework.build` is unchanged � no controller added.

## 189. The collision handler refuses pairs the group table forbids, and every effect line names its groups

**The log, read against the table.** `[Powers] collision groups: � GhostBall/GhostBall=false GhostBall/CompetitorBall=false
GhostBallRegistered=true` and `[Ball:2] spawn � group=GhostBall` are both present and correct, and yet effect lines kept firing.
They could not say *which* bodies were involved, because every body is named `Workspace.SpawnedBalls.Ball`. So the report could
not distinguish "the guard is missing" from "the burst was two ordinary balls". Both halves are now answerable.

**Part 1 � the lines.** `[Powers] pop`, `[Powers] shove` and `[Powers] hit` each gained `ballGroup=<group> otherGroup=<group>`,
one field each on lines that already existed. A burst near a ghost now reads `ballGroup=GhostBall` (the guard is missing) or
`ballGroup=CompetitorBall otherGroup=CompetitorBall` (no bug � the report was two ordinary balls).

**Part 2 � the predicate.** `pairCanCollide(a, b)`, exported and pure, built from `BALL_GROUP` and `GHOST_GROUP` rather than
string literals. **Two groups are enough:** every one of the five registered pairs is decided by whether a ghost is involved and
what it faces � competitors collide, ghost/ghost does not, ghost/competitor does not. No third group is needed because nothing
here distinguishes kinds of solid thing; the belt, the walls and the floor are all `Default`. An unrecognised group returns
`true`, which is the fail-safe direction: the worst outcome is an effect that should not have fired, never a body falling
through the world.

**`Default` collides, both ways round, and it is asserted.** `pairCanCollide(BALL_GROUP, "Default")` and its mirror, plus the
`GHOST_GROUP`/`Default` pair � the belt surface, walls and invisible floor. That is the case whose failure would read as "the
physics is gone" rather than "the ghost guard is wrong", so it is the one under test.

**Part 3 � where the guard sits.** In `onBallCollision`, after `other.HasTag(TAGS.ball)` and **before `rememberTouch` and all
three effects**, so the full ladder is now:

1. `powersActive` ? 2. `other` carries the `Ball` tag ? **3. `pairCanCollide`** ? 4. `rememberTouch` ? 5. `maybePop` ?
`maybeShove` ? `maybeBurst` ? 6. body state + colliding power ? 7. `POWER_COLLISION_COOLDOWN` ? 8. the transfer has somewhere to
go.

It sits beside the tag test rather than above the whole ladder because `powersActive` and the tag test are about *what is being
talked about*, while everything from 3 down assumes two balls actually met.

**The `Touched` connection stays on every body** (item 87). Removing it for a ghost would make the last-touch record � which
feeds the elimination sound � incomplete for the bodies a ghost *does* collide with, and a guard in one handler is a smaller
change than a second connection policy. The cost is one attribute read and two string comparisons per stray event; the
alternative, a proximity scan, would be a query per ball per frame to re-answer a question the physics broadphase already
answered.

**The docblock was rewritten to match.** `onBallCollision` argued that a ghost's `Touched` "cannot arrive"; it now carries the
ladder above and says the guard exists because that assumption was reported false.

**Where the prompt was wrong.** The prompt expected one of "a third group is needed", "the guard belongs above the whole ladder",
or "a decoy's group is set by `setPower`". None held: two groups suffice, the guard belongs beside the tag test, and a decoy's
group comes from `presentPower` � `spawnDecoy` calls `presentPower(decoy, power, �)`, which sets `ball.CollisionGroup =
collisionGroupFor(power)` with the **parent's** power, so **a twin is in the same group as its parent** and a ghost's twin is
itself a ghost. `setPower` would also set the group, but a decoy deliberately never uses it, because that path would register an
aura and a `Touched` connection the twin must not have.

**Validation:** `npm run build` passed; `npm test` passed with **453 tests** across 32 files (six new `pairCanCollide` cases);
`npm run lint` exited 0 with the same 55 pre-existing Prettier warnings in `src/shared/ui/viewport.ts`; both touched files pass
`prettier --check`. `\uXXXX` search under `src/` returned no matches; `flamework.build` unchanged � no controller or service added.

**Studio-only:** that a ghost now passes through balls with no burst, no sound and no shove; that ordinary balls still collide
and still shove; and whether the group fields show a `GhostBall` on a line that still fires, which would prove the physics pair
is not being honoured and make this its own round.

## 190. The painted pickup disc is the collider's inscribed circle again, and the sprite keeps the tuner

**The claim, quoted from source.** `buildFootprint` sized the disc as
`const diameter = math.min(padSize.X, padSize.Z) * scale;` where `scale = effectScaleForRadius(poolBallRadius(),
PICKUP_SCALE_MULTIPLIER)` � `(10 / 0.5) * 0.2 = 4`. Meanwhile `PickupService.createPickup` sets `pickup.Size = PICKUP_SIZE`
(`20 x 20 x 20`) and `positionFor` only lifts it. So the paint was `4x` the thing it described:

| thing | expression | studs | � collider width |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| collider | `PICKUP_SIZE.X` | **20** | 1.00 |
| painted disc | `min(padSize.X, padSize.Z) * scale` | **80** | **4.00** |
| sprite | `PICKUP_SPRITE_STUDS * scale` | **10.4** | **0.52** |

The collection rule was never wrong � the log shows `[Pickup] collected � BALL_SPEED 6.4 -> 12` the instant the collider was
touched. The picture was the only liar, and it lied by exactly the scale multiplier.

**The disc no longer takes the multiplier.** `pickupDiscDiameter(padSize)` in `shared/config/pickup.config.ts` returns
`math.min(padSize.X, padSize.Z)` � the collider's own inscribed circle, `20` studs, ratio `1.00`. A function rather than an
inline `min` because the equality with the collider is the whole rule and a spec should hold it:

| thing | expression | studs | � collider width |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| collider | `PICKUP_SIZE.X` | 20 | 1.00 |
| painted disc | `pickupDiscDiameter(padSize)` | **20** | **1.00** |
| sprite | `PICKUP_SPRITE_STUDS * scale` | **10.4** | 0.52 |

**Why the disc and not the sprite keeps the raw value.** The disc is the only pickup visual that makes a claim about
*reach* � "put the ball's centre in here and it collects" � so it cannot be tuned independently of the box it describes. The
sprite is an **icon**, and an icon may be authored at whatever reads well. That is the split the docblocks now state, in both
directions: `PICKUP_SCALE_MULTIPLIER` says it governs the sprite and *not* the disc, and `pickupDiscDiameter` says the disc
follows `PICKUP_SIZE` and nothing else.

**The sprite is already inside the disc** � `10.4` against `20` � so its value did not change. `0.4` would draw it at `20.8`,
larger than the disc, which is the contradiction this round removed; that is named in the multiplier's docblock as the value
not to use.

**The docblock that was contradicted was rewritten in place.** `buildFootprint` had argued the disc was "inscribed in that
square cross-section" and that "every point inside the ring is inside the collider" � true of the *formula*, false of the
*scaled result*. It now says that was only half true until this item, quotes the `80`-versus-`20` failure, and states that the
disc takes no multiplier.

**Where the prompt was wrong.** (1) `PICKUP_SIZE` is `(20, 20, 20)`, not the `(2, 1, 2)` a previous report recorded � the pad
has **already** been made 20 studs wide, so "the collider is right" is true and the `80`-stud ring is the whole bug. (2) The
disc *already* reads the pad rather than a constant, so the fix was to remove the multiplier from that expression rather than
to re-source the number. (3) The prompt expected the sprite might have to shrink; it does not � it was already half the disc,
and only looked proportionate because the disc was four times too big.

**A stale pin in another spec was found by this round's run.** `apparent-spin.spec.ts` asserted the literal `20` rad/s at
`speed 10`, which broke when `APPARENT_SPIN_GAIN` was retuned from `1` to `2`. It now derives the expectation from
`APPARENT_SPIN_GAIN / BASE_BALL_RADIUS` and still asserts the rate stays under the clamp at `BALL_SPEED 20` � a test that fails
on a designer's tuning is testing the tuning, not the rule.

**Validation:** `npm run build` passed; `npm test` passed with **456 tests** across 33 files (three new disc cases; one
`apparent-spin` case rewritten, named above); `npm run lint` exited 0 with the same 55 pre-existing Prettier warnings in
`src/shared/ui/viewport.ts`; every touched file passes `prettier --check`. `\uXXXX` search under `src/` returned no matches;
