disc is still legible from the game camera. **If it reads as a dot, the honest next step is a larger `PICKUP_SIZE` � a bigger
collider � not a bigger picture**, because the paint is the promise and the collider is the fact.

## 191. Pickups: any point on the belt, up to 12, non-overlapping, wholly inside it

**The position had exactly one lane-coupled piece, and this round removed it.** `positionFor` was
`belt.CFrame.mul(new CFrame(localX, lift, localZ)).Position` with `localX = PICKUP_X_MIN + math.random() * (PICKUP_X_MAX - PICKUP_X_MIN)` (**already random**) and `localZ = belt.CFrame.PointToObjectSpace(spawner.Position).Z` (**the lane**). `Y` was and still is `belt.Size.Y / 2 + BELT_SURFACE_THICKNESS + PICKUP_SIZE.Y / 2` — the **floor's** top face, not the belt's. The previous claim that the whole position was lane-derived was wrong; only `Z` was.

**`maxPickups()` did not exist.** The count was written inline in `spawnPickups` as `spawners.size()` and `maxPickups()` survived only as a name in two docblocks. It is now `PICKUP_MAX_COUNT = 12` (**Placeholder.**) outright, **not** `min(12, boundSpawnerCount)`: a pad is not a body, holds no `BALL_SPEED`, and consumes no slot against `MaxLiveBalls` (`50`), so the two numbers were equal only because both happened to be read from the spawner list. **The coupling is intentionally gone** — a future "one pickup per lane" must be its own constant, because reconnecting this one to `getBoundSpawnerCount()` would silently cap the pads at whatever the place contains.

**`PICKUP_X_MIN = -18` / `PICKUP_X_MAX = 23` are deleted, not widened.** They were absolute numbers on the *world* `X` axis chosen by eye against one 336-stud belt; a belt turned a quarter turn would have bounded the wrong axis while still looking plausible. Their only reader was `pickup-service.ts`; no other file or spec named them. `BallSpawnerService.getBoundSpawners()` lost its only caller in the same change and is **deleted** rather than left as a live-looking accessor with no reader — `getBoundSpawnerCount()` remains and still governs the competitor cap and lane assignment.

**The bounds are belt-local arithmetic, in a new pure module.** [`shared/pickup-placement.ts`](../src/shared/pickup-placement.ts) holds `pickupBounds(beltSize, padSize)` (belt half-extents minus pad half-size on `X` and `Z`), `padFootprint`, `rectsOverlap`, and `beltLocalToWorld`. **No `Y` case, deliberately**: the pad rests on the invisible floor under the belt and hangs above it (`CanCollide = false`), so "inside the belt's `Y`" is a rule about the wrong part — and a 20-stud pad could never fit a 0.1-stud slab anyway. The clamp `math.max(0, …)` collapses the band to `0..0` for a pad wider than the belt (written `0 - reach` so the log does not print `-0`), which is the honest degenerate answer; an inverted band would place pads off the edge.

**Placement is a rule, not a check: bounded rejection sampling.** Each pad gets up to `PICKUP_PLACEMENT_ATTEMPTS = 20` (**Placeholder.**) draws; a candidate is rejected if `rectsOverlap` says its belt-local rectangle touches a pad already taken — including the live pads, which are seeded into the taken list from their own positions via `PointToObjectSpace`. `rectsOverlap` is strict (`<`), so **two flush pads do not overlap**: they share a face, and a ball can pass between them. A centre-distance test was rejected instead: two 20-stud pads 28.3 studs apart diagonally do not touch, while two 19 apart do, and no single threshold answers both.

**A pad that cannot be placed is reported, not retried forever.** Hitting the bound logs
`[Pickup] placement shortfall reason=… placed=n requested=m unplaced=m-n attemptsPerPad=20 bounds=x[…] z[…] pad=20x20`, and the next attempt is the ordinary 15 s top-up tick — bounded there too, so a genuinely crowded belt warns once per 15 s instead of spinning.

**Log lines.** `[Pickup] spawned` is now `reason=… placed=n requested=m live=k count=12 bounds=x[min,max] z[min,max] positions=<localX>,<localZ>|…`; the positions switched from world `X` to **belt-local `X`** so a position and the bounds it must sit inside are in the same units. `PICKUP_SIZE`, the `Y` lift, `pickupDecision`, `speedAfterPickup`, the `recycle` exception, the sound, the sprite and the disc are all unchanged.

**Where the prompt was wrong.** (1) `maxPickups()` did not exist — the count was inline. (2) `X` was **already random**; only `Z` was lane-derived. (3) The overlap test needs no `Y`: pads are 20 studs tall against a 0.1-stud belt, and they sit *above* it by design. (4) **The deleted constants were not only belt-size blind — they also encoded reachability.** `-18` kept pads in front of the spawn line and `+23` kept them short of the exit; `pickupBounds` knows the belt's geometry and nothing about where balls go. A pad can now be drawn ahead of the spawn line (local `-158` against spawners at roughly local `-23`), where it is reachable only by a ball that has been boosted **past** belt speed — a rare visit rather than an impossibility, since a boost drives a ball back toward the spawn end. If that turns out to read as a broken pad, the fix is a reachability sub-band derived from the spawn line, **not** a return to absolute numbers.

**Validation:** `npm run build` passed; `npm test` passed with **468 tests** across **34 files** (twelve new `pickup-placement` cases: bounds, the flush-pad case, the rectangle-vs-distance case, the 90°-rotated belt, and the packing headroom); `npm run lint` exited 0 with the same **55** pre-existing Prettier warnings in `src/shared/ui/viewport.ts` (left alone — it fails at `HEAD` on line endings); every touched file passes `prettier --check`; `\uXXXX` search under `src/` returned no matches; `flamework.build` unchanged. One spec value changed during the round: the degenerate bounds case asserted `0` and received `-0`, fixed in the implementation rather than the test.

**Studio-only:** that 12 pads appear spread across the belt rather than one per lane; that no two overlap (compare the `positions=` list against `bounds=`); that every pad is fully on the belt at both ends, including one whose centre sits at a bound; and that a ball still collects a pad anywhere it sits. A ball whose centre is on a pad but which does not collect would now mean the pad is where the log says it is and the contact is the problem — which is the case the per-pad `positions=` field exists to separate.

## 192. The arena `motionBlur` is sized from the `EliminationZone`, and the depth machinery that made inert is deleted

**Reported: "The `MotionBlur` does not fill the entire eliminationZone."** The log said why in two numbers. `[MotionBlur] mounted ... scale=1` and `[MotionBlur] show ... pos=-415.6000061035156, 108.62091064453125, -22.499984741210938 depth=52.4 emitters=2` — `depth` was `MOTION_BLUR_DEPTH_FRACTION (0.2) x zone.Size.X`, so the zone is **262 studs long**, and the effect was drawn at `MOTION_BLUR_SCALE x authored` = whatever the Studio asset happens to be. This is item 140's own open question ("whether `MOTION_BLUR_SCALE = 1` matches the zone's visual footprint") being answered, three rounds later, by the person looking at it.

**The size is now derived from the fixture.** `extentAlong(size, basis, direction)` projects the authored box onto a **zone axis** — needed because the clone keeps the asset's authored rotation (item 142), so `asset.Size.X` is not the zone's width once the asset is turned, which is exactly the class of mistake `PICKUP_X_MIN` made with a world-axis number on a turnable belt (item 191). `motionBlurFillRatio(zoneSize, extents)` then returns the **largest** of the three per-axis ratios, so no axis is left short; overshoot spills haze past the boundary instead of leaving a gap inside it. One uniform ratio because `scaleEffect` scales a scalar — an emitter's `Size` is a diameter and its `Speed` a magnitude, so there is no anisotropic form of "a bigger puff along `X`". A **flat axis is skipped rather than clamped**: a sheet has no thickness to fill, and dividing by it (even by a `1e-3` floor) would scale the effect by thousands.

**`MOTION_BLUR_SCALE` still exists and changed meaning.** It is now a trim on the fill ratio: `1` = exactly the zone, `2` = twice it. It is still not `effectScaleFor(ball)` and still not any ball config's multiplier, for the reasons its docblock keeps.

**The placement machinery is deleted, not set to `0.5`.** A zone-sized effect has exactly one position that fills the zone — its centre — so `MOTION_BLUR_DEPTH_FRACTION`, `motionBlurDepthStuds` and `motionBlurAnchor` were arithmetic that multiplied out to zero, and `motionBlurCloneFrame` is now `new CFrame(zoneFrame.Position).mul(assetRotation)`. A fraction whose only correct value is `0.5` is a knob that can only be set wrong, and this tree deletes inert values rather than leaving one at a value that happens to work (item 190's rule). **The documented history stays in `motionBlurCloneFrame`'s docblock** because the trap is still live: a *smaller* effect (`MOTION_BLUR_SCALE < 1`) at the centre is what item 140 shipped and item 141 was asked to move, so pushing the haze toward one end again wants a new stated rule.

**Logs.** `mounted` now prints `multiplier=` (it used to print `scale=`, which read as the applied ratio and was not). `show` prints `zoneSize=<x,y,z> authored=<x,y,z> ratio=<n> multiplier=<1> emitters=<n>` in place of `depth=` — so the next report can say whether the ratio is right without a second round trip, and the ratio and its two inputs are on one line. The record keeps `ratio`, `zoneSize` and `extents` because `show` runs **after** the clone is scaled; reading `clone.Size` there would print the result as if it were the input.

**Two stale tuning pins were found by the test runs, and neither was caused by this round.** `powers.spec.ts` pinned `BALL_SPEED_DECAY_RATE` to `0.1` while the working tree has the designer at **5**; `apparent-spin.spec.ts` derived its expectation correctly but assumed the clamp was unreachable at `BALL_SPEED_MAX`, and the gain has moved to **3**, where `20 x 6 = 120` exceeds `APPARENT_SPIN_MAX_RAD_PER_SEC = 90`. Both are the same mistake — restating a designer's number instead of the rule — so both now assert the rule: the decay case asserts `rate > 0` and a finite `1 / rate` (a literal there failed on three consecutive retunes), and the spin case compares against `min(MAX, gain / BASE_BALL_RADIUS * speed)`, clamp included.

**Validation:** `npm run build` passed; `npm test` passed with **471 tests** across **34 files** (seven new `motion-blur` cases: three `extentAlong`, four `motionBlurFillRatio`; four `motionBlurAnchor` cases deleted with the function they pinned, and the three `motionBlurCloneFrame` cases re-derived to the centre); `npm run lint` exited 0 with the same **55** pre-existing Prettier warnings in `src/shared/ui/viewport.ts`; every touched file passes `prettier --check`; `\uXXXX` search under `src/` returned no matches; `flamework.build` unchanged.

**Studio-only:** whether a fill ratio around `262 / authoredSize` reads as haze or as an enormous blur — the ratio is logged, and particle `Size` and `Speed` scale with it, so a very small authored asset wants a bigger authored asset rather than a smaller multiplier; whether the overshoot past the zone's faces is acceptable (it is symmetric about the centre and was chosen over a gap); and whether 100-rate emitters at that scale are affordable, because the clone is one part with two emitters either way and only their size changed.

## 193. Chunky phase banner, an avatar on every body, and a spectate toggle for non-competitors

**Three independent parts, all three shipped.** Each was verified against source first; where a part could have been forced it was measured instead, and the two places the prompt's claims did not hold are named at the end.

### Part 1 -- the banner is a chunky panel

**`buildChunkyPanel`, not `applyChunkyChrome`, and that is not a preference.** `applyChunkyChrome(button: GuiButton, ...)` turns an existing **button** into a transparent hit area with the plates as its children; a readout has nothing to press and no cell to invert. The panel builder takes a parent and a size, which is exactly a fact display.

**The labels stay on big-ui `Text`, decided by the face colour.** Item 58's rule is that big-ui's ink comes from the dark HUD palette it was pushed, so it is legible on a **dark** face and invisible on a light one. The chunky face is `CHUNKY_PANEL_FACE` -- `rgb(52, 52, 58)` charcoal, reached through `chunkyDarkTheme().paint.panel`. Pale ink on charcoal is the pairing that works, so nothing about the labels, the variant or the `Computed` changed; `bannerText` is untouched and every display rule is still its own.

**`autoHeight` was one axis short, and that is the one thing the builder could not express.** That mode reports `Y` from the face's content and leaves `X` at the frame's scale -- right for a sheet, whose width is fixed, and wrong for a chip whose width is its text. The banner therefore sets `frame.AutomaticSize = XY`, `surface.Size = fromOffset(0, 0)` and `surface.AutomaticSize = XY` after building, and the builder's own `syncShadow` then tracks the resolved `Y` exactly as it does for the store. The frame keeps its `TopbarSafeInsets` layer and its one-resumption `AbsoluteSize` report.

**Drawn size, before and after (arithmetic, not measured).** Before: `size=95, 34` -- the last Studio run's `[PhaseBanner] mounted` line, label plus `SPACING.sm` padding. After: the **face** is the same `95 x 34`, because the padding and the label are unchanged; the frame reports `95 x 40` because the shadow plate is `6` taller than the face and the builder's own docblock records that the container grows by `CHUNKY_PANEL_STROKE`; and the painted extent is about `101 x 50` -- the face plus `3` pixels of centred stroke per edge, plus the plate's `10`-pixel offset down and right. The line now prints `size=` (frame) **and** `face=` (surface) so those two cannot be confused for one number.

**`UI_STYLE_GUIDE.md` 2.3 was rewritten in place.** It did not have a banner paragraph -- the claim lived only in item 122's report, which is the second correction below -- so the rule was added where the exemption had been implied: **a readout is a panel, not a control, and it is not exempt from the language**; the builder decides, not the input. Item 122's sentence was rewritten in the log too, since the prompt asked for that argument specifically: it now says the banner moved and the splash and wipe did not, with the reason.

### Part 2 -- every body wears a face

**The twin resolves its parent through a display-only attribute: `AvatarUserId`.** The prompt offered two routes and the honest answer is a third. `Remotes.DecoyOutline` was refused -- it is **owner-only by design** (item 79), and widening it would put two audiences on one channel: a per-viewer reply for the highlight, and a broadcast identity for the avatar, with the deception resting on a reader noticing which field is which. The other candidate, an attribute, is right, but the *source* is what makes it small: the server **already** computes the twin's parent identity at spawn (`identityOf(parent)` into `decoyIdentities`, item 129), so `spawnDecoy` writes that same id into `AvatarUserId` **before `Parent`**, beside the identity it copies.

**`OwnerUserId` was not used, and the twin still has none.** `OwnerUserId` is the field `getCompetitors()` filters on; writing it would make the fake a competitor and change the winner rule. `AvatarUserId` is a display key that **no rule reads** -- the tick loop, the powers and the winner check never see it -- and it is written **only on a twin**, because a real body's `OwnerUserId` is already the answer and a second copy would be a second place for one fact to drift. The client's rule is therefore `OwnerUserId ?? AvatarUserId`, asserted with literals in `shared/ball-avatar.spec.ts` including the both-present case (competition key wins) and the synthetic-owner case (`-1` draws nothing, so no web request is made for a debug ball).

**A client controller, cached per `UserId`, and nothing drawn on failure.** `BallAvatarController` watches `TAGS.ball`, resolves the id, and fetches `Players:GetUserThumbnailAsync(userId, HeadShot, Size48x48)` -- a **yielding web call**, which is why it is client-side and why it is never inside `updateBadge`. One request per distinct player per session: the `thumbnails` map caches **failures too**, so a player with an unavailable thumbnail is asked once rather than once per body per round, and the `[BallAvatar]` line names the user id once. A failure draws no billboard at all -- an `ImageLabel` pointed at `""` is the grey box the brief forbids.

**Offset and size are its own; the far cutoff is reused.** `POWER_BADGE_OFFSET_STUDS` is `14` and the badge is `20` **pixels** tall, so a same-offset avatar would sit inside the badge. `BALL_AVATAR_OFFSET_STUDS = 40` (**Placeholder.**) is `radius (10) + badge offset (14) + 16` of clearance, measured from the ball's centre with `body.Size.Y / 2` added -- the badge's own fix (a fixed number buried it at 20 studs) applies to the face for the same reason. `BALL_AVATAR_SIZE = 36` **pixels**, square because a `HeadShot` is. `MaxDistance` **reuses** `POWER_BADGE_MAX_DISTANCE`: that number is a fact about the arena's 377-stud diagonal rather than about badges, and two cutoffs would let the face cull while the name it sits above still draws.

**The red outline did not move.** `DecoyOutlineController` is untouched and stays owner-only. The face is identical on both bodies precisely because it must give nothing away; the highlight is the one thing that does.

### Part 3 -- spectate, for players who are not in the round

**The camera did already engage for non-competitors, exactly as the prompt suspected.** `isActive()` required a phase, a tagged part and a character -- a player with no ball has a character, so a spectator's camera was taken from `Waiting` to `PostGame` by the phase alone. That is why the button's `off` state could not have been true.

**So non-competitors are excluded from the automatic engage, and the cost is stated in the code.** `cameraWantsArena(phase, competing, spectating)` is `spectating || competing` inside the three arena phases; a competitor's behaviour is **byte-identical** to item 186 (the phase rule, the `Waiting` generation bump, the `CharacterRemoving` suppression), and a spectator now keeps their own camera until they press the button. The price: a non-competitor who never presses it watches from their character for the whole round, which is the point of offering the choice.

**The replicated fact is a `Player` attribute: `Competing`.** The scan for a body carrying my `OwnerUserId` was refused for three reasons: it is a walk of the tagged list on every phase change, it answers **no** during the window between the phase changing and the body replicating -- which is exactly when the camera decides -- and it answers no again for a player whose ball was eliminated, who must **keep** the arena camera they already have. `RoundService` writes `true` where a body is demonstrably spawned and `false` for every player in `clearAllBodies`, the one place a round's body set ends. **`Player:SetAttribute` reaches only that player**, so this is one write per competitor rather than a broadcast. On the client it is read once at boot and then watched with `GetAttributeChangedSignal`, which is what makes its timing irrelevant: the attribute may replicate before or after `RoundState` and either order re-runs `observe`.

**The toggle survives a phase change because it is a latch the phase rule reads, not a phase-keyed flag.** `TreadmillCameraController.setSpectating(on)` sets the flag and re-runs `observe`; `spectating` is written **only** there and by the button, so `Waiting -> Playing -> PostGame` re-evaluates the same answer. **`Stop spectating` restores through the existing branch** -- `observe`'s `if (this.engaged) restore(...)` -- so there is no second `CameraSubject`/`CameraType` copy. The latch is cleared by the button when this player becomes a competitor, because a racer watching their own ball from a fixed pose cannot play, and that case is reachable (a spectator who enrolls, or a debug spawn).

**The button is a chunky control in `hudCore`.** `applyChunkyChrome` is right here -- it is the one place in this round where a button is correct -- and the label comes back on the chrome so the two words are one assignment. `hudCore` (order 20) with the picker and the leaderboard rather than a new layer: a new `ScreenGui` would need a new integer in a chain the guide states as total, and this control never draws over a sheet or a wipe, so order 20 is correct for it. `spectateAvailable(phase, competing)` keeps it off screen for competitors and in `Intermission`, where every body has been cleared and there is nothing to watch.

### Where this prompt was wrong

1. **`UI_STYLE_GUIDE.md` had no banner paragraph.** The grep for "banner" in that file returned one hit, the layer table row. The "HUD palette on purpose" argument lived **only** in item 122's report, so there was nothing to rewrite there -- the guide needed the rule *added*. Both are now consistent.
2. **`buildChunkyPanel`'s `autoHeight` cannot express the banner's shape.** It reports `Y` and holds `X` at the frame's scale, which is right for a sheet and wrong for a chip; the banner had to set `AutomaticSize.XY` on the frame and the face after building. The prompt's premise -- "the panel builder, including its `autoHeight` mode" -- assumed that mode covered a shrink-wrapping overlay.
3. **The twin's identity was already reachable on the server**, which is what makes the attribute cheap: `ownerIdentityFor`/`decoyIdentities` (item 129) computes exactly the pair the avatar needs. The prompt framed the choice as "attribute on the twin" versus "widen the remote" without noting that the server already knows the answer and the attribute is a one-line copy.
4. **`POWER_BADGE_OFFSET_STUDS` is a reuse candidate only for the far cutoff.** Its `14` sits above the radius, and the badge is `20` **pixels** tall, so the avatar needs its own offset; only `POWER_BADGE_MAX_DISTANCE` transfers.

**Audit.** New: `client/controllers/ball-avatar-controller.ts`, `client/controllers/spectate-controller.ts`, `shared/ball-avatar.ts` (+ `.spec.ts`), `shared/spectate.ts` (+ `.spec.ts`). Changed: `client/controllers/phase-banner-controller.ts`, `client/controllers/treadmill-camera-controller.ts`, `server/services/ball-spawner-service.ts`, `server/services/round-service.ts`, `shared/attributes.ts`, `shared/tuning.ts`, `docs/powers-and-vfx.md` (3, badge, new avatar section), `UI_STYLE_GUIDE.md` (2.3, layer table), `HANDOFF.md` (item 122 rewritten in place). **`flamework.build` was regenerated** -- deleted with `out/tsconfig.tsbuildinfo`, never `rm -rf out` -- and the new controllers are registered at lines 5 and 30:
`"roblox-treadmill-race:out/client/controllers/ball-avatar-controller@BallAvatarController"` and
`"roblox-treadmill-race:out/client/controllers/spectate-controller@SpectateController"`.
Build exit 0; **`npm test` = 487 passed in 36 files** (16 new cases: 7 in `ball-avatar.spec.ts`, 9 in `spectate.spec.ts`; no existing test value changed); `npm run lint` 0 errors with the same 55 pre-existing `viewport.ts` warnings; every touched file passes `prettier --check`; `\uXXXX` search under `src/` is zero.

**Studio-only:** that the banner still reads at the top centre under the topbar and that its plate does not clip the glyphs; that a `36`-pixel face is legible above a 20-stud ball and clears the 20-pixel badge at the game camera's distance (the clearance is exact at one distance, by construction); that a twin's face is identical to its parent's while the owner still sees only the red outline; and that a spectator toggles the arena view off and back to their own character mid-round, including across a `Waiting -> Playing` change.

## 194. The banner had no text because the label was under the face; the spin log could not answer "which ball"

**Two reports from one Studio run. One is fixed outright, the other is a diagnosis the log could not make, and the reason it could not is itself a bug.**

### The banner's text was drawn *under* the panel

**Reported: "I don't see the text in round's status HUD."** The screenshot is a bare charcoal chip, and the log says the label is fine: `[PhaseBanner] mounted ... size=108, 34 face=95, 34 ... text="Intermission"`. A face measured at `95 x 34` is a face sized *by its label*, so the label existed, was parented and had text -- and was drawn underneath the plate.

**Cause: draw order.** `buildChunkyPanel` gives the face `zIndex + 1` (`2`), and big-ui's `Text` defaults its `ZIndex` to `1`. That is the identical defect item 122 fixed on the picker with `LABEL_Z_INDEX = 6` ("above the chrome's face at +1 ... or the labels would be covered by the very plates they sit on"). The banner set `AutomaticSize` through `Fusion.Hydrate` for the same class of reason -- a property big-ui does not expose -- and simply did not set this one.

**Fix: `BANNER_LABEL_Z_INDEX = 6`**, applied in the same `Hydrate` call as the parent and the auto-size. Not `2` or `3`: the value is the tree's existing label order, so the next element inserted between the face and the label has room. Nothing else about the banner moved.

### "A few balls not spinning" -- and why the log could not say which

**The model is `rateSource=phantom` whenever a body has a skin.** `BallRenderController` rolls the phantom from `apparentSpinRate(BALL_SPEED)`, and `marker-spin-controller` applies **no** rate on that path by design (a second rotation would double the drawn speed). So a ball does not turn exactly when its `BALL_SPEED` attribute is at or below `SPIN_DEADBAND_SPEED` -- and with the designer's decay now at **5**, a ball starting at `BALL_SPEED_START = 10` reaches the floor in about two seconds. A field where most bodies read `0` for most of a 76-second round is what the current model *means*, which is why the report is "a few" rather than "all": the `BALL_SPEED_START_VARIATION` bodies keep a positive speed longer.

**The log could not confirm that, and the reason is a diagnostic bug.** `STATE_LOG_LIMIT = 12` lines at one per second, counted from the first body -- but the countdown before `Playing` is **14.4 seconds** (`[Countdown] start ... startsIn=14.434s`), and the bodies exist for all of it with `BALL_SPEED=0`. **All twelve lines were spent on a parked field before the round started**, which is why the run has no sample from any frame in which a ball was actually racing.

**Fix: the budget re-arms when the race does.** The first frame any body reports a speed above the deadband resets `stateLogCount`, so the twelve lines are spent on a field that is moving. Latched on that observable rather than on the phase, so the controller needs no `RoundState` subscription.

**Fix: the line now describes the whole field, not one sampled body.** `spinning=n/total speeds=[...]` is appended to every sample: every live body's `BALL_SPEED` in map order, and how many are above the deadband -- which, under this model, *is* the set of bodies that turn. The previous line reported one body chosen by map order, so a run where one ball of eight did not spin could print eight good samples and never mention it.

**Fix: the "GAVE UP" watchdog no longer fires on a finished round.** It tested `trackedMarkers.size() === 0` alone, so it printed at 09:35:06 -- after `[Round] cleared 1 ball(s)` -- with `markers seen=0 tracked=0 ... Check the tag string and that the markers are children of a Ball-tagged body`, for a round in which discovery had worked perfectly and the markers had been tracked for 100 seconds. It now also requires `liveBallCount() > 0`, prints that count, and re-arms (`firstBallSeenAt = undefined`) whenever the field is empty, so a later round can warn for itself.

**Not changed:** the spin model itself. `rateSource=phantom`, `apparentSpinRate(BALL_SPEED)` and `SPIN_DEADBAND_SPEED` are untouched -- whether a ball *should* keep turning once `BALL_SPEED` is 0 is a design question (a ball holding station on a treadmill does not roll, which is the model's whole premise), and it wants the per-body line above to be answered from a real race rather than guessed at here.

**Validation:** `npm run build` exit 0; **`npm test` = 487 passed in 36 files** (no test changed -- both fixes are in code the Jest runtime cannot construct: a Fusion label's draw order and a `RenderStepped` log line); `npm run lint` 0 errors with the same 55 pre-existing `viewport.ts` warnings; both touched files pass `prettier --check`; `\uXXXX` search under `src/` is zero; `flamework.build` unchanged -- no controller added.

**Studio-only:** that the phase name now reads on the chip (and that the label is not clipped by the face's `UIStroke`); and, from the next round's `[MarkerSpin] state ... spinning=n/8 speeds=[...]` lines, whether the unspinning balls are the ones reading `BALL_SPEED=0` -- which would make "the ball should still roll while it travels" the next design decision rather than a defect.

## 195. Panel depth is gone: a panel is a surface, so it has no shadow plate

**Reported, with a screenshot: "there is no panel underneath to give it depth AND there's a black line at top right", and "remove the depth from non-buttons/interactables".** Both symptoms are one cause, and the ask is the right fix rather than a workaround.

**The cause, from the numbers already in the log.** `[PhaseBanner] mounted ... size=108, 34 face=95, 34`: the frame was **108** wide and the face **95**, a difference of exactly `CHUNKY_PANEL_DEPTH - CHUNKY_PANEL_STROKE/2 (7) + CHUNKY_PANEL_STROKE (6)`. That is the shadow plate. It was an **offset sibling** nudged `(7, 7)` down and right, and the container was `AutomaticSize` -- so the container *measured* the plate, grew to include it, and the face stopped being the container's own box. The plate's height was then clipped by that measurement, which is why what survived was a **short horizontal bar at the top right** of the chip instead of a band down two edges, and why on a 34-pixel chip nothing else read as depth at all. "No plate under it" and "a black line at the corner" are the same broken plate seen from two sides.

**Items 122 and 123 had each already spent a round on a variant of this** -- a square plate under a rounded face, then a pale corner that was never the shadow. Three fixes to one cosmetic plate is the signal: the plate is the defect. **A panel is a surface, not an object sitting on another one**, and depth belongs only to things you press -- where the box is a **fixed layout cell** and the face is inset *inside* it, a shape with no overhang and no measurement feedback.

**`buildChunkyPanel` now returns one face.** `CHUNKY_PANEL_DEPTH` and `CHUNKY_PANEL_SHADOW` are **deleted**, not zeroed (this tree removes inert values); the `shadowColor` option, the `shadow` field on `ChunkyPanel`, the `halfStroke` arithmetic and `syncShadow` are gone with them. The builder keeps what is left of the language: `CHUNKY_PANEL_FACE` charcoal, `CHUNKY_PANEL_STROKE` outline, `CHUNKY_PANEL_CORNER` radius, `autoHeight`, `clipsDescendants` and `zIndex`. The frame is now **exactly the face's box**, which is the invariant the plate broke.

**Every panel caller is unbroken by construction; two had to drop a fade.** The payout sheet and the reward toast each drove the plate's `BackgroundTransparency` from the same `NumberValue` that fades the face, and both now drive the face alone -- one layer cannot drift from another that no longer exists. The toast also dropped `panel.shadow.Active = false`. The store, the inventory, the picker, the leaderboard and the phase banner needed nothing: they only read `frame` and `surface`. **`applyChunkyChrome`, `buildChunkyButton` and `buildChunkyTabs` are untouched** -- every control keeps its shadow strip, its `setRaised` pressed state and its `shadowOf` tint, because a control's cell is fixed by its layout and the inset has nothing to measure.

**The banner's two size fields will now agree.** `[PhaseBanner] mounted size=<frame> face=<surface>` printed 108 x 34 against 95 x 34 in the run that reported this; with no offset plate they are the same box, and the pair stays in the line so a future plate would show up as a disagreement rather than as a geometry bug.

**Docs rewritten in place, not appended to.** `UI_STYLE_GUIDE.md` §1 now states two anatomies with the single question that picks between them ("can you press it?"), §1.1's depth table drops the panel row and says so, **§1.2b was replaced** -- it used to argue at length for the offset sibling, complete with the two bugs it thought it was fixing, and now records why the sibling itself was the third bug -- §1.3 no longer claims "both plates" for panels, §5.5 gains the one sentence that stops this section being read as a reason to give a sheet a plate, and the §7 checklist asks for "no panel has a shadow plate at all". `chunky-chrome.ts`'s `CHUNKY_CONTROL_DEPTH` docblock loses its reference to the deleted constant and says depth is a control cue now.

**What is lost, stated plainly:** sheets no longer read as cards raised off the screen. They read as flat charcoal panels with a thick near-black outline and a rounded corner -- the same silhouette as the rest of the UI, which is the look the report asked for. If a sheet later needs to separate itself from a busy background, the lever is the **outline**, not a plate: `CHUNKY_PANEL_STROKE` is now doing the job the plate used to do, and its docblock says so.

**Validation:** `npm run build` exit 0; **`npm test` = 487 passed in 36 files** (no test changed -- the builder is not constructible in the Jest runtime, and no spec asserted a palate); `npm run lint` 0 errors with the same 55 pre-existing `viewport.ts` warnings; all five touched files pass `prettier --check`; `\uXXXX` search under `src/` is zero; `flamework.build` unchanged -- no controller added or removed.

**Studio-only:** that the store, the inventory, the picker, the payout, the toast and the banner all read as a deliberate flat panel rather than as "the shadow failed to draw", and that the chip's black top-right line is gone (it should be: there is no plate left to leak).

## 196. Spin is base-plus-speed and only inside `Playing`; the `Waiting` drift was already fixed and the log field that hid it is renamed

**Four parts, three of them shipped as asked and one of them not done at all, because it was already done.** The last part is the interesting one: the report's evidence is a diagnostic field that measures nothing.

### Parts 1-2 -- the rate, and the numbers before and after

**The formula before this round was `min(90, APPARENT_SPIN_GAIN x speed / BASE_BALL_RADIUS)` above a `0.5` deadband, else `0`.** With `APPARENT_SPIN_GAIN = 3` (not `1` -- the docblock had been stale since item 187) and `BASE_BALL_RADIUS = 0.5` that is `min(90, 6 x speed)`, so the anchor was **not** being met: the rate at `BALL_SPEED = 10` was **`60 rad/s`**, which is `9.5` rev/s and **`57` degrees of rotation per frame** at 60 Hz -- the aliasing fold the gain of `3` was rolled back for twice. The prompt's "20 rad/s is the approved rate" was right about the *intent* and wrong about the code.

| `BALL_SPEED` | before (gain `3`) | after (base `10` + gain `0.5`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `0` | **0** -- the sliding-ball bug | **10** |
| `10` | 60 (aliased) | **20** -- the approved anchor |
| `20` | 90 (clamped) | **30** |
| rocket `18` | 90 (clamped) | 28 |
| `BALL_SPEED_MAX = 50` | 90 (clamped) | 60 (aliased) |

**The split is `SPIN_BASE_RAD_PER_SEC = 10` and `APPARENT_SPIN_GAIN = 0.5`**, and that choice makes the whole thing `10 + BALL_SPEED` -- one number a reader can hold. `10` is half the spawn rate: a sliding ball reads as rolling (about `1.6` rev/s), and a ball at full `BALL_SPEED_START` still reads as the fastest thing on screen, so the two states are distinguishable at a glance. The gain had to come down from `1` because the base is carrying part of the total; **the no-slip argument that produced `1` is about the speed-following term only and does not survive a constant term**, which is stated in the constant's docblock rather than quietly dropped.

**`SPIN_DEADBAND_SPEED` is deleted, and it had a second reader.** It was not only the spin path: `writeTailWind` gated the trail on `speed > SPIN_DEADBAND_SPEED`. That use is now `TAIL_WIND_MIN_BALL_SPEED` (same `0.5`, its own name and its own docblock): a trail is about the ball losing ground in the *world*, a roll is about the ball meeting the *floor*, and the two coinciding was an accident of the old formula. Two retunes that had to move together were one retune that could move alone.

### Part 3 -- the phase gate, and the frame holds

Both controllers read `ReplicatedStorage.RoundState` once at `onStart` and subscribe — the same `StringValue` `RoundStateController` prints, read the way `decoy-outline-controller` and the camera already read it, so there is no second source. `BallRenderController` gains a `phase` field and skips the accumulation when it is not `Playing`; `MarkerSpinController` gains the same latch for its fallback path.

**The phantom's frame holds, it does not reset**, and that is the right answer: a ball frozen on a stopped belt has no canonical facing, so snapping to the identity would rotate the texture by up to a quarter turn at `PostGame` entry and again at the next `Playing` — two visible jumps carrying no information. The accumulator is this controller's own state, and nothing about a phase change invalidates a rotation. The position is still copied every frame, so a body spawned into `Waiting` is drawn where it is.

### Part 4 -- what the log says now

`rateSource` reads **`phase`** outside `Playing` (it used to read `deadband`, which described a speed condition that no longer exists). `omegaVisual` reports `0` there — because the skin *is* applying zero, not because the field is empty — and reports `SPIN_BASE_RAD_PER_SEC` at `BALL_SPEED = 0` **during `Playing`**, which is the field finally answering the question it looks like it answers.

### Part 5 -- the body was already not drifting, and the field that said otherwise is renamed

**`stepBallSpeeds`' first line is already `if (!this.roundActive) { return; }`** — every write in the method (along-belt velocity, sway, `tickDelta`, `writeBoosted`, `writeTailWind`) is behind it, and `enterWaiting` sets the flag **`false`**, with a docblock that reads *"Not `true` any more … the flag is now set in `enterPlaying` and nowhere else"*. That is exactly the bug the prompt describes, and it was fixed in an earlier round.

**The `RELATIVE_SPEED = -10` in the report is `ballSpeed - beltSpeed`, an arithmetic field, not motion.** It reads `-10` on a body that is not moving because `BALL_SPEED` is `0` and the belt reference is `10`; it is the velocity the model *would* write if it ran. The same run's `velocity=` field is the measurement, and it settles it:

```
t=0.395  velocity=(-0, 33.036, 0.012)     <- bouncing, along-belt 0.012
t=0.931  velocity=(-0, 15.61,  0.019)
t=1.480  velocity=(-0, -12.407, 0.025)
t=3.646  velocity=(0, 0, 0)                <- and stays exactly zero for 13 s of Waiting
t=17.878 velocity=(-15.658, -0.001, 9.291) <- the model, after Waiting -> Playing
```

So **no change was made to the gate** — writing one would have been a second, redundant guard, and the tempting "zero the along-belt component instead" is a *bug*: `setRoundActive(false)` zeroes `BALL_SPEED`, and the write is `right x -(BALL_SPEED - BELT_SPEED)`, so a zero write produces `+10` toward the exit. That arithmetic is now in `stepBallSpeeds`' docblock, because it is the trap.

**What was fixed is the field that hid this.** The sample line now prints `along=` (the body's own velocity projected on the belt axis), `MODEL_RELATIVE=` (the old number, honestly named) and `roundActive=`. And the docblock's axis paragraph — which claimed "along-belt is world `X`, and in this scene the belt's `RightVector` is `+X`" — is rewritten: this scene's `RightVector` is `(0, 0, -1)`, an earlier fixture ran along `+X`, and that stale sentence is why the `-10` looked like along-belt drift to a reader comparing it with `velocity.X`.

**Item 46 did not regress:** `setRoundActive(true)` still seeds each ball's own `startSpeeds` value at `Playing` entry, and it runs before the first `stepBallSpeeds` tick, so the first `RELATIVE_SPEED` computed is `BALL_SPEED_START - BELT_SPEED = 0`. Unchanged, and the new `roundActive=` field in the sample line now shows the flag the seeding depends on.

### Where this prompt was wrong

1. **`APPARENT_SPIN_GAIN` was `3`, not `1`, so the "approved 20 rad/s anchor" was not what the code did.** It drew `60` at spawn speed — the documented aliasing regime — and `90` (clamped) at every speed from `15` up. The prompt asked to preserve a number the build had already left behind; this round lands the anchor properly instead.
2. **`BALL_SPEED_MAX` is `50`, not `20`.** The rate cannot stay under the `~31 rad/s` fold across the whole range while holding `20` at speed `10` — `10 + 50 = 60`. The spec asserts the band for the range the race actually occupies (start, decay, a rocket's `18`) and *asserts the failure* at `SPRINTER_BOOST_SPEED` and the ceiling rather than pretending otherwise.
3. **Part 5's premise is false: the inactive path did not write at all, and did not go through a different branch.** `if (!this.roundActive) return;` is the first line of `stepBallSpeeds` and `enterWaiting` passes `false`. The "drift" was a diagnostic arithmetic field; the body's measured along-belt velocity was `0.012` and then exactly `0`.
4. **`SPIN_DEADBAND_SPEED` was not dead** — `writeTailWind` read it. Deleting it required its own constant, not just a deletion.
5. **The axis docblock was stale in a way that caused a misdiagnosis:** it said along-belt is world `X` and `RightVector` is `+X`, for a belt that runs along world `-Z`.

### Decisions

1. **Current → new at 0 / 10 / 20:** `0 → 10`, `60 → 20`, `90 (clamped) → 30`. Anchor `20` at `BALL_SPEED = 10` now holds for the first time.
2. **Split `BASE = 10`, `GAIN = 0.5`**, making the rate `10 + BALL_SPEED`: half the total fixed so a sliding ball rolls, half following the attribute so a fast ball reads faster, and the sum is one number to hold.
3. **The gate lives in both render controllers**, reading the same `RoundState`; the phantom **holds** its accumulated frame across the pause.
4. **`rateSource = "phase"`** outside `Playing`; `omegaVisual` is `0` there and `SPIN_BASE_RAD_PER_SEC` at `BALL_SPEED = 0` inside it.

## 198. The `Waiting` slide was the landing, not the model — bodies are held horizontally while the round is inactive

**Reported for the third time: "still sliding in `Waiting`."** Item 197's client probe paid off: it measured the slide, and it is neither the model nor the phantom.

### What the probe measured

```
10:34:48.903  probe phase=Waiting  ballDelta=0  phantomDelta=0  drift=0     (all 8 bodies)
10:34:49.904  probe phase=Waiting  ballDelta=2.792  phantomDelta=2.792  drift=0
              ballDelta=5.266 / 5.892 / 3.058 / 1.748 / 5.763 / 4.264 / 3.157
10:34:50.608  spin-probe  |v|=6.605  BALL_SPEED=5.052     |v|=3.867  BALL_SPEED=3.612
```

Four of eight bodies moved **1.0-2.1 studs in world `Z`** — the along-belt axis on this belt — in the second after spawning, and `spin-probe` still read `|v| = 6.605` two seconds in. Then they stop, and stay stopped: item 197's sample line shows one body's position frozen to a thousandth for 27 seconds.

**So `stepBallSpeeds`' gate was working and irrelevant.** The bodies are spawned a few studs **above** the invisible floor slab and fall onto it during `Waiting`; the landing itself pushed them along the belt. `phantomDelta` equalled `ballDelta` and `drift=0` on every line, so the client was drawing exactly what the server had — the picture was honest and the physics was the problem.

### The fix

`stepBallSpeeds`' inactive branch now calls **`holdBodies()`** instead of returning immediately. It removes the **horizontal** component of each body's velocity — along `RightVector` and along `right x up` — and writes nothing else.

- **`Y` is untouched**, so gravity still pulls a body down and one spawned into `Waiting` still *lands* rather than hanging. That is the difference between this and a freeze: an `Anchored` toggle would be a second thing to get wrong on every death path.
- **It is not a second model.** No `relative`, no decay, no sway — and therefore it cannot reproduce the trap the file documents: `right x -(BALL_SPEED - BELT_SPEED)` with a zeroed attribute is `+10` toward the exit, while writing **nothing along the belt** is the only expression of "not moving".
- **It costs nothing after the first couple of seconds.** A settled body's horizontal velocity is contact noise (`~0.003`), below `HOLD_VELOCITY_EPSILON = 1e-3` — note the threshold is *tighter* than the noise, so the loop keeps writing for a moment longer than strictly necessary and then stops. It early-outs per body, and after settling writes no properties at all.
- **One line per inactive stretch:** `[Spawner] hold engaged: N body/bodies had horizontal velocity with the round inactive`. That is the measurement that says how many bodies were sliding, so the next run either shows it caught them or shows it caught none.

**Why the model gate stays exactly as it was:** it is still the right rule, and the hold is additive. `setRoundActive(true)` still seeds each ball's `startSpeeds` value before the first tick, so `Playing` entry is still neutral (`RELATIVE_SPEED ≈ 0`) — item 46 is unaffected by a branch that only runs when the round is inactive.

### Where the prompt's (and my) reasoning was wrong

1. **"The write must be gated on the round being active"** — it already was, and had been for two rounds. The movement was never the model's.
2. **"A body with `BALL_SPEED = 0` during `Waiting` has zero along-belt velocity"** — true of the *model's* contribution and false of the body: the body had up to 5 studs/s of along-belt velocity from the landing. Acceptance criterion 4 needed a hold, not a gate.
3. **My own item 196 report generalised from one sampled body** and declared `Waiting` clean. Item 197's probe measured all eight, which is how this was found; the lesson is that "the sampled body is still" is not "the field is still".

**Validation:** `npm run build` exit 0; **`npm test` = 491 passed in 36 files** (nothing to add — the hold lives in a `DataModel` service and its behaviour is measured by the two log lines); `npm run lint` 0 errors with the same 55 pre-existing `viewport.ts` warnings; both touched files pass `prettier --check`; `\uXXXX` search under `src/` is zero; `flamework.build` unchanged.

**The probe stays for one more round.** `[BallRender] probe` is still in `ball-render-controller` (capped at 16 lines) purely to confirm the fix from the client side: after this change its `ballDelta` should read `0` from the first sample onward. It gets deleted once the report stops.

**Studio-only:** that the field sits still through `Waiting` — including the first two seconds, which is where the slide was — and that the `hold engaged` line appears once per lobby with a body count.

## 199. The placement bound is derived from the largest drawn radius -- and the disc already fits, which the prompt's premise did not

**Reported: "place pickups so the painted disc stays entirely on the belt."** The work is done, but the premise is a snapshot of the build before item 190: the log quoted in the prompt (`bounds=x[-156.5,156.5]`, a `40`-stud disc radius) predates the round that made the disc the collider's inscribed circle. The current log proves it — `[PickupSprite] first visuals ... pad=20x20x20 ring=20 studs`.

### Part 1 -- the three radii, from source

| thing | expression | studs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| pad half-width | `PICKUP_SIZE.X / 2` | **10** |
| disc radius | `pickupDiscDiameter(padSize) / 2`, i.e. `math.min(padSize.X, padSize.Z) / 2` -- **no multiplier** (item 190) | **10** |
| sprite half-width | `PICKUP_SPRITE_STUDS * effectScaleForRadius(poolBallRadius(), PICKUP_SCALE_MULTIPLIER) / 2` = `2.6 * (10 / 0.5 * 0.2) / 2` = `2.6 * 4 / 2` | **5.2** |

**The largest is the pad's own half-width**, and the disc ties it rather than exceeding it. `PICKUP_SCALE_MULTIPLIER` is **`0.2`**, and it sizes the sprite only.

### Part 2 -- the derived bound

`pickupBounds(beltSize, padSize, drawRadius)` now subtracts `math.max(padSize.X / 2, drawRadius)` per axis, and the caller passes `pickupDrawRadius(PICKUP_SIZE, PICKUP_SCALE_MULTIPLIER)` -- a new pure function in `pickup.config.ts` that takes the **max** of the three radii above, computed from `PICKUP_SIZE`, `PICKUP_SPRITE_STUDS`, `poolBallRadius()` and the multiplier. No literal.

**On the shipped scene the region does not move**, and that is the honest result rather than a failure:

```
before  bounds=x[-156.5,156.5] z[-76.5,76.5]        (belt 333 x 173, pad half-width 10)
after   bounds=x[-156.5,156.5] z[-76.5,76.5] drawRadius=10
```

The arithmetic that shows a pad at the new maximum still fits: `156.5 + 10 = 166.5`, exactly the belt's half-extent, in both axes. The user's own log has `positions=...|144.448,76.379` and `z=76.379 + 10 = 86.379` against a `86.5` half-extent -- inside, by `0.12`.

**What the derivation buys is the next retune.** At `PICKUP_SCALE_MULTIPLIER = 1` the sprite would draw `52` studs across, a `26`-stud radius, and the bound would tighten to `166.5 - 26 = 140.5` on its own. Before this round it would have stayed at `156.5` and painted a sprite past the edge with no code change anywhere. `pickup.config.spec.ts` asserts both the shipped equality and that case.

### Part 3 -- the log field

`[Pickup] spawned` and the shortfall warning both carry `drawRadius=<n>` beside `bounds=`, so the number the bound was derived from is visible next to the region it produced. Without it, `bounds=` alone cannot distinguish "the pad's radius" from "the sprite's" after a retune.

### Part 4 -- what this does not fix, recorded in the disc's own docblock

**The disc still overhangs the collider on a non-square pad**, and the earlier round's finding stands: a ball whose centre is inside the ring but outside the pad's box does not collect. That is deliberately out of scope -- the designer chose to keep the large disc and constrain placement. `pickupDiscDiameter`'s docblock now says so and says **not** to make the picture consistent by shrinking the disc: the collider is the gameplay value, and a disc smaller than the box would understate the reach a ball actually has.

### Decisions

1. **Radii: 10 / 10 / 5.2**, largest is the pad's half-width (the disc ties it).
2. **`drawRadius` = `pickupDrawRadius(PICKUP_SIZE, PICKUP_SCALE_MULTIPLIER)`, subtracted as `max(padHalf, drawRadius)` per axis.** Region unchanged at `x[+-156.5] z[+-76.5]`, `drawRadius=10`.
3. **The overlap test stays on the pad's box, and that is now provably sufficient**: the disc is the pad's *inscribed* circle, so it can never exceed the box -- two discs that clear each other imply two boxes that do. If a future retune made the sprite wider than the pad the *bound* would tighten but the overlap test would not, and that is the case to revisit; it is named in the report rather than pre-solved.
4. **If the region ever cannot hold `PICKUP_MAX_COUNT`**: nothing new. `PICKUP_PLACEMENT_ATTEMPTS` bounds the draw per pad, and a shortfall already warns with `placed/requested/unplaced`, `attemptsPerPad`, `bounds=` and `drawRadius=` and retries at the 15 s top-up. The region would have to shrink below about `4 x 3` pad cells (`12` pads on a `313 x 153` band is ~`105` cells today) before that fires.

### Where this prompt was wrong

1. **The disc does not exceed the collider, and has not since item 190.** The `40`-stud radius in the quoted log is from the build where the disc took the multiplier; the current log reads `ring=20` on a `20`-stud pad, and the sprite is half the pad.
2. **The overlap test needs no disc radius**, for the reason above: the disc is inscribed, so `discs disjoint => boxes disjoint`. It would only matter if the sprite were ever the largest, and then the bound -- not the overlap rule -- is what breaks first.
3. **The region still fits the pad count comfortably**, so the "what if it is too small" concern is real but not current: `12` pads on `~105` packable cells.

**Validation:** `npm run build` exit 0; **`npm test` = 497 passed in 36 files** (six new cases: two on `pickupBounds` with a drawn radius, four on `pickupDrawRadius`; eight existing `pickupBounds` call sites now pass the radius explicitly); `npm run lint` 0 errors with the same 55 pre-existing `viewport.ts` warnings; all five touched files pass `prettier --check`; `\uXXXX` search under `src/` is zero; `flamework.build` unchanged.

**Studio-only:** that no pad's painted disc crosses the belt edge at any placement (it should not have been crossing since item 190 either), that pads still spread across the belt, and that `[Pickup] spawned` reads `placed=12 requested=12 ... drawRadius=10`.

## 200 -- The spin ceiling was the bug: `90 rad/s` is `86` degrees per frame, so boosted balls read as still

**Reported symptom:** "same issue" -- balls that do not appear to spin, and balls that appear to slide. Item 199 verified every pickup pad fitted the belt, so placement was not the cause. The log was.

### The evidence, straight out of the log

Every ball in the field at once, in `Playing`, from the single `[MarkerSpin]` field summary (fields elided):

```
[MarkerSpin] ... BALL_SPEED=79.95 ... omegaVisual=89.95 ... spinning=9/9 speeds=[79.95,79.95,79.95,...]
```

`BALL_SPEED = 79.95` is `BOOST_TARGET_BALL_SPEED = 80` arriving through the pickup boost, and `omegaVisual = 89.95` is
`SPIN_BASE_RAD_PER_SEC (10) + 79.95` **landing exactly on `APPARENT_SPIN_MAX_RAD_PER_SEC = 90`** -- `spinning=9/9` is the
count of bodies that *have* a marker and a non-zero rate, and it was `9/9` while the designer reported balls that were not
turning. That is the tell: the rate was non-zero and unreadable, not missing. The clamp was not a safety net any more; it
was the operating point of every boosted ball.

### Why `90 rad/s` is invisible

`90 rad/s` is `14.3` revolutions per second. At 60 frames a second that is **`1.5` radians = `86` degrees of rotation
between consecutive frames**. A sphere carrying six face textures is symmetric every `90` degrees, so once consecutive
frames land more than **`45`** degrees apart there is no frame-to-frame correspondence to recover direction from: the eye
resolves the ball as **still**, or as turning backwards. **That is the long-running "a few balls do not spin" report** --
and it tracked boosted balls specifically, which is exactly why it read as "a few" rather than "all".

The docblock on the ceiling had *argued for* this: it said the clamp "does not police legibility, deliberately", on the
reasoning that clamping would make a fast ball stop turning while it kept moving. The reasoning was sound when the gain was
`1` and nothing could reach the clamp. Two retunes later -- `BOOST_TARGET_BALL_SPEED = 80` and the base-plus-speed split --
every boosted ball sat on it, and the alternative the docblock feared (a clamped ball) is what the *fold itself* was already
producing, with none of the readability.

### The change

`src/shared/tuning.ts`: `APPARENT_SPIN_MAX_RAD_PER_SEC` **`90` -> `31`**. That is `29.6` degrees per frame at 60 Hz, comfortably
inside the `45`-degree limit, and `4.9` revolutions a second -- fast, obviously rolling, unambiguous. It is the number this
tree's prose has used since item 187 to describe where the fold starts, so the ceiling is now stated at the point the prose
already named.

**The formula is unchanged** -- `min(MAX, SPIN_BASE_RAD_PER_SEC + GAIN * speed / BASE_BALL_RADIUS)` = `min(31, 10 + speed)`:

| `BALL_SPEED` | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `0` | `10` | `10` |
| `10` (spawn) | `20` | `20` |
| `18` (rocket) | `28` | `28` |
| `21` | `31` | `31` (clamp binds from here up) |
| `30` (sprinter) | `40` | **`31`** |
| `79.95` (boosted) | **`89.95`** | **`31`** |
| `100` (`BALL_SPEED_MAX`) | `90` (clamped) | **`31`** |

The anchor is preserved: **`20 rad/s` at `BALL_SPEED = 10`**, untouched. Above `21` the drawn rate stops following the
attribute, and that is the deliberate trade recorded in the constant's docblock: a slower, readable roll is a smaller lie
about speed than an unreadable one, because the whole purpose of this rate is to say "it is rolling". `BELT_TEXTURE_SCROLL_MULTIPLIER`
still owns "how fast the world looks".

### Docblocks rewritten in place

- `APPARENT_SPIN_MAX_RAD_PER_SEC` -- the "does not police legibility" argument is **reversed**, with the arithmetic that
  reversed it (`86` degrees a frame against a `90`-degree symmetry period) and the cost stated.
- `apparentSpinRate` -- new section naming the bug: the clamp used to be documented as a guard against `inf`, and the log
  shows it clamping nine bodies at once instead.
- `APPARENT_SPIN_GAIN` -- the "above 21 the rate is inside the fold, stated rather than hidden" paragraph is replaced: above
  `21` the rate now binds on the ceiling, and the section says why accepting the fold produced a frozen-looking field.

### Spec

`apparent-spin.spec.ts` gained the case that would have caught this: **every speed the model can produce is inside the
legible band**, asserted at `BALL_SPEED_START`, `SPRINTER_BOOST_SPEED`, `BALL_SPEED_MAX` and `1000`, plus a derived check
that `math.deg(MAX / 60) < 45` -- the ceiling itself, in degrees per frame, against the symmetry half-period rather than
against a pinned literal. It replaced the case that asserted the opposite (`> 31` at both boosted speeds).

**Validation:** `npm run build` exit 0; **`npm test` = 497 passed in 36 files**; `npm run lint` 0 errors with the same 55
pre-existing `viewport.ts` warnings; all three touched files pass `prettier --check`; `\uXXXX` search under `src/` is zero;
`flamework.build` unchanged.

**Studio-only:** that a boosted ball now visibly rolls instead of reading as still or backwards; that a ball at spawn
(`10`) is unchanged from item 196; and that the roll slowing between `21` and its boosted maximum is not distracting.

**Not in scope, still open:** the pickup sprite fails to load (`rbxassetid://135266450823195`,
`AssetFetchStatus.Failure`) so a pad draws only its ring; `[Pickup] collected ... power=recycle ... consumed=no` repeats at
frame rate while a ball rests on a recycle pad; balls knocked sideways off the belt in `Playing`
(`left belt side=-Z overshoot=2.244`); `BALL_SPEED_MAX == SPRINTER_BOOST_SPEED == 100` leaves the sprinter no headroom.

## 200. `ring=20` was a DIAMETER -- the pads were never off the belt; the log field was ambiguous, and the spin ceiling was the real `90`

**Reported: "pads are off the belt, `drawRadius=10` must be wrong."** It is not. The prompt's own arithmetic (`74.255 + 20 = 94.255`) assumed `ring=20 studs` was a **radius**; it is a **diameter**, so the disc radius is `10`, `drawRadius=10` is correct, and every pad in the reported run was inside the belt.

### The evidence, from the log in the prompt

`[PickupSprite] first visuals ... pad=20x20x20 ring=20 studs`: `buildFootprint` sets `ring.Size = Vector3(RING_THICKNESS_STUDS, diameter, diameter)` with `diameter = pickupDiscDiameter(padSize) = min(20, 20) = 20`, and `FootprintInfo.diameter` is documented as *"the ring's diameter"*. Diameter 20 -> **radius 10**.

Every one of the twelve placements, against `x +-156.5 z +-76.5`:

```
localX=  58.208 localZ=  46.209   zslack=30.291
localX= -98.484 localZ= -64.728   zslack=11.772
localX=-144.276 localZ=  61.299   zslack=15.201
localX= -82.672 localZ=  74.255   zslack= 2.245   <- the tightest, and the one the report used
...  all inside
```

The tightest pad's disc reaches `74.255 + 10 = 84.255` against an `86.5` half-extent: **2.245 studs inside**. `74.255 + 20` would have been over the edge, which is exactly the misreading.

### Part 1 -- the three radii, from source

| element | expression | studs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| pad collider half-width | `math.min(PICKUP_SIZE.X, PICKUP_SIZE.Z) / 2` | **10** |
| disc radius | `pickupDiscDiameter(padSize) / 2` = `min(X, Z) / 2` (no multiplier, item 190) | **10** |
| sprite half-width | `PICKUP_SPRITE_STUDS * effectScaleForRadius(poolBallRadius(), 0.2) / 2` = `2.6 * 4 / 2` | **5.2** |

Largest: the pad's half-width, tied by the disc. `drawRadius=10` **equals** it. `PICKUP_SCALE_MULTIPLIER` is **`0.2`** and sizes the sprite only.

### Part 2 and 3 -- the useful work: the log can no longer be misread

The bound was already right (item 199 derives it from the largest drawn radius), so **the region does not change**: `belt=333x173 bounds=x[-156.5,156.5] z[-76.5,76.5] drawRadius=10`. What changed is that a reader can now check it:

- **`ringDiameter=` and `ringRadius=`** replace `ring=`. A field that does not say which invites exactly the off-by-two that caused this round.
- **`spriteAuthored=` / `spriteWidth=` / `spriteRadius=`** replace `sprite=` alone, with `drawn=` kept as the **rendered pixel** size and now visibly a different measurement. `drawn=19.2px` and `sprite=2.6 studs` sat on one line under one word and had nothing to do with each other.
- **`belt=<x>x<z>`** added to `[Pickup] spawned` and the shortfall warning, so `bounds=` and its two inputs (`belt / 2 - drawRadius`) are on one line. A belt resized after `[Treadmill] bind` is now visible here rather than inferred.
- The belt's bind-log size is `size=(333, 0.1, 173)` and the bound is `333/2 - 10 = 156.5` and `173/2 - 10 = 76.5` on the same run -- **the spawn-time size matches the bind log**, so `positionFor` is not reading a stale size.

Two new spec cases pin the fit with literals: a pad at the corner of the region has its disc **flush** with the belt edge (`bound + discRadius == half-extent`, both axes), and the tightest real placement (`localZ=74.255`) leaves `2.245` studs.

### The real `90` in this tree, and it was not `drawRadius`

A spin spec added to the tree asserts the drawn rate must stay inside the aliasing fold at every speed, and it failed:

```
FAIL apparentSpinRate > holds every drawn rate inside the legible band, at any speed (item 200)
  expect(math.deg(APPARENT_SPIN_MAX_RAD_PER_SEC / 60) < 45)  ->  false   (90/60 rad = 86 degrees per frame)
```

**`APPARENT_SPIN_MAX_RAD_PER_SEC` was `90`,** described in its own docblock as "a safety net, not a rate" and justified by a comparison that has since inverted: with `BOOST_TARGET_BALL_SPEED = 80` the rate is `10 + 80 = 90`, which is **86 degrees of rotation per frame** — past the 45-degree half-period of a six-face sphere, where the eye resolves the ball as *not turning at all*. That is the "balls do not spin" report, arriving from the other end. The ceiling is now **`31` rad/s** (`29.6` degrees per frame), and a boosted ball clamps there instead of aliasing. The docblock is rewritten in place: it argued for the old value twice, and both arguments are answered.

**One dead import was removed** (`ROCKET_TARGET_SPEED`) that the new spec left unused -- a lint error, not a behaviour change.

### Decisions

1. **Radii 10 / 10 / 5.2**, largest is the pad's half-width; `drawRadius=10` matches it exactly.
2. **Neither was wrong: `drawRadius=10` under-reports nothing, and the disc is not 20 radius.** The *log field* was wrong -- ambiguous about diameter versus radius, and it is now explicit.
3. **Bound unchanged:** `x[+-156.5] z[+-76.5]` on a `333x173` belt, `drawRadius=10`. A pad at the bound is flush with the edge, never past it.
4. **The belt's spawn-time size matches its bind log** (`333x173` both), so there is no stale-size bug. The new `belt=` field makes that checkable in one line from now on.

## 201 - A visible margin between the painted disc and the belt edge, and the bound's result on the log line

**Reported:** "Cmon dude. Same issue still", with a screenshot showing pads sitting hard against the far edge of the belt.

**The arithmetic said the pads were already inside, and it was right.** Item 200 proved `ring=20` is a *diameter*, so the disc's radius is `10` -- the same as the pad's half-width -- and the tightest placement in the previous log was `localZ=74.255`, drawing its paint to `84.255` against an `86.5` edge: **2.2 studs of belt**. Nothing crossed.

**A pad cannot look wrong there, though.** At the bound the disc is *tangent* to the edge -- `86.5 - 10 = 76.5`, and a pad placed at `76.5` reaches exactly `86.5`. Zero clearance is the largest legal placement and it is **visually indistinguishable from overhang**: there is no belt between the paint and the drop, so the disc appears to be hanging over it. The bug was in the *rule's* choice of extremum, not in its arithmetic. Two rounds were spent proving the pads were inside a region that puts them flush.

### The change

`PICKUP_EDGE_MARGIN = 12` (**Placeholder.**), subtracted in addition to the drawn radius:

```ts
const drawRadius = pickupDrawRadius(PICKUP_SIZE, PICKUP_SCALE_MULTIPLIER);
const bounds = pickupBounds(belt.Size, PICKUP_SIZE, drawRadius + PICKUP_EDGE_MARGIN);
```

`pickupBounds` is untouched -- it already subtracts whatever reach it is handed, so the margin is the caller's decision and the pure geometry keeps one job. **The new region on the scene's `333 x 173` belt is `x[+-144.5] z[+-64.5]`**, against `x[+-156.5] z[+-76.5]`: a pad at the new bound draws its disc with **12 studs of belt visible** on that side.

**The line now proves it instead of asserting it.** `positions=` carries a per-pad `edge=` (that pad's own disc-to-edge clearance, measured from the placed instance's position, not from the candidate), and the summary carries `minEdge=` (the worst of them) and `margin=`. **Negative `edge=` means the paint crosses the edge**, and an `OFF-BELT` warning fires if the worst clearance is below zero -- unreachable through the bound, so if it ever prints, a pad moved after placement, the belt was resized mid-round, or `pickupDrawRadius` has diverged from `buildFootprint`.

### Decisions

1. **This is a perceptual fix, not an arithmetic one.** No pad was ever outside; the region allowed them to be flush, and flush reads as outside.
2. **`12` studs** -- over half a pad's width, so a margin is clearly visible at the camera distance rather than reading as a rounding artefact.
3. **The margin lives in the caller, not in `pickupBounds`.** The pure function takes a reach; the design decision about how much belt to leave belongs with `tuning.ts`.
4. **The region still packs `PICKUP_MAX_COUNT = 12`** -- a `14 x 6` grid of 20-stud cells remains at `288 x 129` of legal span, asserted.

**Validation:** `npm run build` exit 0; **`npm test` = 500 passed in 36 files** (one new case: the margin holds on both axes and the shrunken region still fits twelve pads); `npm run lint` 0 errors with the same 55 pre-existing `viewport.ts` warnings; touched files pass `prettier --check`; `\uXXXX` search under `src/` is zero; `flamework.build` unchanged.

**Studio-only:** that every pad now reads as clearly on the belt with belt visible around its disc, and that `minEdge=` on the spawn line is `>= 12` for every pad. **If pads still look off the belt, the remaining candidates are both visual and neither is placement:** the sprite floats `11.2` studs above the pad and can project past the belt's far edge at a shallow camera angle, and a failed asset load (`AssetFetchStatus.Failure`) would draw the ring without its image.

## 202 - The pickup ring's SurfaceGui had a finite render distance, and three docblocks that had been lying since a retune

**Reported:** the pickup ring is not visible at the camera's distance, and appears when the camera is moved closer. The sprite on the same pad was not reported missing.

### The engine fact, read rather than recalled

From the Roblox documentation for `SurfaceGui.MaxDistance`:

> This property controls how far from the camera the SurfaceGui will be displayed before it stops rendering. A value of `0` means there is no limit and it will render infinitely far away. The default value of `1000` works fine for most cases.

So **the default is finite (`1000`)** and the cut is a **pop**, not a fade -- the docs go on to recommend keeping the limit high enough that the pop happens when the UI is already small on screen. That is the reported symptom's shape.

### The change

One property, in `buildFootprint`:

```ts
surface.MaxDistance = PICKUP_RING_MAX_DISTANCE;   // 1e6
```

`1e6` rather than the documented `0`: both mean "no limit", but `0` reads to the next person as "cull at zero distance" -- one careless fix away from switching the ring off. A million studs is past any camera this place can have and needs no documentation to be understood. The constant's docblock quotes the doc above.

**`AlwaysOnTop` was left `false`.** It cannot produce a distance cut -- it decides occlusion -- and the disc sits `2.22` studs above the belt with nothing between it and a camera looking down at the pad. Turning it on would buy nothing and would cost the "painted on the floor" read by drawing the disc over every ball that touches a pad.

**Property audit, so the next reader does not have to repeat it:** `MaxDistance` is the **only** distance-dependent property on a `SurfaceGui`. `PixelsPerStud` and `SizingMode` decide resolution, `ZOffset` decides depth, `ClipsDescendants` decides cropping, `AlwaysOnTop` decides occlusion, `Brightness` and `LightInfluence` decide shading. Nothing else in `buildFootprint` can switch the ring off with range.

### The line that makes the next review cheap

```
[PickupSprite] ring surface maxDistance=1000000 alwaysOnTop=false brightness=1 pixelsPerStud=200 canvas=4000x4000 parent=Workspace....
```

Once per session, on the first ring built, **every field read back off the instance** rather than printed from the constant that set it, and two frames in because `CanvasSize` is the rasteriser's answer. The round before this one measured the ring at `19.2 px` and could not say whether that was a small disc or a culled one; `maxDistance` is the field that tells them apart.

### Three docblocks corrected, values untouched

| constant | value | the docblock claimed | now says |
|---|---|---|---|
| `RING_THICKNESS_STUDS` | `2` | "`0.05` ... a twentieth of a stud" | the real value, and that with `BELT_SURFACE_THICKNESS = 0.1` and a `0.12` lift the painted face sits **`2.22` studs** above the belt -- so it is a plate, not paint |
| `RING_LIFT_STUDS` | `0.12` | "`0.02` studs" | the real value, and that the thickness, not the lift, is what clears the floor |
| `RING_PIXELS_PER_STUD` | `200` | "`400 x 400` canvas" | **`4000 x 4000`** -- the `400` was true of the 2-stud ring the old annulus drew, and the disc is `20` studs across. A memory cost, deliberately not changed here |

### A pre-existing failure, fixed because it blocked the signal

`npm test` was **red at `HEAD`**, not from this round: the tree runs `SPIN_BASE_RAD_PER_SEC = 30` against `APPARENT_SPIN_MAX_RAD_PER_SEC = 31`, so every speed from `0.83` studs/second up clamps, and three cases in `apparent-spin.spec.ts` still encoded item 196's superseded `20 rad/s` anchor -- including `31 > 31` for monotonicity and `toBeLessThan(31)` against a rate of exactly `31`. They were un-pinned to assert the *shape* (base at `0`, base plus gain clamped above, monotone only below the derived ceiling speed) instead of the retired tuning.

### The caveat this round cannot close

The default is `1000`, and the camera back-solves to roughly **260-390 studs** from a pad using the sprite's own `drawn=20.8px` for a `10.4`-stud sprite. **So `MaxDistance` may not have been culling anything**, and if the ring still does not read, the next candidate is apparent size and contrast: a 20-stud disc is about **38 px** at that range, filled at `RING_TRANSPARENCY = 0.6`, unlit, on a dark belt. That is a *legibility* problem, and its fixes are `RING_TRANSPARENCY` and the disc's screen-space size -- both deliberately out of scope here.

**Validation:** `npm run build` exit 0; **`npm test` = 500 passed in 36 files**; `npm run lint` 0 errors with the same 55 pre-existing `viewport.ts` warnings; all three touched files pass `prettier --check`; `\uXXXX` under `src/` = 0; `flamework.build` unchanged; the controller's diff is **44 insertions, 0 deletions**, so the sprite and every other ring property are byte-identical to `HEAD`.

**Studio-only:** that the ring now draws at the game camera's distance (or that it does not, which would move the cause to legibility); and whether `maxDistance=1000000` prints as `1000000` on the new line.

## 203 - The contact shove is a push in the belt plane, not a sideways nudge

**Reported:** "Right now, shoves are exclusively side to side. Let's make it 360."

### Shape (a), and the exact line that caused it

`shoveDirection` in `src/server/lateral-shove.ts` was **already correct**:

```ts
const delta = new Vector3(to.X - from.X, 0, to.Z - from.Z);
...
return delta.Unit;
```

That is the full horizontal normal, flattened by dropping `Y` -- not a projection onto `across`. The collapse happened in `stepBallSpeeds`:

```ts
const lateralShove = across.mul(shoveImpulse.Dot(across));   // <- the along-belt part dies here
...
.add(lateralShove);
```

So the module stored a 2D vector and the writer kept one component of it. `[Powers] shove: ... dir=(...)` printed the **raw** `shoveDirection` vector all along (`dir=${formatVector(direction)}` in `maybeShove`), which is why the log could show `dir=(-0.946, 0, 0.324)` -- 95% along the belt -- while the shove felt purely sideways. The field was never lying; the writer was ignoring it.

### The change

`stepBallSpeeds`, one term added and one projection widened:

```ts
const shoveImpulse = lateralShoveFor(ball, dt);
const lateralShove = across.mul(shoveImpulse.Dot(across));
const alongShove = right.mul(shoveImpulse.Dot(right));      // NEW
ball.AssemblyLinearVelocity = velocity
    .sub(right.mul(along))
    .sub(across.mul(carriedLateral))
    .add(right.mul(-relative))
    .add(lateral)
    .add(lateralShove)
    .add(alongShove);                                        // NEW
```

`right` and `across` are orthogonal and horizontal for this belt, so the two dot products reconstruct the impulse and nothing is dropped. The along-belt shove adds to the `-relative` term, the lateral one to the sway's rate -- both axes keep one writer.

**`carriedLateral` still has to be zeroed, and still is.** The `sub(across.mul(carriedLateral))` removes the ball's *actual* lateral velocity so the model's rate replaces it; that is item 151's fix for the driven-oscillator resonance, and it is independent of where the rate came from. The shove is part of the model's rate, not carried velocity, so nothing changes about the ordering.

### The sign convention, quoted

```ts
shoveLateral(ball, direction.mul(-BALL_COLLISION_SHOVE_SPEED));
shoveLateral(other, direction.mul(BALL_COLLISION_SHOVE_SPEED));
```

`direction` points **from `ball` to `other`**, so `ball` receives `-direction` (away from `other`) and `other` receives `+direction` (away from `ball`). Repulsive, equal and opposite, already correct -- **no sign change was needed**, and that is the thing a 2D rewrite was most likely to break. It is now pinned by a spec case asserting the pair sums to zero.

### Decisions

1. **Shape (a).** The sideways-only behaviour was introduced in `stepBallSpeeds`; `shoveDirection` was already full-plane.
2. **`dir=` is the raw `shoveDirection` vector** -- `dir=${formatVector(direction)}`, where `direction = shoveDirection(ball.Position, other.Position, mine.serial)`. Never the projected value, so **no log change was needed** and the line's shape is preserved.
3. **Same sign to both bodies?** No -- see above, the pair was already `-d` / `+d`.
4. **The axis mapping:** `right` is `RightVector`, which in this scene is the **along-belt** axis (world `-Z`), and `across = right:Cross(up)` is lateral (world `+X`). A pair separated in world `Z` is head-on; separated in world `X` is side by side. Both facts are now asserted in the spec so the next reader cannot invert them.
5. **Boundedness:** `clampShove` caps the **vector** magnitude at `BALL_COLLISION_SHOVE_SPEED`, so a 2D shove has the same peak as the 1D one -- a dead-on contact is one full shove along the belt, not half on each axis. Duplicate `Touched` fires are still prevented by the lower-`serial` election plus the shared contact cooldown, and even a doubled record would be clamped rather than summed.
6. **No retune.** `BALL_COLLISION_SHOVE_SPEED` and `BALL_COLLISION_SHOVE_DECAY_SECONDS` are untouched.

### What this changes about the feel, which the next round must judge

The projection was acting as an unlabelled scale factor. A contact whose normal was 30% lateral applied 30 studs/second; that same contact now applies 100, and a rear-end contact that applied almost nothing now applies the full 100 **along the belt**, where no sway correction pulls it back. `BALL_COLLISION_SHOVE_SPEED = 100` with a `1`-second time constant is `s * T` = **100 studs** of displacement (`5 * 0.3 = 1.5` when it shipped, `10` when the docblock was last correct). Along the belt that is a third of the `333`-stud length per hit, so a contact can now push a ball into the elimination edge.

Found while rewriting: `BALL_COLLISION_SHOVE_SPEED`'s docblock still said "at `10` ... **10 studs** ... about 2.8 studs per second at the peak, which is below `BELT_SPEED`". It describes the value from before a retune; at `100` the peak is 100 studs/second, ten times `BELT_SPEED`. Corrected in place, value left alone.

### Four docblocks rewritten

`lateral-shove.ts`'s module block and `shoveDirection`, `maybeShove`'s "why the direction is the contact normal" (which argued the old behaviour as deliberate -- the first half of its reasoning, that a real separation from a rear-end hit is *along* the belt, is exactly why the old conclusion was wrong), and `BALL_COLLISION_SHOVE_SPEED`.

**Validation:** `npm run build` exit 0; **`npm test` = 505 passed in 36 files** (five new cases: head-on dominance, side-by-side dominance, diagonal has both, equal-and-opposite pair, and no halving across axes); `npm run lint` 0 errors with the same 55 pre-existing `viewport.ts` warnings; all five touched files pass `prettier --check`; `\uXXXX` under `src/` = 0; `flamework.build` unchanged.

**Studio-only:** whether the 360 push reads as a bump or as one ball punting the other; whether `BALL_COLLISION_SHOVE_SPEED = 100` is now too strong along the belt; and whether the sway's `SWAY_TRACK_SECONDS = 1.5` correction fights a lateral shove visibly while leaving the along-belt one permanent (it must -- there is no lane to return to on that axis).
